schedule.desc: Come help chalk out the fastest route between the SEC and the Crowne Plaza. Meet outside at ground level between the venues.
schedule.title: Chalking Session - Wednesday

schedule.desc: As the world enjoys Part 2 of Denis Villeneuve's cinematic vision of Frank Herbert's masterpiece, solo performance artist Dan Collins has been wondering - what if we distilled Dune down to its component parts? What if we added some whimsical and comedic songs? What if the whole story could be told in one hour, by one man, with one guitar? Behold: Dune! The Musical! Fresh off the back of a critically-acclaimed run at Edinburgh Festival in 2023, Dan's show is the perfect way to experience this SF classic and is the opening event of the convention!.
schedule.title: Dune! The Musical

schedule.desc: Use your best supervillian surgery skills to reassemble soft toys into new monstrosities... or maybe you'd rather just add some eyes to a sock? Whatever your sewing or glueing level, come and create creatures to haunt our nightmares! Recommended for ages 6-15.
schedule.title: Frankenstuffies Workshop
Online Writers' Communities and Critique Groups

schedule.desc: Karl Popper was a philosopher who was instrumental in the development of the modern scientific method. Carl Sagan was a scientist who championed the scientific method and the art of sceptical scrutiny to help us understand the universe and our place in it. Humans (and other animals) are prone to unconscious biases, which have significant evolutionary benefits, but also cause a multitude of problems. How can we learn from these two great polymaths of the 20th century to challenge our biased brains to explore reality and make better decisions?
schedule.title: Is There a Dragon in Your Garage?

schedule.desc: What is Costume Con? Where is it? What happens there? And why should you consider attending?
schedule.title: An Overview of Costume Con

schedule.desc: Trying to find the perfect system for your new campaign idea? What kind of mechanics will produce the atmosphere you want? This panel will discuss and showcase indie TTRPG systems in SFF, discussing the pros and cons of their many approaches to narrative and to game mechanics (or, in some cases, lack thereof).
schedule.title: TTRPGs: Introduction to Indies

schedule.desc: Learn about the ten general principles that underlie all of biology's theories, what they imply about living systems, and their implications for SF. In the process, you will learn about what makes a theory and biology's core research questions. By the end of the hour, you will understand the "big picture" of what is biology.
schedule.title: All of Biology in 60 Minutes or Less

schedule.desc:
From page to stage, a crash-course in theatrical sci-fi, songwriting and clown. In this workshop, Dune! The Musical's own Dan Collins takes us through the steps involved in taking a show from script to production. Fun Fact: theatre pioneer Joan Littlewood, who spent much of their career developing theatre in Scotland, coined the term workshop for theatrical production to remind performers, directors and producers that theatre is for every one.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops/.
schedule.title: A Science Fiction! Theatre Workshop! From Page to Stage!

schedule.desc: Part of our Introduction To series, which offers a general overview of popular SFF tropes, areas or authors. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to Scottish SFF
Timekeeping on Mars

schedule.desc: The staff of this year's Business Meeting will discuss what is on the agenda for this year's meeting and answer questions about how it all works.
schedule.title: About the Business Meeting

schedule.desc:
1. Podcast Pedagogy: Navigating Unique Themes in Asynchronous Course Design - Jason Aukerman
2. A University Course Entitled "Science Fiction as Laboratory for Societal Questions" - Jack Glassman
schedule.title: Pedagogical Futures

schedule.desc: Fantasy is not all fun and wish-fulfilment but is also a genre of desire and longing that often forces protagonists to confront their inner demons. Are such stories endemic to children's and YA literature, or are they artificially injected in order to transmit adult preoccupations? Has fantasy for children and young adults become darker over time? And if so, what does it mean? Our panellists discuss these questions and more as they explore the darker side of modern stories.
schedule.title: Dealing With Your Dark Side

schedule.desc: Do digital tools change the analogue gaming experience? What are the pitfalls and joys of online play? And what is everyone supposed to do with their dice hoards, and those minis they've been painting?! This panel takes a closer look at the gaming tabletop, and the experience playing online and in-person.
schedule.title: The Gaming Tabletop: Digital and Analogue

schedule.desc: This talk will look at depictions of birth and pregnancy in science fiction from the perspective of a practising obstetrician and a gaze into the future of human reproduction via the exciting developments in pregnancy care today.
schedule.title: The Future of Birth: Obstetrics and Science Fiction

schedule.desc: With credits on films ranging from AI:Artificial Intelligence and The Golden Compass to The Corpse Bride, Guest of Honour Chris Baker shares his experiences of working as a concept designer.
schedule.title: Chris Baker (Fangorn): Concept Design for Film and Television

schedule.desc: We've all wanted to take a bite out of a gorgeous piece of animated food: the hearty and comforting bacon and eggs of Howl's Moving Castle, the explosively flavorful wagyu of Food Wars, or even the dubious treasure bug sorbet of Dungeon Meshi. Come find out with us how anime can create connections between food, the audience, and cooking - but bring your own snacks!
schedule.title: Let Them Cook - Food in Anime

schedule.desc: The Lodestar award for Young Adult Literature became part of the Worldcon awards only in 2018, after many years of discussion and debate. Does Worldcon need an equivalent award for Children's Literature, too? What would it offer beyond the existing established awards? Our panellists discuss the whys, the why nots and the challenges.
schedule.title: What Do We Need from a New Children's Literature Award?

schedule.desc: A meetup for users of the Zombies, Run! app to connect, share experiences, and discuss their adventures in virtual zombie-infested worlds, while motivating each other to stay active and have fun.
schedule.title: Zombies, Run! app users meetup

schedule.desc: Join a panel of authors to discuss their relationship with music. What music might they listen to when writing and why? Does music serve as an inspiration for their story content? This panel is part of an exciting academic research project where audience questions can also be part of the study.
schedule.title: Soundtracks of Space and Time: The Use of Music in Writing Science Fiction and Fantasy

schedule.desc: Macbeth is known as The Scottish Play. It is considered a major part of Western theatrical canon. The panel discusses everything from memorable performances of the play to the influence of Macbeth on the sci-fi genre. We'll also touch on the superstitions and stories surrounding this famous work.
schedule.title: Shakespeare, the Scottish Play and Science Fiction

schedule.desc: From farming sims, to solo TTRPGs, to cleaning up your Animal Crossing island after a long break... 'cosy gaming' is on the rise! What are your favourite worlds to escape and relax back into? This panel will discuss our favourite cosy games, and why gaming can be such a comfort.
schedule.title: Cosy Gaming

schedule.desc: Science fiction and fantasy inspired theatre can be found everywhere from the local pub to the Royal Albert Hall. Our panel takes a look at the history of fannish things on stage and how they come to be, from fan works such as The Enchanted Duplicator to Off-West End shows such as Fan Boy, The Dark Sublime and Be More Chill to Broadway's disastrous Via Galactica.
schedule.title: Sci-Fi  on the Stage and at The Fringe

schedule.desc: Work together to create a brand new fairytale in this fast-paced group storytelling session. Whether it turns out spooky, romantic, tragic, or very silly is up to you. Recommended age 7-12.
schedule.title: Fairytale Mad Libs

schedule.desc: In 1987 the BBC TV show Star Cops gave us the international Space Police Force. What would policing orbital colonies, asteroid settlements, moon settlements and spacecraft moving around the solar system look like in the next 30 years? What would it be for? Can we avoid replicating the issues found in policing on Earth?
schedule.title: Policing the High Frontier

schedule.desc: 2024 marks 200 years since the birth of William Thomson (aka Lord Kelvin), Glasgow University Professor for over 50 years and one of the most influential scientists of 19th century. Yet Lord Kelvin pre-dated the twin revolutions in relativity and quantum physics of the early 1900s that underpin much of our modern technology. So, what would Lord Kelvin make of our 21st century world? Would it look as much like science fiction to him as the world of Star Trek (and the USS Kelvin!) does today?
schedule.title: We Need to Talk About Kelvin

schedule.desc: Have you ever wondered how a book gets professionally edited? The editors on the panel will talk you through the editing process, share tips on how to edit and what to look out for before submitting, and answer all your questions.
schedule.title: Learning the Editing Process

schedule.desc: Doing research in the right amount can offer experiences and adventures that make up stories in and of themselves. For this presentation, I turned to well-known authors and asked them about the funniest, weirdest, and most wonderful things they discovered while doing research for their books. (Among other authors: Holly Black, Cassandra Claire, Seanan Macguire, Sebastien de Castell, Daryl Gregory)
schedule.title: Becoming a Literary Indiana Jones: Exactly The Right Amount of Research

schedule.desc:
The Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of Japan and the Science Fiction Fan Groups Association of Japan present the Seiun Award recipients for 2024 and offer the trophy for the best translated works. They will also present the Japanese SF Grand Prize recipients for 2024.

The panel will also discuss the current status of Japanese science fiction, authors, prizes (SF Grand Prize, Seiun prize), and current  and future developments.
schedule.title: The Seiun Awards and the Current Status of Japanese SF

schedule.desc: The deepest reaches of space are haunted by aliens so powerful they are godlike. The ocean's floor holds ancient civilisations that predate humanity, overseen by beings from beyond time itself. And a colour can drive anyone who sees it mad in an instant. Cosmic horror is everywhere and utterly unknown. Our panellists discuss its attraction and ongoing power.
schedule.title: The Horror Out Of Space

schedule.desc:
What kinds of worlds can be built and stories be told when magic has rules that can be inferred from strict experimentation vs. when magic is a matter of beauty and taste? Is there overlap? The principles of perspective in representational art derive from mathematics, the principles of colour theory derive from optics, and the principles of colour creation derive from chemistry. Yet in our world there is often a hard divide between what is considered art and science. What could the division between art and science, or challenges to that division, mean for fictional magical systems?

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Magic as Art vs Magic as Science (Online)

schedule.desc: Meetup for Romance Fantasy Manhwa Fans
schedule.title: Romance Fantasy Manhwa Fans meetup

schedule.desc: How much science is just enough in sci-fi for children and young adults? Our panel discusses the challenges of writing science and technology into stories without oversimplifying or being condescending or overly didatic. How can you include elements of real-life scientific research and technological developments in a way that interests, intrigues and excites your readers?
schedule.title: Writing Science into Your Sci-Fi for Young Readers

schedule.desc: From Star Wars' "The Imperial March" to 2001: A Space Odyssey, certain SFF scores have crossed the boundary out of genre to become iconic pieces of music in their own right. What makes a score 'iconic' in this way, and what are some current examples of this?
schedule.title: Iconic SFF Musical Scores

schedule.desc: Join your fellow fibre arts fans for a lively meetup! This is designated as more show and tell than a crafting-only session, so be prepared for chatting while you craft. (See also the Quiet Crochet, Knitting, and Fibre Arts Meetup.)
schedule.title: Crochet, Knitting, Sewing, and Fibre Arts Lively Meetup

schedule.desc: Speculative fiction imagines many other worlds and other forms of government but less frequently depicts how we get from one state to another. With revolutions forming the centre of fiction as diverse as Ken MacLeod's Fall Revolution sequence, China Mieville's Iron Council, Ursula K. Le Guin's The Day Before The Revolution, or Nnedi Okorafor's The Shadow Speaker, this panel will discuss the different ways speculative fiction has tackled revolution, and revolutions aftermath, and its favourite examples of fantastical revolutions.
schedule.title: Revolutions in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Make light-up cards and more! Learn to craft with LEDs and copper tape. (This workshop is running twice to accomodate more participants.) Recommended for ages 6-15.
schedule.title: Paper Circuit Workshop 1

schedule.desc: We have selected some fandom veterans, as well as recent Worldcon attendees, to share their stories of how they prepared for and how they experienced their first Worldcon. We hope you will get inspired for your first time at Worldcon.
schedule.title: My First Time at Worldcon

schedule.desc: Join us at this meetup for writers and fans of fan fiction, where enthusiasts can share stories, discuss beloved fandoms, and connect with fellow fans. Come be a part of this vibrant community, where inspiration flows freely, creativity is sparked, and fan-created content is celebrated with open arms. We can't wait to meet you and dive into the world of fanfiction together!
schedule.title: Fanfic Writers and Fans Meetup

schedule.desc: Fandom is a family, and speculative fiction is full of found families, from quest groups to spaceship crews. We will talk about the attraction of found families, the pitfalls of writing them, and the best examples of found families in fiction... as well as those we'd love to be adopted into.
schedule.title: Blood is Thicker than Water: Found Family in SFF

schedule.desc: We often hope that there is a Great Technological Fix to our problems. However, what happens when engineering or science is applied without fully considering the effects on the people who are having the problems? The panel discusses examples from science fiction and the real world and what solutions are proposed for today's problems. What are the consequences to people if they succeed? Or fail? Or both?
schedule.title: Engineering Solutions to People Problems

schedule.desc: In addition to being a devastating disease and a fascinating area of biological study, cancer is an incredibly potent idea, woven through our culture and art. In this talk we will explore some of the most important features of cancer as a biological and clinical phenomenon, and link these facts to the cultural importance of the disease, with particular reference to ideas in science fiction. We will touch on molecular biology, clinical medicine, technology, politics, and the history of ideas.
schedule.title: Cells gone rogue: cancer as an idea in the 21st century

schedule.desc: Recent years have seen Chinese science fiction and fantasy films and TV shows released internationally to great success, notably The Wandering Earth and Three-Body Problem. What other SFF shows and films popular in China deserve wider recognition in the rest of the world?
schedule.title: Chinese SFF Film and Television

schedule.desc: There is a question haunting Fantasy Scholarship, the sound of which is enough to make a room of fantasists groan: Is Fantasy (in all its transmedial incarnations) even worthy of academic study? This roundtable considers this question to be simplistic and constrictive and its assumption of a hierarchy between scholarship and fandom to be misguided, bordering on elitist. Instead, we propose a roundtable that focuses on what makes Fantasy Academia worthy of attention from fandom and creative practitioners alike.
schedule.title: Futures of Fantasy Scholarship

schedule.desc: Every reader deserves to see themselves reflected in stories; that also holds true for disabled readers, even if disabled main characters are still few and far between. What does disability look like in genre Middle Grade and YA literature today, and how has representation changed over the last few years? Does target age matter? Which stories are must-reads, and whose stories remain untold or invisible? How can we best make sure they are written and heard?
schedule.title: Disability Representation in Middle Grade and YA Fiction

schedule.desc: The panel discusses the science behind terraforming - with particular emphasis on Mars and Venus - and compares it with fictional examples e.g. Kim Stanley Robinson’s Red/Green/Blue Mars trilogy. Do we have the technology to carry out such large-scale planetary engineering projects successfully? Even if we do, should we, especially if the world has potential to develop life of its own?
schedule.title: The Science, Fiction, and Ethics of Terraforming

schedule.desc:
"Do you think we're living inside a computer simulation, Mum?" My kids love delaying bedtime by asking me tricky questions, and this particular existential crisis left me utterly lost for words. To try and find an answer, I've been throwing all the physics I know at the problem. As the Astronomer Royal for Scotland, I'm used to creating giant maps of the universe that transport us 10 billion years back in time. But what if all the ancient light that I've spent my entire career collecting is just a series of computer impulses in an elaborate simulation of my own reality? I know how to simulate an entire Universe of galaxies: have I been naive to think a future scientist couldn't create a complete virtual world much closer home?

For Glasgow WorldCon, I'm going to share the journey I've taken to understand how one day we might simulate our own lives. We'll look at the laws of physics that govern the universe and delve into the inner workings of your computer and artificial intelligence. I'll ask why philosophers feel so challenged by the concept of living in a predetermined virtual world when it's clear that interactions on the smallest and largest scales in our universe can be mathematically defined. By exploring the intersections of physics, astronomy, and philosophy, I'll be inviting you to reconsider what is 'real'.
schedule.title: The Universe: Reality or Simulation?

schedule.desc: A meetup for fans of World of Warcraft to gather, discuss game updates, share strategies, and connect with fellow adventurers in the immersive world of Azeroth.
schedule.title: World of Warcraft fans meetup

schedule.desc: How do video game mechanics affect a game's narrative? Hear from industry professionals as they unpack their best practices for games writing. One for those looking to dive into the intricacies of choosing your own adventures, branched narratives and narrative tools.
schedule.title: Writing for Video Games

schedule.desc: The final WSFS Mark Protection Committee meeting for the 2023/2024 year. This might be a good meeting to go to if you have questions for the MPC. This meeting is open to Glasgow Worldcon attendees, but only MPC members have the right to vote and introduce or debate business.
schedule.title: Mark Protection Committee Meeting

schedule.desc:
Learn calligraphic scripts, practice and then write out a quote or short poem to take home.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Medieval Calligraphy Workshop

schedule.desc: LGBTQ+ books, especially in the traditional publishing world, have to negotiate many barriers to reach publication or achieve commercial “success”. This panel will discuss those challenges and possibly offer advice to help navigate them.
schedule.title: Queerness in Publishing: Breaking through Barriers
The Lost Wonders of Science Fiction

schedule.desc: A light-hearted look at some technologies and projects from aerospace and defence featuring things outwardly-normal engineers thought were a good idea at the time, until a look at the fine print revealed details that should perhaps have raised a degree of operator concern. The take-home message? Just because you can do a thing doesn't mean that you should!
schedule.title: Inadvisable Rocket Science

schedule.desc:
An interactive session in which we create an entire world, people it (or 'thing' it), and look at why everything needs to be 'just right' to make it work as a cohesive whole. We will be pulling together all the elements of worldbuilding and looking at how these affect and interact with each other - and why one wrong thread can make the whole thing fall apart.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Build a World From Scratch

schedule.desc:
Welcome to Glasgow 2024, A Worldcon for our Futures.

Join our Chair, Professor Esther MacCallum-Stewart, in welcoming our guests and attendees to Worldcon. Hear from Glasgow's Lord Provost who will share a warm welcome with our members. This is also your chance to get a first look at this year's Hugo Award and hear from the designer Iain J. Clark about how this beautiful award was constructed. We will present a series of fannish awards including the First Fandom Awards for the Hall of Fame, Posthumous Hall of Fame, Big Heart and Sam Moskowitz Archive, as well as the Special Award given out by each Worldcon. Learn about many of the things to do over your five days at Glasgow 2024 and things you won't want to miss. Finally, join us in a loving farewell to the community members we have lost over the last year as we introduce our new Memorial Garden.
schedule.title: Opening Ceremony

schedule.desc: Despite what some people think, the Y2K bug was a real problem that took a large amount of work to fix, but it's not the only large-scale computer problem that we have faced or will face. Mere weeks before the convention, a CrowdStrike update brought transport and health networks to a grinding halt. This panel will talk about what might happen, what might not happen, and how we could think differently about preparing.
schedule.title: Big Bytey Bugs! When Is the Next Computer Apocalypse Due?
Table Talk: Ruth Frances Long / Jessica Thorne

schedule.desc:
Magnetism is a force of nature that humans are beginning to harness. Much new technology is dependent on rare earth minerals for which China is the main producer, making their continued availability a matter of geopolitics. Skimming over deep science and history to look at current technologies, this talk will gaze into a future of applications, supply chains, and consequences.

WARNING: This presentation will feature items that people can handle (carefully!), but be aware that powerful magnetic fields can affect pacemakers, credit cards, computers, USB sticks etc.
schedule.title: Magnetism – the Force of the Future

schedule.desc: Is it possible to thrive, or only survive, in today's economic landscape? How has science fiction tackled this problem?
schedule.title: Surviving Late-Stage Capitalism as a Creative

schedule.desc: What does a world need for people (or aliens) to be able to live there? In this workshop with scientist and author Julie Novakova, you will learn about some of the ways life might arise and be supported before being challenged to create and draw your own worlds. Recommended age 10-16.
schedule.title: Constructing a Habitable World

schedule.desc:
1. The Posthuman Proletariat: Exploitation and Alienation in Humans - Dylan Phelan
2. From Kalasatama to the Suicide Tower: Futures of the Democratic Welfare State in Contemporary Finnish SF - Esko Suoranta
3. The Cost of Abolition in Yoko Ogawa's The Memory Police - Hannah Mimiec
schedule.title: Proletariat Futures

schedule.desc: Edwin sings nerdy folk songs about such diverse topics as computing, space travel, pie shops, zombies, ghosts and punctuation. With a ukulele or two.
schedule.title: Filk Concert: Edwin Brady

schedule.desc:
“Strong female character” has too often been a euphemism for a sword-wielding amazon battling those who wronged her. Fun and glorious though those women are, this panel will talk about the women who lead through intelligence, charisma, patience, or other skills.

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Strong Female Leads Who Don't Kick Ass (Online Version)

schedule.desc: Our group of critics and reviewers will talk about our Hugo nominees for Best Novella, Novelette and Short Story before the winners are announced, what they say about the state of the genre, and discuss the spread!
schedule.title: Hugo Shortlist Discussion: Best Novella, Novelette and Short Story

schedule.desc: Past technological breakthroughs have often led to major changes in industry, accompanied by job losses in particular economic sectors. AI could have the biggest impact of all. The panel discusses what AI might mean for industry and the labour market. Will some types of occupation always need the human touch, e.g. a psychotherapist or carpenter? Or are we all at risk of being replaced by machines? The panel will discuss the ways in which this new space can be regulated and the changes that will need to occur in society, from Universal Basic Income to a greater emphasis on creativity.
schedule.title: AI and Work - Do Androids Dream of Taking Your Job?

schedule.desc: Epic fantasy stories usually encompass multiple volumes and thousands upon thousands of pages. What is the appeal of the epic novel? Is it the multi-act storylines, the interwoven structure, the intricate details, the big cast of characters? Or the fact that you can use them as a weapon? Or all of the above? Come along to find out just what makes an epic novel deeply satisfying for readers and writers alike.
schedule.title: Epic Appeal

schedule.desc: Science fiction contains many examples of plagues, epidemics, and their impact on human civilisation. The panel discusses the experience of living through a global pandemic compared with fictional examples. It considers which were closer to reality (the 2011 movie Contagion is often cited) and which were substantially off target. How will the experience affect our genre in the future?
schedule.title: Going Viral - Pandemics in Fact and Fiction

schedule.desc: The past decade has seen a rush of comic book adaptations hitting both the big and small screen - not just familiar properties and characters such as Batman, but also old favourites like The Sandman and newer comics such as Sweet Tooth and Invincible. What elements make an adaptation successful, and what should stay on the page?
schedule.title: Adapting Comics for the Screen

schedule.desc: Generation starships are both interesting science and a great story concept. The Initiative for Interstellar Studies brings you three related programme items exploring the worldship in fact and fiction. This first session will feature a short presentation laying out the definition of the worldship concept and outlining its history in science (Goddard, Tsiolkovsky, Bernal) as well as in science fiction (Heinlein, Aldiss, MacLeod et al.).
schedule.title: Worldships 1: Introduction

schedule.desc: At the COP28 climate summit, most countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. However, it remains unlikely that global warming can be limited to less than 1.5°C. The panel discusses how we should respond to the climate crisis. Are small changes such as biofuel-powered aircraft and electric cars sufficient, or do we need a wholescale rethink of how society operates? What insight does climate fiction (cli-fi) offer?
schedule.title: Sustainability 1: Adapting to a Changing World

schedule.desc: Who makes the royal robes, who weaves the flags of the republic, and what are those snazzy space suits made of? Fabric and clothing are an integral part of the world, and this is no less true in SFF: so who does it best? What worlds best use fabric and crafts in their creation, and which writers give us clothes we want to wear?
schedule.title: Cut From Whole Cloth

schedule.desc: Come along after the Opening Ceremony to Hall 4 where we will raise a glass to the start of the convention, sponsored with our thanks by the City of Glasgow, a major sponsor and supporter of the convention!
schedule.title: Civic Reception
Fight the Power: Systems as Villains in SFF

schedule.desc: You're on the wrong side of the river! It's been 25 years since Rick and Evelyn stole collective hearts in a race across the desert. Did the romantic swashbuckler genre peak with The Mummy? How long do scarab beetles live? Is the film even historically accurate? Panellists will discuss all these aspects of the film and its influences on genre culture.
schedule.title: 25th Anniversary of The Mummy

schedule.desc:
A chance to meet and welcome Trans Atlantic Fan Fund (TAFF) delegate Sarah Gulde and Get-Up-And-Over (GUFF) delegate Kat Clay. Fan funds exist to bring fans together and strengthen connections across SF fandom worldwide. The event is a chance to share stories from fan fund trips past and present as recounted by delegates, hosts, and fans they met along the way; catch up with old friends and make new ones.

The reception takes place in the fan lounge area of Hall 4.
schedule.title: Fan Funds Reception

schedule.desc: Many podcasts rely on interviews with creators, fans, and other interesting people. What makes a great podcast interview, and how do you learn the skills you need to put your guest at ease and make an entertaining podcast? And how should you approach being a podcast guest?
schedule.title: The Art of the Interview

schedule.desc: Food and culture are inextricably linked, and no genre understands that more than fantasy. Far from the stereotype of hearty broths for every meal, writers have given us fantastic feasts and meagre meals of every flavour you can imagine. But what are our panellists' favourite morsels to read about eating? What gets their mouths watering, and where can you read it? How has food in fantasy changed over time?
schedule.title: Fantastic Foods: What's On The Menu?

schedule.desc: The old answer to "Are there lines we shouldn't cross?" is "Don't like, don't read", combined with liberal use of the back button. But does that still hold true? What is allowed in fanfic, and are there any rules of engagement? When is fanbinding good and when can it lead to trouble? How about when fanfic intersects with real world privilege and harassment? What are the consequences if we cross any of those lines, with the author, publishing house, or fellow readers?
schedule.title: What Lines Should We Cross When Writing Fanfic?

schedule.desc: These are the stories that you need to watch, and here's why you need to watch them. Join us for an in-depth conversation about what to seek out and what to avoid.
schedule.title: The Best SFFH Film and TV of 2023/2024

schedule.desc: Part of our Introduction To series, which offers a general overview of popular SFF tropes, areas or authors. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to Dark Academia

schedule.desc:
Sometimes the system (or society) is the bad guy. This panel will look at stories that engage with problematic systems and how they cause evil, as well as what heroes can do to fight them.

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Fight the Power: Systems as Villains in SFF (Online)

schedule.desc:
The famous photographer Chase Jarvis once said, "The best camera is the one that's with you". Given the fact that our smartphones are just about always with us, they offer the most convenience for capturing special moments from Worldcon and other events. In this workshop, you will get to know the key features of your smartphone camera and build confidence in capturing both important memories and artistic shots.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops/.
schedule.title: Getting the Best Out of your Smartphone Camera

schedule.desc: More people speak Klingon than Esperanto! There are people writing Elvish poetry. HBO developed Dothraki (a mixture of Arabic and Spanish) for Game of Thrones, and Suzette Haden Elgin invented Laadan to lead a revolution. So how do you go about creating one or more languages for your own world? How do you embed an ideology in your language? Our expert panel takes you through the basics and the interesting twists.
schedule.title: Creating a Language for Your World

schedule.desc: To seek out new life and new civilisations, one must be properly dressed. Starfleet issues a uniform to its crew. What can we tell about characters, crews, stories, and media by the uniforms we see? What biases do we have, and what assumptions do we make when we see a uniform in sci-fi?
schedule.title: What's In a Uniform? Colonial Appearances in Star Trek & other SF

schedule.desc: Join eight authors as they launch their new books! In this special group launch, you'll get to hear from each author as they introduce their new title before you'll have the opportunity to meet and chat with them, get books signed, etc. It'll be a geat way to discover new novels, novellas, and short fiction by a variety of science fiction, fantasy, and horror authors! Featuring S.B. Divya (Loka, book 2 of the Alloy Era series; SF), Gregory A. Wilson (Heretic, the final book of the Gray Assassin Trilogy; Fantasy), Sam Wilson (The First Murder On Mars; SF), Jane Flett (Freakslaw; queer literary Horror), J.E. Hannaford (Unfamiliared; Cozy Fantasy novella), Jim Alexander (story collection Rerun to Eden; SF), Jan Kotouc (Frontiers of the Imperium, Central Imperium Book 1; SF), and Dan Moren (The Armageddon Protocol, the final book of the Galactic Cold War series; SF).
schedule.title: Group Book Launch - Thursday

schedule.desc: A meetup for people with ADHD to connect, share experiences, offer support, and exchange strategies for managing challenges and thriving with ADHD in daily life.
schedule.title: Meetup for People with ADHD

schedule.desc: Improv Storytelling Comedy Gameshow, loosely based on (but not approved by) the classic game The Extraordinary Adventures of Baron Munchausen. Join our panellists as the host encourages them to tell the most elaborate lies possible. Laugh as the other panellists attempt to stop them. Classic British comedy style panel show fun.
schedule.title: Outrageous Liars: The Gameshow

schedule.desc: How are diseases and injuries classified in the real world, and how could our current system of classification be adapted to handle the stuff of sf and fantasy? This presentation will introduce the ICD-10 system, also known as the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems.
schedule.title: What Ails Frodo? And How Should It Be Classified?

schedule.desc: Dark academia, horror, mystery... games can be a wonderful escape and also offer a unique medium to explore difficult and dark topics, as long as they're addressed with care. What is the appeal of horror in games? Which videogames and analogue game systems facilitate these stories well, and how can you reduce potential risk at a table?
schedule.title: Beyond the Veil: Approaching Dark Topics in Games

schedule.desc: Water nymphs, Strigas, Leshy, Koschei the Deathless—these, and many more, are fantastic creatures that populate Polish and Slavic folklore and tales. But which of them have been used in the works of foreign authors and creators, and how often do people draw from Slavic mythology? And why?
schedule.title: Slavic Mythology in Polish and Foreign SFF

schedule.desc:
1. Future Without Tense: Time in the Translation of Chinese SF - Eero Suoranta
2. Conjuring Historical Figure Narration and Alternative History Imagination in the Japanese ACG Series Fate - Gao Weiming
3. Dictatorship and/as Dystopia: Clashing Timelines in Brazilian (Science) Fiction - Jade Arbo
schedule.title: Alternate Timelines

schedule.desc: A meetup for science fiction and fantasy enthusiasts in Edinburgh to come together, discuss favorite books, movies, and TV shows, and connect with like-minded fans.
schedule.title: Edinburgh SFF group meetup

schedule.desc: Anime openings, endings, and soundtracks have always been as crucial to an anime's success as its plot, characters, and animation style. What are your favourite anime soundscapes? What makes an opening a shounen opening? And what can shows like K-ON, Carole and Tuesday and Bocchi The Rock! tell us about the importance of music to storytelling?
schedule.title: Music in Anime

schedule.desc: Panellists will pick their favourite 90s sci-fi or fantasy show and spar with facts to determine which will win the coveted title of "Number One 90s SFF Show!"
schedule.title: 90s Sci Fi Shows Fight!

schedule.desc:
Join Cat Hellisen for this interactive workshop on how to use all your senses to enrich your writing.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops/.
schedule.title: Using All Senses to Deepen and Enrich Your Writing

schedule.desc: Filk and Musical theatre combine to make Fannish musicals! Back in 2005, Glasgow Worldcon Interaction hosted the Hugo nominated "Lucas Back in Anger". This year we have Dune! The Musical! But why is this so uncommon? What has led to the seeming decline in popularity of this form of transformative work? What kind of dialogue did they typically engage in with our culture? Do the Starkid musicals count as fanworks? Why have none of them been nominated for a Hugo? Given the amount of drama that surrounds Worldcon, why not have a Worldcon musical, and what would that look like?
schedule.title: Worldcon! The Musical! - Transformative Musicals

schedule.desc: How are SFF TV shows and films addressing climate change? Is humanity doomed, or is there hope? The panel discusses representations of climate change on screen.
schedule.title: Climate Change and the End of the World

people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

schedule.desc: Worldbuilding and gaming are intertwined, sharing an influential and co-dependent legacy. This panel will explore worldbuilding in video games, TTRPGS, board games and more, and will look at games about worldbuilding, challenging assumptions and offering new approaches. They may even tackle the question, map or no map?
schedule.title: Worldbuilding in Gaming

schedule.desc: Many children's books fade into obscurity, some are popular for a short time, and some become classics that are still read decades later. But what about the children's books that no one else seems to remember? Our panel discusses all the reasons why children's books are remembered and why they might be forgotten.
schedule.title: What Makes Childhood Books Memorable?

schedule.desc: Horror podcasts want to bring the audience on a scary journey, but how do podcasters make sure their audiences have a safe and satisfying experience? As listeners, what do we expect to be warned about, and how should horror podcasters craft their warnings?
schedule.title: Content Warnings and Horror Casts

schedule.desc: Connect with fellow adventurers and fans of Baldur's Gate to share tales of epic quests, discuss favorite characters and memorable moments, and revel in the rich lore of this beloved video game series set in the iconic Forgotten Realms universe. Join us for camaraderie and nostalgia as we celebrate the legacy of Baldur's Gate!
schedule.title: Fans of Baldur's Gate Meetup

schedule.desc: Stars have their own life cycle, much like living things do. The difference is that stars' cycles take millions and often billions of years. This presentation will describe this cycle, from the beginning that all stars share to their diverse possible ends, as visualised by the latest results from the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes. Come join us on this astronomical journey!
schedule.title: The Life Cycle of Stars

schedule.desc: What does it take to develop and publish a game? Join different designers as they share their experiences in creating games, from having an idea to publishing the final product, with choose-your-own-adventure books, interactive fiction, TTRPGs, board games and more.
schedule.title: Introduction to Game Publishing

schedule.desc: Female rage has featured heavily in horror. How has SFF treated the subject? Are women allowed to have strong emotions in science fiction? Our panellists will examine depictions of female rage in SFF films and television shows.
schedule.title: Female Rage in SFF

schedule.desc: Join this moderated group discussion as we circle up and tell stories about the weirdest materials we ever made a costume out of. Those who want to share can put their name in a hat. Each person chosen at random will have 5 minutes to share their project from concept to completion and 5 minutes for participants to ask questions. It's about talking fast and impressing us with your outlandish successes and epic costuming fails!
schedule.title: Non-Traditional Costume Materials Show and/or Tell

schedule.desc: Join fellow enthusiasts in celebrating all things anime, manga, and Japanese pop culture at the Otaku Meetup. Immerse yourself in vibrant discussions, cosplay showcases, and shared appreciation for the diverse and dynamic world of otaku.
schedule.title: Otaku Meetup

schedule.desc: Fungi exist in every climate on Earth, from the Arctic to the Equator, and in our fiction, too. From the gray caps of Ambergris to the fungus-clouded atmosphere of Mexican Gothic, they can bring a strangeness to a story or be its macguffin, as in Star Trek: Discovery. The panellists will discuss their favourite fictional fungi and what it is that is so fascinating about the kingdom.
schedule.title: Fungi in Speculative Fiction

schedule.desc: Jim Henson has created or contributed to some of the most iconic science fiction and fantasy works of all time. He has shown us the way through the Labyrinth to Fraggle Rock and up into space and other Farscapes and even galaxies far, far away. Join the panel as they discuss Jim Henson, his creations, and their enduring impact on the genres we love.
schedule.title: The Fantastical Worlds of Jim Henson

schedule.desc: A panel of different scientists critique and debunk the 'science' of a number of selected movies.
schedule.title: More Fiction than Science

schedule.desc: Did you enjoy the Glasgow 2024's Gaelic Word Of The Day on social media? Wondering what the difference between Scots and Scottish Gaelic is? Have you had people tell you Scots isn't a language or that Gaelic "isn't spoken here"? Confused? Come along, and find out how many languages Scotland has and how they co-exist in the modern day.
schedule.title: Languages of Scotland

schedule.desc: Science fiction and fantasy have long been seen as the literature of ideas and boundary-pushing. In an age when we are seeing increasing legal challenges to both new and classic fiction that pushes social norms, especially around race and queerness, what is the role of SFF in challenging that? Can SFF continue to push boundaries set by the law, and if so, how?
schedule.title: Book Bans and Moral Fascism

schedule.desc:
This is the world premiere of a new science fiction opera, Morrow’s Isle.

The libretto has been written by Guest of Honour Ken MacLeod, inspired by The Island of Dr Moreau as imagined by The Men Who Stare at Goats (book and film). The music is composed by Gary Lloyd and will be accompanied by Company Carpi’s dancing. You can hear more from the creators here.

Gary Lloyd & Bettina Carpi told us: “We make hybrid dance theatre, and opera, always featuring strong societal topics, and with texts based on the work of, or written originally by, outstanding writers, poets and novelists. We always perform with live music, we always work with emerging young artists and involve community groups, and we're always trying to reach audiences that may not be familiar with the kinds of work we make and the work of the many artists with whom we collaborate.”
schedule.title: Morrow's Isle - Opera

schedule.desc: Podcasts started as a niche hobby, ballooned into a media empire, and now we're seeing stories that the business of podcasting is in decline. How has the rise of the podcasting industry affected the individual podcaster? Do you run your podcast as a small business or as a hobby you can monetise, and how do you keep your podcast finances sustainable? What are the benefits of joining a podcasting network, or do you prefer to do your own thing?
schedule.title: Podcasts and Big Business
Co-Writing: a Growing Trend

schedule.desc: It wasn't too long ago where certain story concepts were being described as unfilmable, and yet in some cases, the impossible has already been achieved. But does 'just because you can, doesn't mean you should' apply double here? This panel examines the improbable, the impossible, the downright daft, and the wishlist for TV and film adaptations.
schedule.title: They Adapted WHAT?

schedule.desc: Men In Black let us know that aliens walk among us. Would aliens work the local corner shop, or are they more likely to try to take over the world? The panel discusses the liklihood of either options and many others in between.
schedule.title: How Real Aliens Would Behave on Earth

schedule.desc: Much of early modern Europe saw a frenzy of witch-hunting, but Scotland in the 16th and early 17th centuries was particularly badly affected, with thousands put on trial and hundreds executed. "Thou shall not suffer a witch to live," the King James Bible proclaims, words that King James himself took to heart, developing an obsession with witchcraft after becoming convinced that Scottish witches had attempted to drown him at sea by calling up a storm. He was also the patron of Shakespeare who wrote Macbeth.  How do all of these influences play out?  Was the king a driver or follower of the deadly, broader cultural darkness of the milieu?
schedule.title: King James, Witchcraft, Macbeth

schedule.desc: The ableist world presents many challenges for disabled people. Those whose disabilities aren't apparent at a glance often struggle in silence. How can people living with chronic pain, autism, ADHD, blindness or low vision, deafness, and other invisible disabilities be better supported so that all people can thrive and enjoy the same experiences?
schedule.title: The Challenges of Invisible Disabilities

schedule.desc: Sometimes fanfic writing is driven by spite when the latest sequel or episode invalidates your cherished fan theory or your WIP fanwork, the writer or showrunner treats a character or plotline badly, or the ending of a show does not satisfactorily tie up loose ends or character arcs. Our panellists reveal when spite or rage makes them get their fanfic on. How have they seen this play out as fandoms evolve over time? And what about when it is regressive, such as invalidating a canon interracial relationship?
schedule.title: Writing Against Canon

schedule.desc: Pursuing storytelling in multiple mediums could be the path forward for your creative career. How can you make your IP work for you? Discover the how-to, the pitfalls, and the advantages of franchising your IP.
schedule.title: Franchising Your Intellectual Property

schedule.desc: The wool trade underpinned the medieval English economy and later inspired the Highland clearances that led to the loss of entire communities. The desire for silk created trade routes between China and Europe, bringing prosperity in its wake. Demand for cotton and cotton clothing drove the industrial revolution, helped make the slave trade profitable, and encouraged the creation of sweatshops. What role might textiles play in imagined worlds?
schedule.title: Worldbuilding with Wool, Silk and Cloth of Gold

schedule.desc:
Join us for a convention opening night of Scottish culture with a ceilidh dance with added Science!

We're delighted to be joined by the Science Ceilidh Band who have performed at Worldcon before. They will take time at the start to teach you the right moves as well.

We also hope to see many Landing Zone tartans swirling!

More on Ceilidhs: Scotland has a strong tradition of song, poetry and dance, and Glasgow 2024 will fully embrace this. We will run a number of dance events during the convention, starting with a Ceilidh (KAY-lee) on Thursday night. Descended from the Gaelic word for 'gathering' or 'party, nowadays when people think of a Ceilidh, they think of a fun filled night of wild dancing, good music and great company! Ceilidh dancing is truly glorious when done right, fuelled by a sense of community and often a few pints. Here at Glasgow 2024, we want to honour this tradition and hold our own Ceilidh! Don’t worry if you’re unsure about how to participate, there will be instructions for all.
schedule.title: The Science Ceilidh

schedule.desc:
We’ll be sharing songs and music until late. Come join our Filk Circle!

Additional space for smaller circles is available in Jura and Barra.
schedule.title: Open Filk - Thursday

schedule.desc:
From Ursula K. Le Guin's experiments with anarchism in the Hainish Cycle to Malka Older's Infomocracy, via Ankh-Morpork's autocracy and Ellen Kushner's republican Riverside, SFF experiments with all kinds of governments but so frequently comes back to monarchy and empire. Why are we drawn to these forms of government in our fiction? Who is most effectively playing with different governments today? And what governments aren't we seeing in our SFF?

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Governments in SFF (Online)

schedule.desc: Join your fellow convention members, and perhaps some big names, for a gentle stroll (1.3 miles/2km) around Festival Park, across the river from the SEC, led by Farah Mendlesohn and Mike Scott. The route is wheelchair-accessible, and we will adjust our pace to match the abilities of the slowest walkers. Sign up at the Registration Desk by 18:00 the previous day, and meet at 09:00 outside the Crowne Plaza hotel’s main entrance.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars - Friday, Festival Park

schedule.desc: Science fiction costuming has become significantly more sophisticated over time. The panel discuss examples of early costumes, what has led to the complex costumes we expect to see today, how early science fiction costuming impacted on the storytelling, and where we would like to see SF costuming go in the future.
schedule.title: History of Costumes Throughout Science Fiction

schedule.desc: Uzumaki, Amigara Fault and Tomi; when we want something to scare us, Junji Ito is always there to hold our hand in the dark. But what about the other artists hiding in the shadows? Join us as we explore lesser-known but just as scary horror manga and anime. After all, nothing is scarier than things you don't already know...
schedule.title: This Genre Was Made for Me: Horror in Anime and Manga

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s Glasgow 2024 feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organisers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we may otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Friday

schedule.desc: Trinidad and Tobago has a long rich history of speculative fiction story telling. The panel will discuss the evolution of Trinidadian speculative fiction throughout the centuries, beginning with oral tales, through its presence in Calypso, and into the future in the publishing industry.
schedule.title: Under the Silk Cotton Tree

schedule.desc: Scotland is home to the world's largest Performing Arts festival: let's look at the work involved in producing your own play, explore the challenges involved bringing science fiction to the stage, and what's coming to the fringe that might interest you.
schedule.title: Producing SF Drama for The Fringe and Beyond

schedule.desc: Your survival in a zombie outbreak may depend on coming to this talk! Scientist Sarita Robinson explains the dos and don'ts that will give you your best chance at outwitting the shuffling undead. Not for the faint of heart! Recommended for ages 8-12.
schedule.title: How to Survive Zombies

schedule.desc: The panel discusses how ideas from the past – whether presented as science fiction or factual predictions – have stood the test of time. Which have come true, which were way off, and which are still future possibilities? And who proved better at predicting the future? Was it the scientists, mathematicians and engineers… or the science fiction writers?
schedule.title: Predicting the Shape of Things to Come

schedule.desc: So you've started a podcast! You've got microphones and editing software and even a few listeners! What's next? How do you keep your podcast exciting and build an audience? How do you measure success or failure? Does every podcaster want to keep growing their audience, or are you happy in your small niche?
schedule.title: The Difficult Second Album

schedule.desc: From debut authors to seasoned ones, publishing takes its toll on all. But what are the causes? How can you learn cope with the demands of publication both before and after release? What do you need to know in order to survive the marketing jungle?
schedule.title: Maintaining Your Mental Health in Publishing

schedule.desc:
1. Representing History in The Three Body Problem and The Poppy War - Melissa Hosek
2. Pseudo-Documentary in Science Fiction: The Future as Witness to History - Xuying Yu
3. Terry Pratchett in the Time of Steam-Engines: What Is Our Role in a Pre-determined Future? - Samuel Poots
schedule.title: Speculative Histories

schedule.desc: Part of our introduction to series, which offer a general overview of popular tropes, areas or authors SFF. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to African SFF

schedule.desc: Carrying sufficient supplies to support the crew for the duration of a long-haul space mission isn't practical, so they will need to produce their own food on board. What vegetables will they take into space? How will they grow them (allowing that gravity may be reduced or even absent for much of the journey)? And what crops will they eventually plant when they settle on new worlds? The panel discusses some <s>onions</s> options.
schedule.title: Vegetables in Space

schedule.desc: This meetup provides an opportunity for our bisexual attendees to share a common space within a supportive community setting.
schedule.title: Bisexual Attendees Meetup

schedule.desc: Expert ballon sculptor John Wardale will take requests to make animals, vehicles, aliens and more. Recommended age 3-12
schedule.title: Balloon Animal Sculpting

schedule.desc:
Preliminary Business Meeting. Attendees at the Preliminary Business Meeting set the agenda for the rest of the sessions throughout the convention; vote on resolutions; and hear reports from past, current, and future Worldcons.

There will be a 45-minute lunch break each day from 12:15 to 13:00. A pre-ordered, pre-packaged lunch for £10 will be available from The Village Hotel. Orders may be placed between 9:15 to 10:15 each day and then picked up during the lunch break.
10-minute ergo/bio breaks will be planned at 11:00 and 14:00. The exact time of the break will be dependent on where we are in the business, but breaks should occur within 10 minutes of the planned time.
schedule.title: WSFS Business Meeting - Friday

schedule.desc: Human activities such as mining, urbanisation, and industrialisation release pollutants - including heavy metals, microplastics, persistent organic compounds and radionuclides - to the environment. This talk will discuss the affect of these contaminants on environmental and human health using examples from Scotland and further afield and explain how analytical science is critical for achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals
schedule.title: Analytical Geochemistry and Sustainability

schedule.desc: Connect with fellow admirers of Octavia Butler's visionary works to celebrate her groundbreaking contributions to science fiction literature and discuss the enduring impact of her narratives on society and culture. Join us for insightful discussions and a shared appreciation of Butler's unparalleled storytelling prowess.
schedule.title: Fans of Octavia Butler Meetup

schedule.desc: Works of art often tell stories. Artists can present narrative in many ways: by using a series of images representing moments in a story or by selecting a central moment to stand for the whole story. Our panellists discuss how to make a narrative visual.
schedule.title: Artists as Storytellers

schedule.desc: From inspiring the plot of Forbidden Planet to being quoted by Klingons in Star Trek VI and then appearing as a character himself in Doctor Who, William Shakespeare casts a long shadow over science fiction. Our panellists will explore these and the Bard of Avon's other influences on SFF.
schedule.title: All the Shakespeare: the Bard's Influence on SFF

schedule.desc: Comics such as The Department of Truth, The Once and Future, Hexagon Bridge, and I Kill Giants occupy a creative ground between DC/Marvel and the literary graphic novels of Alison Bechdel or Joe Sacco. This is a chance to talk about some of the best darned comics of the last few years--and to look at the aesthetic matters and means of production of independent, 'author-owned' comics.
schedule.title: Not Just Superheroes: The Best of the Rest in Modern Comics

schedule.desc: Internet of things, AI and other applications are driving demand for digital storage and memory. Existing storage media are advancing to provide greater capacity whilst novel media such as DNA are being explored. Demand for conventional volatile and emerging non-volatile memory is growing with powerful new developments emerging. This talk explores the amazing advances in memory and storage that will enable future computing technologies.
schedule.title: Memories of Tomorrow

schedule.desc: Fantasy has just as much scope for social progress as SF, and magic could arguably more easily bridge worlds and cross the gulfs between the stars than technology. How do authors use magic in a science fictional way? What are some of the panel's favourite space stories that use magic rather than technology?
schedule.title: The Magical Future: High Magic as High Tech/Spells in Space

schedule.desc: The moment has finally arrived, and expectations are high. For some writers, their debut is the ‘BANG’ beginning of a starry career, but for others, it fizzles out. Are authors truly prepared for either outcome? Is this the one-off chance to make it? What can you do if your debut is not as you expected?
schedule.title: The Impact of a Good Debut on a Writer’s Career

schedule.desc: From Claire North's Ithaca to Vaishnavi Patel's Kaikeyi, books set in or based on ancient civilizations are popular with readers and writers alike. But can writers borrow from ancient cultures without the ancient context? Do they inevitably place modern perspectives on ancient worlds and thus can never extract from them neutrally?
schedule.title: Ancient Cultures and Context
Surviving Futures

schedule.desc:
Take a guided tour of his artwork with Guest of Honour Chris Baker (Fangorn).
Meet in the Art Show in Hall 5 at his exhibit.
schedule.title: Fangorn: Artshow Walkthrough

schedule.desc:
Join Helen Gould's workshop on how to become a sensitivity reader or consultant. This is your chance to learn more about these important roles and the responsibilities they carry in an interactive setting.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Becoming A Sensitivity Reader/Consultant

schedule.desc: Measurement science has seen amazing advances in recent years, from medical diagnostics to remote sensing. However it still typically takes over a week to receive a forensic DNA profiling result, and hours of sample preparation plus access to large expensive laboratory-based instrumentation to measure trace levels of pollutants in environmental samples. The panel discusses why we don’t yet have a universal analytical device that can read out composition in real time. What are the challenges? And how might these be overcome?
schedule.title: Where’s My Tricorder? Measurement Science in Fact and Fiction

schedule.desc: Filk is the music of fandom: a musical culture, a genre, and just as importantly, a community. Our experienced filkers talk about when and how they fell in love with filk, how their relationship with it may have changed since that initial rush of emotion, and why it touches the soul of the fannish audience. And they’ll persuade you, too, to fall in love with this unique part of our community.
schedule.title: Why We Fall in Love with Filk

schedule.desc: Come join other Pokémon GO players to share your latest discoveries and your enthusiasm for this AR gaming phenomenon in a scheduled meetup.
schedule.title: Pokémon GO Players Meetup

schedule.desc: An hour will not be enough for interviewer Amal El-Mohtar to chat to our GoH Terri Windling about all her achievements. Terri Windling is an American writer and eminent editor in the field of fantasy literature, as well as a visual artist, folklorist, and fairy tale historian.
schedule.title: Guest of Honour Interview: Terri Windling

schedule.desc: Part of our Introduction To series, which offers a general overview of popular SFF tropes, areas or authors. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to Cosy SFF

schedule.desc: As anyone who's ever tried to create something knows, the biggest hurdle is starting in the first place. How do you go from talking about what you want to make (armchair making) to actually building things? And how do you keep from being pulled into Side Quests or distracted from ongoing projects by the New Shiny?
schedule.title: Making Makers Make

schedule.desc: Iain M. Banks authored many popular science fiction novels, but what of the books he wrote as Iain Banks? While billed as literary fiction, these often contain SFFH elements, whether gothic horror, multiverse SF, or general weirdness. Friends of and experts on Iain Banks will discuss his slippery, uncategorisable, and undeniably brilliant writing, as well as recommending their favourite Iain (no M) Banks books.
schedule.title: Iain Banks: Between Genre and the Mainstream

schedule.desc: In the second of the Initiative for Interstellar Studies programme items on worldships in fact and fiction, the panel discusses the scenarios that might prompt a worldship mission, from ecological collapse or nuclear war to exploration, colonization, or search for extra-terrestrial intelligence. The panellists also explore the role of AI - if any - in conducting uncrewed missions in preparation for the worldship stage, propulsions systems for getting to Alpha Centauri, and downlink options for getting messages back to Earth.
schedule.title: Worldships 2: Reasons for Going and What Can Be Achieved Soon

schedule.desc: In the aftermath of the Second World War, a generation of British fans were starting or preparing to transition from fandom to professional writing. Arthur C. Clarke was the best known of this cohort, but his contemporaries included Frank Arnold, Ken Bulmer, John F. Burke, and William F. Temple. Join us as we look back on these writers as they took their first steps into the world of paid authorship.
schedule.title: Arthur C. Clarke and Post-war Britain's Fan-to-Pro Ascensions

schedule.desc: Nnedi Okorafor, Rebecca Roanhorse, N.K. Jemisin: all high-profile, recent converts from writing novels to writing comics. Where does the attraction lie in writing for a different medium, and what challenges have they faced?
schedule.title: From Prose to Pow!

schedule.desc: Is Young Adult solely a marketing category, or has it developed its own conventions - and the tropes and cliches that go with them? Our panel of publishing experts discusses what categorises a science fiction or fantasy novel as Young Adult and examines current trends and expectations.
schedule.title: The Conventions and Cliches of YA Fiction
Using Nanomedicines to Improve Our Health – Small Yet Mighty

schedule.desc: Genre classifications make booksellers' lives easier. But can writing always be fit into specific categories? Is the rise in talk of ‘combined genres’ reflecting something new, or is it just another way to classify?
schedule.title: Combining genres: From Science-Fantasy to Romantasy

schedule.desc: Part of our Introduction To series, which offers a general overview of popular SFF tropes, areas or authors. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to Romantasy

schedule.desc: Using natural materials, learn to make some simple spells and other crafts of the fairy folk. Recommended for ages 3-10
schedule.title: Fairy Crafts and Spells

schedule.desc: Abigail Nussbaum is a Hugo Award-winning critic and author of the blog Asking the Wrong Questions -- and now, author of the collection Track Changes: Selected Reviews! Join Abigail and Niall Harrison for a discussion about sf criticism, the state of the field, and the intersections between the fantastic genres, politics, and culture, followed by the opportunity to buy Track Changes.
schedule.title: Book Launch: Track Changes by Abigail Nussbaum

schedule.desc: Nnedi Okorafor’s work spans the entire gamut of genre, from fantasy to sci-fi to horror, while also writing for all ages and across books, graphic novels and TV - with no little success, as proven by her Hugo, Nebula, World Fantasy, Locus, Lodestar Awards, a Wole Soyinka Prize for Literature and an Eisner Award nomination.
schedule.title: Guest of Honour Interview: Nnedi Okorafor

schedule.desc: A talk about what science is and what it is not. A brief run through human stupidity and malice, concentrating on why much of what you think you know about science is not correct. To go all sci-fi - the future of humanity depends on people knowing this stuff.
schedule.title: Are You Smarter than a Monkey?

schedule.desc: Editors at major SFF publishing houses talk about their career paths, how they started and how they ended up in their current positions.
schedule.title: Editors and Their Career Paths

schedule.desc: "Mrs. Hawking" is the first in a trilogy of fully staged and professionally filmed theatrical shows. Part Victorian adventure and part superhero story, our story begins in the year 1880 in the reign of Queen Victoria. Young Mary Stone has just arrived alone and friendless in London, unsure of what to do with herself after a lifetime of keeping house for her late parents in India. She has no choice but to accept a position as a house girl for Mrs. Victoria Hawking, an aloof, mysterious society widow who seems to want nothing to do with her. But when she discovers Mrs. Hawking’s true business, as a secret champion to the otherwise helpless women of London, Mary is drawn into a world of new heroic purpose battling against devious blackmailers, rescuing kidnapped children, and struggling against the restrictive place their society forces on women. Content notes: mentions of stillbirth. Running time: 56 min
schedule.title: Mrs. Hawking

schedule.desc: Just add murder! From crime-solving wizards to undead detectives, the joy of the fantasy, science-fiction and horror genre is its versatility and how well it plays with others, especially crime. Come along as this panel discusses their favourite genre mashups and the ingredients to a criminally good SFFH story.
schedule.title: Fantasy Noir and Other SFFH Mashups

schedule.desc: The most important challenge currently facing human civilisation is global climate change, with much of it driven by fossil fuel combustion. The panel discusses the current status of renewable energy and reviews emerging and alternative energy sources from back-yard nuclear reactors to space-based solar power. How far are these from practical application on a scale that would remove our reliance on coal, gas and oil?
schedule.title: Sustainability 2: Fuelling the Future

people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

schedule.desc: Few places are as magical as a library. From the mysterious underground library in Erin Morgenstern's The Starless Sea to the shadowy machinations of The Invisible Library created by Genevieve Cogman, libraries are far more than shelves of books and their fierce guardians. Why are readers and writers endlessly drawn to these repositories of the written word? And what does the library of the future look like?
schedule.title: All They're Stacked Up to Be: Libraries in SFF

schedule.desc: A podcast by three fantasy authors who love to overcomplicate their writing lives and want to help you do the same.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Worldbuilding for Masochists

schedule.desc:
Join the Luna Press book launch to celebrate the release of the 2024 Summer titles!

Nikhil Singh: Dakini Atoll; Neil Williamson and Andrew J Wilson: Nova Scotia 2, New Speculative Fiction from Scotland; Tiffani Angus and Val Nolan: Spec Fic for Newbies Vol 2; and Teija Marija Smits: The Utopia of Us Charity Anthology. Also in attendance in the room, many of the authors in our anthologies!
schedule.title: Luna Press Book Launch Party

people.name: Francesca T Barbini - Luna Press Publishing
Nova Scotia Vol 2: New Speculative Fiction from Scotland

schedule.desc:
Come celebrate new and upcoming releases from the Edinburgh SFF Writers! Hear about our books, meet the authors and members of this vibrant local community, grab a book cake,
some gorgeous bookish merch and maybe even some advance copies. Featuring Nicholas Binge (Dissolution), Annabel Campbell (The Outcast Mage), A.Y. Chao (Paris Celestial), Genoveva Dimova (Foul Days / Monstrous Nights), David Goodman (A Reluctant Spy), Shauna Lawless (The Land Of The Living And The Dead), Catriona Silvey (Love And Other Paradoxes), and Lorraine Wilson (We Are All Ghosts In The Forest).
schedule.title: Edinburgh SFF Writers - Book Party

schedule.desc:
Learn how to make a little beaded leaf that can then be stitched onto a garment. Technique is freeform peyote stitch, all materials provided, although if you have any size 11 seed beads you'd like to use, please bring them.

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Making Beaded Leaves

schedule.desc:
This is a chance to create a fanzine for and about the Glasgow 2024 Worldcon. The aim is to produce the fanzine by the time the Hugo Ceremony starts. Come along to find out more about the project and get involved.

This session will be taking place in Hall 4 within the Fan Lounge area.

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Let's Create the Glasgow 2024 Fanzine - Kick Off Session

schedule.desc: What do you see when your character gets part of what they want? Mixed success, Disaster with a twist, Fail with hope, Critical Fail, this panel digs into how TTRPGs play with success and failure and the narrative consequences or chaos that can ensue! For both those playing and those facilitating, the resulting story may turn out to be nothing close to what anyone imagined.
schedule.title: That's a Mixed Success

schedule.desc: Fanfiction is in part a refuge for people who feel underserved by commercial fiction offerings. This is expressed via fixits, fluff, whump, queernorm worlds with happy endings, rescuing a character from their creator, and of course the forbidden crossovers. Our panel discusses why that is, what we get from fanfic that we can't find elsewhere, and what commercial fiction has learned and should learn from transformative works.
schedule.title: Writing the Gaps: How Does Fanfic Reach the Parts Commercial Fiction Does Not?

schedule.desc: From Melisa Scott's Shadow Man to Yoon Ha Lee's Ninefox Gambit, speculative fiction has long been a place to play with ideas of gender. We will consider the ways that authors have used the freedoms and limitations of speculative fiction to explore the space of gender and expand on the boundaries around gender expectations.
schedule.title: Playing With Gender and Gender Expectations in SFF

schedule.desc: Our group of critics and reviewers will talk about our Hugo nominees for Best Novel, Series and Graphic Story before the winners are announced, what they say about the state of the genre, and discuss the spread!
schedule.title: Hugo Shortlist Discussion: Best Novel, Series and Graphic Story

schedule.desc:
Come hear what is on offer from next year's Worldcon, and what's being proposed for 2026 and beyond!

In the first half of the session, we'll hear first from Los Angeles in 2026, the single bid for the 2024 Worldcon.  There will also be presentations from bidders for the 2027 and 2028 Worldcons.

After an interval of 15 minutes. Seattle Worldcon 2025 will present their plans.  They will be followed by bids for 2029 and beyond.
schedule.title: Future Worldcons Q&A

schedule.desc:
"Is tric gum bi draoidheachd is seanchas a' nochdadh sna h-òrain Gàidhlig, air am fighe le ar saoghal fhèin mar a bha e ann am beatha nan Gàidheal o shean. Gheibhear beartas eisimpleirean dhiubh, mìneachadh, agus cothrom òran ionnsachadh. Tro mheadhan na Gàidhlig.

Gaelic Lore: Magic in the Melodies
Just as the Gaels see the mundane and otherworlds as intertwined, so is the rich tapestry of Gaelic song threaded with examples of otherworldly encounters, love, magic, and loss. Learn about some prominent examples and enjoy the chance to learn a Gaelic song. This programme item will be held through the medium of Gaelic.
schedule.title: Seanchas nan Gàidheal: Draoidheachd sna Fuinn

schedule.desc: The COVID-19 pandemic affected us all, but different countries took very different approaches to dealing with it, from strict extended lockdowns to essentially ‘business as usual’. This panel discusses the lessons learned – or not learned – and considers how we might better manage the next pandemic.
schedule.title: Learning from COVID – An International Perspective

schedule.desc: A meetup for fans hailing from Southeast Asia, celebrating the region's diverse culture, literature, films, music, and more, where enthusiasts can connect, share interests, and revel in the rich traditions of their homeland.
schedule.title: Meetup of Southeast Asian Fans

schedule.desc:
1. Beyond the Posthuman Predicament: Focusing on Critical Nonhumanism in Recent Korean SF - Inchan Pak
2. Posthuman Futures in Annihilation and Subway - Xiuqi Huang
schedule.title: Posthuman Futures

schedule.desc:
Join the University of Glasgow Advanced Research Centre for a Research Showcase covering everything from talks on Star Wars, giant robots, and space gaming to stalls showcasing research-informed games created at the University, tours of labs, a Q&A with University of Glasgow alumnus (the Astrogamer) Scott Manley, a gamified theatre performance, and opportunities to playtest cooperative games from rogue AIs and space weather to flooding crises.

If there is high demand and you aren’t able to access any particular event, or need to wait until a later time to browse the showcase in the ARC, then we encourage you to enjoy the sights around this historic and futuristic University, and will aim to signpost you to different attractions. @UofGGamesLab #TeamUofG
schedule.title: Games and Gaming Lab Research Showcase and Playtesting

schedule.desc:
Islamic geometric art is a traditional decorative art used to add beauty to everything from manuscripts of the Qur'an to architecture across the Islamic world. These characteristic patterns can be constructed with just a compass, ruler, and basic understanding of geometry. In this workshop, you will learn to construct a basic eightfold pattern at the heart of many Moroccan designs, based on a motif known as the "Breath of the Compassionate". 

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Islamic Geometric Art Workshop

schedule.desc:
We are exceptionally proud and privileged to present a performance of the score of the 2014 film Interstellar by organist Roger Sayer, who worked on the composition of the film score with Hans Zimmer, recorded the original organ soundtrack of the film and whose passion for this piece of music is unmatched. He will perform the score along with other science fiction-related pieces(*) and will speak about the score and experience of recording for the film. 

Playlist:
Also Sprach Zarathustra (theme from 2001: A Space Odyssey)
Three movements of The Planets Suite
Q&A with Roger Sayer
Interstellar 'Suite'
schedule.title: Interstellar Film Score Performance & Q&A

schedule.desc: Quantum technologies (QTs) may potentially revolutionise a host of applications in computing, communications, and sensing with new or enhanced capabilities. Bringing QTs from Earth into space may greatly expand its horizons, including the creation of a space-based quantum internet. In this talk, we will cover efforts to utilise CubeSats (a type of nanosatellite) to develop quantum space missions, the prospects for globe-spanning quantum constellations, and display an actual quantum CubeSat and hardware.
schedule.title: Quantum In Space! Big Adventures for Small Satellites

schedule.desc:
Come along and play the ultimate game of trust and treachery and catch the werewolves before they chomp the entire town!
A playfully theatrical experience in which allegiances are formed, suspicions raised, and barefaced lies are the currency! Like the television show 'The Traitors' (BBC) but with even more bite!
*Trigger warning: there are descriptions of deaths as our gory story unfolds. 
You may find the sing up link for this item at the bottom of this page: https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/glasgow-university/
schedule.title: Bunbury Banter Theatre presents “Werewolf”
