schedule.desc: Return to the Forbidden Planet rocked our spaceship. The Rocky Horror Picture Show had us dancing the timewarp. The Little Shop of Horrors, taught us botany and Young Frankenstein put on the Ritz. The panel will talk about the best and worst SF musicals, originals versus adaptions, and why we should have more of them.
schedule.title: SF&F Musicals on Stage

schedule.desc: Ahsoka brought to live-action televison characters who have populated books, comics and animated television from a period stretching some 33 years. Our panel reflects on how Star Wars Rebels, The Clone Wars, and Timothy Zahn's Thrawn series have come to fruition in this modern continuation of selected parts.
schedule.title: Ahsoka: Fusing Clone Wars, Rebels and Heir to the Empire

schedule.desc: Why is so much fantastical YA fiction set in historical periods or variations of them? What are the benefits of setting a plot in one era rather than another? What is the appeal of times gone by, that we so often go back to them in fantasy works? So many questions, so little time - and yet time is at the center of this panel.
schedule.title: Once Upon a (Different) Time

schedule.desc: Even with sales numbers dropping and the distribution channel scattered and shredded, there's never been a better time to be a comics fan. Marvel and DC are doing some of their best work in years, perhaps under the pressure from the strong stories from other publishers as well as the surge of independents. Our panellists consider the state of comics publishing today. Look out for the Comic Book Sommelier session where you can get personalised recommendations!
schedule.title: Never Had It So Good? Life as a Comics Fan Today

schedule.desc: There were also Worldcons in Glasgow in 1995 and 2005 when a lot about the world, fandom, and even the SEC seemed quite different. What was it like to run those conventions and to attend them? What was significant at the time, and what stands out now? What still seems just as relevant in 2024?
schedule.title: A Retrospective Look at 1995 and 2005 Scottish Worldcons

schedule.desc: OK, we tried, but it's time to admit it - we messed up the world. YA literature often acts as the little boy who dared to cry out "The emperor has no clothes!" But should literary youth also be tasked with saving the world we've created? Do non-literary youth even want to, or could we stop them if we tried? Some teenagers sneak out to save the world while others "just" save their parents and loved ones. Is this trope empowering or another form of unrealistic escapism? All this and more in this panel for the generations.
schedule.title: And Adults Will Shout "Save Us!"

schedule.desc: Whether the wild faeries of A Midsummer NIght's Dream, the spiteful Tinker Bell in J.M. Barrie's Peter Pan to the less than pleasant creatures in Heather Fawcett's Emily Wilde's Encyclopaedia of Faeries, faeries (aka fay, fae, fey, fair folk or fairies) have been a staple of the fantasy fiction landscape for centuries. Join our panel as they delve into the various interpretations and manifestations of these beings and our eternal fascination with them.
schedule.title: Faeries in Fantasy Literature

schedule.desc: Special Guest Samantha Béart is a BAFTA nominated actor for their role as Karlach in Baldur's Gate 3. Other games include The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow, Demon’s Souls and Bithell Games' The Solitaire Conspiracy. Samantha's extensive career includes Random in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (who they also played in the subsequent UK theatre tour) and Orr in Torchwood for Big Finish. Come and hear all about their career and passions!
schedule.title: A Fireside Chat with Samantha Béart

schedule.desc: For fans and creators of colour, underrepresentation, erasure, and invisibility are major problems in SFF. For East and Southeast Asian fans and creators in particular, this is compounded by the racism and xenophobia of techno-orientalism: a damaging trope where East Asianness specifically is shorthand for dehumanisation, materialism, and dystopia (think Blade Runner, Neuromancer, or Cyberpunk 2077). How do we create and critique in genres that see us as the enemy?
schedule.title: When the Future Hates and Fears Us: Techno-orientalism in SFF

schedule.desc: From Walter M. Miller's A Canticle to Leibowitz to Bogi Takács' Three Partitions, the work of Ada Palmer's Terra Ignota and Frank Herbert's Dune and in the work of our guests of honour, Nnedi Okorafor and Ken MacLeod, religion has been an invigorating part of science fiction. This panel will discuss science fiction's contested relationship with religion and godhood and the ways the literature of the future incorporates the faiths of the present and past.
schedule.title: Religion and Godhood in Science Fiction

schedule.desc:
In this hands-on tasting experience you'll learn all about the history and crafting of gin. You'll taste a variety of different gins that reflect this history and the ways that gin has been made and appreciated through time. Of course this will include our signature Glasgow 2024 Gin, crafted and distilled in collaboration with Pixel Spirits Distillery & Spirit School. Space is limited and advance sign up is requested, although drop-ins are welcome if space is available.
Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Gin Tasting Session #1

schedule.desc:
Join Gareth L Powell for his workshop on creative writing.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Creative Writing Workshop from Gareth L Powell

schedule.desc: Let's gather during Worldcon to debate whether we should pursue incorporating WSFS and implementing more accountability within WSFS and the Hugo administration process. What are the pros and cons of such a solution, and should we make any changes? The intention is to specify what we expect for the future of the Hugo Awards.
schedule.title: How is the Hugo Award Administered These Days, Anyway?

schedule.desc: It's now 50 years since Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson unleashed Dungeons and Dragons on an unsuspecting world. Since then DnD has been joined by a legion of other games with TTRPGs developing in ways scarcely imaginable to anyone who had picked up Gygax and Arneson's first box set. Join us as we mark the first 50 years of tabletop roleplaying and explore the strange roads down which TTRPGs have led players.
schedule.title: 50 Years of TTRPGs

schedule.desc: In this panel, three lecturers from the University of Cambridge and Imperial College London, Stephen Cave, Kanta Dihal and Kerry McInerney, will discuss how they use science fiction to teach the ethics of science and technology. We will address two key issues: the role science fiction plays in their classroom as examples of ethical issues in science and technology and the role of science fiction in the ‘sociotechnical imaginary’: how does SF shape the expectations and actions of a wide range of stakeholders in science and technology, from engineers to policy makers, and why it is important for students to be aware of this?
schedule.title: Using Science Fiction to Teach Ethics

schedule.desc: This hands-on workshop will introduce you to the mathematical art of modular origami. Recommended for ages 8-15.
schedule.title: Modular Origami

schedule.desc: Want to know more about what's involved in storyboarding for a feature film? Guest of Honour Chris Baker reveals all.
schedule.title: Chris Baker (Fangorn): Storyboarding for Film

schedule.desc:
Join us for a guided tour around the University of Glasgow’s Quantum Research Labs!
Maximum of 30 people per tour. Each tour lasts 45-60 minutes, with stacked starts: 15:00, 15:15, 15:30.
You may find the sing up link for this item at the bottom of this page: https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/glasgow-university/
schedule.title: Quantum Lab Tours

schedule.desc: From Samuel Butler's 1872 novel Erewhon to Kazuo Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun, readers and writers continue to be fascinated by artificial intelligence, in both utopian and dystopian settings. As scientists and engineers note the implausibility of many science fiction scenarios, what does it take to create a believable fictional AI character? Join our panel as they discuss their favourite, and least favourite, AIs, robots and sentient machines.
schedule.title: Imagining our Great AI Overlords

schedule.desc:
Ken MacLeod is one of Scotland's foremost science-fiction writers and thinkers, equally at home in the vastness of space as the intricate politics of his home country.

Come along as Ken chats with Niall Harrison about his journey from IT analyst to award-winning SF writer. Stops along the way will include Space Opera, A.I., technology, poetry and Faster Than Light travel.
schedule.title: Guest of Honour Interview: Ken MacLeod

schedule.desc: During this talk, you will be boarding a Pan-African spaceship sending Afronauts to Mars. During the voyage, Afronauts rewrite the history and future of space exploration and give birth to Pan-African space law that halts the exploitation of humans, non-humans and more-than-humans. The reimagining happens by exploring the future through an alternative past - what if the first person on the Moon were a Kenyan female? How would space law have evolved?
schedule.title: Reimagining Space Law Through Afrofuturism

schedule.desc:
Chat, share, and crochet/knit/weave/spin/sew in this quiet work session. Chatting is allowed, but this meetup is specifically for those looking for a low-volume opportunity to connect with other crafters. (See also the Crochet, Knitting, Sewing, and Fibre Arts Lively Meetup.)

No sign-ups are required but a maximum of 10 people can join this session.
schedule.title: Crochet, Knitting, Sewing, and Fibre Arts Quiet Meetup

schedule.desc: Gwen Knighton, award winning wire harper, singer-songwriter, and founding member of the band Three Weird Sisters, shares songs and tunes from places far and near. Born and raised in the Southern United States, she emigrated to the UK in the early aughts and narrowly escaped London for Scotland just two years ago. Gwen lives in Perth.
schedule.title: Filk concert: Gwen Knighton

schedule.desc: A stand-out characteristic of Glasgow 2024 has been our artwork, from the announcement of the Worldcon bid right through to the convention itself. Whether designing covers for publications, badges, logos, tiaras, Zoom backgrounds, postcards, Hugo award bases, labels for our GIn2024 bottles, and even our tartan "Landing Zone", Glasgow 2024's award-winning artists Sara Felix and Iain Clark have taken on every challenge and delivered stunning and unique art. Join them to hear more about their creations.
schedule.title: The Art of Glasgow 2024

schedule.desc:
It's now 50 years since Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson unleashed Dungeons and Dragons on an unsuspecting world. Since then DnD has been joined by a legion of other games with TTRPGs developing in ways scarcely imaginable to anyone who had picked up Gygax and Arneson's first box set. Join us as we mark the first 50 years of tabletop roleplaying and explore the strange roads down which TTRPGs have led players.

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: 50 Years of TTRPGs (Online)

schedule.desc: Bring a book and a beverage and read silently, potentially ending with a chat to your neighbours about what you just read.
schedule.title: Silent Reading Meetup

schedule.desc: Actual play media is a new form of entertainment that is only increasing in popularity. This panel discusses the unique pleasures of watching other people play games, as well as the differences between a professional and a home game. How is actual play effecting gaming products, and what developments do we see for the future of live play?
schedule.title: Watching, Playing, Performing: TTRPG Actual Play

schedule.desc: If 2000 AD's Judge Dredd started out as a punk rebellion against the right-wing politics of the 1970s, have the Judges now morphed to become a symbol of law and order rather than a satire? Our panel discusses the changing perceptions and roles of Judge Dredd and his cohorts.
schedule.title: Copaganda and the Judge Dredd Conundrum

schedule.desc:
Come join us for a Timey-Wimey voyage through dances from fantasy and science fiction film, television, and literature! 

Fancy a Hunger Games District 12 wedding dance….or maybe a Targaryen one from House of the Dragon?  Wonderland’s Lobster Quadrille or a Firefly Shindig? Travelling to Bridgerton like Ruby Sunday and the Doctor or to the 25th century like Buck Rogers?  We’ll dance and laugh our way through them all! 

No experience is needed - all dances will be taught.  Costumes, creative dress from anywhere in space and time, and masks (the masquerade kind, not the Covid kind) are encouraged, but if you don’t have fancy dress, come as you are.  Personal disco balls and lobsters will be supplied!
schedule.title: The Timey Wimey Masked Ball

schedule.desc: Diasporas are created both by voluntary and involuntary migrations from countries of origin. How does one write from within and about the diasporic experience? What hurdles do diasporic writers face? And how can real-life experiences with diaspora be applied to a speculative setting?
schedule.title: Writing Diasporas in SFF

schedule.desc: 1. Nnedi Okorafor's Postcolonial Subversion of the Space Opera Technologiade in Binti (2015) - Joseph S. Norman
schedule.title: Diasporic Futures

schedule.desc: Your favourite anime has just been picked for a live action adaptation! With famous failures like Dragon Ball and Cowboy Bebop, those words can be more scary than exciting. But with recent flashy hits like Netflix's One Piece, there's more hope than ever for an adaptation to hit the mark and get it right. What makes a good live action anime, and what makes a really bad one? Join us on a deep dive into old adaptations, and share in our hopes for the future.
schedule.title: How to Make a Good Live Action Anime

schedule.desc: Take a hero, add adventure, sprinkle over some mortal peril, a test of character and skill, finish with an ultimate battle, and for just deserts, serve a triumphant return. Welcome to the hero's journey! This exact narrative template has inspired countless stories, but does it deserve its revered status? Come along to find out!
schedule.title: The Hero's Journey and why it works ... or doesn't!?

schedule.desc: From YouTube to Twitch to Instagram and Tiktok, creative content channels are everywhere, covering everything from gaming to comics to media critiques to costuming. What makes a compelling creative content channel, and how do you tailor the content to your platform? How do you find the best channels in your area of interest and unearth the smaller channels that don't grab the attention of the algorithm? Our panellists answer these questions and share some of their personal favourite channels.
schedule.title: Creative Content Creators

schedule.desc: The Glasgow SF Writers' Circle - a Glasgow institution for over 35 years - presents Gallus, an anthology of brand-new speculative fiction. This selection of brilliant short stories with a unique Glaswegian flavour covers the genre spectrum from fantasy to science fiction to horror and beyond, and features Hal Duncan, Ruth EJ Booth, Cameron Johnstone, and Annabel Campbell, as well as several voices making themselves heard for the very first time. Join editors Neil Williamson, Brian M. Milton, and E.M. Faulds and enjoy the fun!
schedule.title: Gallus: An Anthology by the Glasgow SF Writers’ Circle

schedule.desc: Get active and burn off some energy with some team games.
schedule.title: Team Games

schedule.desc: Part of our Introduction To series, which offers a general overview of popular SFF tropes, areas or authors. There will be more in depth items later in the programme related to the same topic.
schedule.title: Introduction to Genre Poetry

schedule.desc: From Matilda Wormwood to Lyra Belacqua and Percy Jackson, some of our most memorable and significant heroes come from children's literature. Why do these children make such a big impact? What turns ordinary kids into extraordinary heroes? And what can our young protagonists teach their adult counterparts about courage, loyalty, and how to overcome even the most terrifying villains and situations?
schedule.title: Great Heroes in Children’s Literature

schedule.desc: There's a whole wide audience of readers who love a spicy villain romantasy! What makes SFF narratives featuring villainous, or even morally-grey, characters as love interests so appealing? Are villains ever really worthy of love, or must they first be redeemed? Is there such a thing as too much of a villain?
schedule.title: Deliciously Evil: Villain Romances and Why We Love Them

schedule.desc:
We're seeing fewer stories where the lines of "good" and "evil" are clearly marked. Characters who blur the lines between hero and villain, or just step right over it are blossoming thoughout SFF. What makes these characters compelling? Can a character go too far to be redeemed? Does the want for morally grey characters reflect a larger trend in our society?

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: 50 Shades of Morally Grey Characters in SFF (Online)

schedule.desc:
Rebecca E. Treasure reads Flash for Apex Magazine. In this workshop, she will share her approach to writing flash. Bring your flash pieces, and be prepared to write a new one in this fast-paced workshop.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Flash Course in Flash Fiction

schedule.desc: Delve with us into the rich tapestry of voices shaping fandom and fantastic literature. Join our discussion as we explore the diverse perspectives and under-represented groups contributing to the ever-evolving landscape of storytelling and fan culture. Which of them require our special attention?
schedule.title: Under-Represented Groups in Fandom and Fantastic Literature

schedule.desc: An opportunity for small press professionals to meet up.
schedule.title: Small Press Publishers Meetup

schedule.desc:
John Robertson’s popular live-action video game, is a fast-paced, highly interactive show with improvisational comedy and retro gaming, where the audience experiences a multiplayer adventure run by John live in the hall!

The show is hugely popular, has appeared at the UK Eastercon and sells out annually in the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.
schedule.title: The Dark Room

schedule.desc: Comics and graphic novels present unique ways to tell stories, whether through an inherent part of the medium such as the size and layout, or by the way the story itself is formed of separate illustrated moments in time which force the reader to fill in the gaps between. Our panel looks at the different structures of storytelling in comics, discusses how they translate between physical and digital comics, and considers the benefits and challenges of this art form.
schedule.title: The Unique Storytelling Medium of Comics

schedule.desc: Most of Iain Banks's science fiction novels were set in the universe of The Culture, an advanced society of humans (or humanoids), drones, and unfathomably advanced machine intelligences. The Culture is usually presented as a utopia, with its inhabitants living lives untroubled by want in a society without property, government, or money. But is there a dark side to The Culture, with its tendency to interfere violently in the affairs of societies outside it? And have The Culture's humans given themselves over to decadence, abandoning their independence as they leave all decision-making to their machines?
schedule.title: The Sinister Underbelly of Iain M. Banks' The Culture

schedule.desc: Writers from the University of Edinburgh's Creative Writing MSc and PhD programmes share their creative work in this exciting showcase of new speculative work. The writers in this showcase come from all over the world and quite literally embody the Worldcon for Our Futures. They represent the next generation of spec fic writers and are concerned with ideas of alternative possible futures in their work. Sit back, enjoy these varied readings and be entertained!
schedule.title: University of Edinburgh New Writers Speculative Showcase

schedule.desc: The question of what turns matter into life threads through science fiction—from Golems to Frankenstein—and through science. Today's scientists are updating Mary Shelley's masterpiece, but now instead of sewing bodyparts together, we are working at the molecular scale, able at last to measure, interpret and perhaps even control how life's molecules make living things. But Shelley's tale was just as concerned by the ethical questions, and we'll see these have absolutely not gone away.
schedule.title: Frankenstein 2.0: Life from a Bag of Chemicals

schedule.desc: Laughs in Space is a fiction anthology celebrating the funny side of SF, and includes 24 stories, 22 of which are original to this book. Authors include Lavie Tidhar, Ian Watson, Fiona Moore, Emma Levin, Ida Keogh, Andrew Wallace, David Gullen, Rick Danforth, Gary Couzens, and many more. Pubished by The Slab Press.
schedule.title: Book Launch: Laughs in Space

schedule.desc: Nebula Science Fiction was the first official Scottish SFF magazine, although many more fanzines came after its release. Scottish fandom is brimming with intriguing publications crafted by its fans, and we will explore some of them in this panel!
schedule.title: Pure Dead Brilliant History of Scottish Fanzines

schedule.desc:
As long-duration spaceflight becomes reality, can we use science fiction to help direct research on astronauts' reproductive health and potential human reproduction in space? Join St Andrews University researchers in this interactive workshop to hear about their ongoing project using AI to connect science and science fiction and contribute your knowledge of fictional reproductive futures, from Bujold's uterine replicators to Brin's Gubru.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Workshop: Imagining Reproductive Futures Using Data Science

schedule.desc: Early space exploration was largely government-led, but independent companies such as SpaceX and Virgin Galactic are now gaining prominence. Does this encourage experimentation or lead to unnecessary risk-taking? Should our future in space be privately or publicly funded, and - if private - how do we balance commercial gain against sharing advances of potential benefit to all?
schedule.title: "For All Mankind…"?

schedule.desc: Neurodivergent authors and readers approach the art of fiction in different ways from neurotypical people. Stories may be a way to understand and process the world. For neurodivergent authors, traditional advice on how to write fiction may actually be harmful or counterproductive. In this panel, a group of neurodivergent authors and readers will discuss both how they process fiction written by others and how they write their own stories.
schedule.title: Neurodivergent Approaches to Stories

schedule.desc: There are many issues surrounding AI-generated art. The algorithms often draw on copyright material without permission, the outputs are frequently biased or stereotyped, and the issue of who owns the final artwork is yet to be resolved. If in the future anyone with access to a computer can create images in seconds that would take a skilled professional many hours of work, how will this affect artists' income?
schedule.title: AI and Art - Do Androids Dream of Besting Picasso?

schedule.desc: H. G. Wells’ Time Machine was published in 1895. Since then time travel stories have proliferated. Some time travel stories are simply ways to travel into the past but many others work to interrogate history, play with theories of time or engage in chronotopical structural experimentation. With so many examples, what makes one stand out? Which tropes and tales are our favourites?
schedule.title: "You Gotta Go Back, Marty!" Time travel in Sci-Fi

schedule.desc: Playing in fantastical game worlds often sparks our imagination. Learn more about how game systems like Magic: The Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons and more can generate ideas for fantasy writers.
schedule.title: Games as Inspiration

schedule.desc: In 2007 the International Space Station suffered a computer failure. NASA reported that “drops of humidity and mold were discovered” on the malfunctioning components. Subsequent studies found many microorganisms that survive inside and even outside the station. This talk will introduce the space station's microbiome, the challenges it poses to our aspirations to travel through space, and some of the surprising ways that science is fighting back.
schedule.title: Fighting Fungi in Space

schedule.desc: For young LGBTQIA+ people who grew up under the shadow of AIDS, Section 28, and media invested in the trope of "Bury Your Gays", it was hard to imagine what happy old age would even look like. But this is changing. How do the stories that queer authors are writing today make space for queer triumph? How do writing these utopias have the potential to change the world we live in? And how do we use science fiction to fight back against the current cultural and political pressures on trans people?
schedule.title: Queer Triumph and Utopias in Fiction

schedule.desc: Alternate histories have been a genre staple since L. Sprague de Camp sent Martin Padway back to 535CE, with writers and historians looking the trousers of time firmly in the split to see what the different legs might have been. But are they too reliant on the Great Man theory of history? Could history have been different, or is this the only possibility? And who is writing great alternate history today?
schedule.title: The Trouser Legs of Time

schedule.desc: How pirates have been depicted on screen has changed across the decades with several modern TV shows (One Piece, Black Sails, Our Flag Means Death) pushing the traditional piratical role in new directions. Our panellists will discuss what has influenced the portrayal of pirates on screen and what directions they would like to see in the future.
schedule.title: Black Sails and Deathly Flags: Pirates of the 2020s

schedule.desc: 1984, The Parable of the Sower, and Robin Hobb's Assassin series were all recently adaptated into graphic novels. What does the new medium bring to our favourite stories, and how does it change them? What adaptations have impressed us, and what should be next?
schedule.title: Adapting Science Fiction Books into Comics

schedule.desc: Plushies of the world (and their owners) – assemble! This is the meetup for all plushie crafters and owners, and for the plushies themselves. Tell us story behind your fluffy stuffed companion. All sizes and shapes welcome!
schedule.title: Plushies and Mascots Meetup

schedule.desc: Gathering around the table to tell stories is a powerful experience - powerful enough to fuel new innovations in storytelling and even therapy. Actual play pioneers Cat Blackard and Doug Banks (The Call of Cthulhu Mystery Program) take you down the rabbit hole of Surprise RPGs and The Omniverse Method. Their experimental roleplay techniques pull players and audiences into the game like never before, opening hearts and minds and offering bold new storytelling opportunities that blur the lines between fiction and reality. They're joined by interactive narrative scholar and game designer Dr. Theresa Jean Tanenbaum and game master Jessica Mudd to share stories, findings, and advice for bringing your games to life.
schedule.title: Surprise RPGs: Interactive Storytelling on the Bleeding Edge Or… How a Back to the Future RPG Changed My Life

schedule.desc: From Iain M. Banks' Culture-running Minds to Aliette de Bodard's mindships traversing the Xuya universe, through Anne McCaffrey's Ship Who Sang, Ann Leckie's many-bodied ships of the Raadch, and of course HAL 9000, the idea of intelligent starships pervades science fiction. But what is so attractive about a starship that not only steers, but thinks for, itself? And which authors have written the idea most interestingly?
schedule.title: Big Smart Objects: Sentient starships in SF Fiction

schedule.desc: At a time when media and political attention on trans issues has intensified, this roundtable panel turns backward – to imagined future genders past. Each of the three panel contributions investigates how expanded possibilities of gender were envisioned in a key SF work of the late twentieth century. What ideas of gender transformation and complexity were possible at this time, when transgender studies was just emerging and the study of science fiction was gradually gaining scholarly recognition? And what might such visions have to offer contemporary debates on transgender futures?
schedule.title: Transgender Retrofuturisms

schedule.desc: Zardoz was John Boorman's weird 1974 science fiction film, with the tagline "Beyond 1984, Beyond 2001, Beyond Love, Beyond Death. In it Sean Connery strides across a post-apocalyptic landscape in one of cinema's more bizarre costumes. Something of a flop on initial release, it has developed a cult following since then. Looking back on it now, is Zardoz a heroic failure, an under-appreciated gem, or something else entirely?
schedule.title: Zardoz 50 Years On

schedule.desc: Join our panellists as they explore humour in writing: how to do it, where it can flop, and why it's so hard to sell.
schedule.title: Being Funny: Humour in Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror (ONLINE)

schedule.desc: A celebration of one of the most lauded science fiction television shows in recent years. What is it that makes this show so special, and what, if anything, compares?
schedule.title: The Expanse: The Greatest SF Television Series of the 21st Century!

schedule.desc:
Faith and the divine have played a huge role in fantasy, from Terry Pratchett's Small Gods to N. K. Jemisin's Inheritance Trilogy and Silvia Moreno-Garcia's Gods of Jade and Shadow. This panel will discuss the presentations and representations of the divine in fantasy, the ways writers put faith on the page, and the role of gods in story.

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Gods and Faith in Fantasy (Online)

schedule.desc: In 1896 Georges Méliès created Le Manoir du Diable, sometimes known in English as The Haunted Castle or The House of the Devil. Widely believed to be the first horror movie, the three-minute film has cauldrons, animated skeletons, ghosts, transforming bats, and, ultimately, an incarnation of the Devil. Since then horror movies have been a staple of the cinema. In 2023 there were 46 films released and more than 75 million tickets sold. But as taboos fade and horrors are defamiliarised, the genre constantly needs to reinvent. How does horror in the 2020s pull from the past and in turn push new frontiers? What are the best and worst in horror movies and TV in this decade?
schedule.title: Horror in the 2020s

schedule.desc: With shows like Supernatural, Lucifer and Good Omens interrogating the fundamentals of lore, we ask - who are the bad guys? Are Angels even good? Who are the real demons? Is God just a bad parent?
schedule.title: Angels, Demons and Modern Tales

schedule.desc: Buffy, Batman and Star Trek, to name but three, each feature at least one legendary episode in which the standard format is replaced with a musical one-off production. Why is this change of pace so consistently popular amongst show fans? How is it that even non-regulars to a given show find this a trending topic so often when that episode drops? Join us for this discussion of these very special episodes!
schedule.title: The Mayhem of the Music Meisters! Musical SFF Episodes on TV

schedule.desc: The Ig Nobel Prizes, and Improbable Research more generally, celebrate "research that makes people LAUGH... then THINK". Put another way, it celebrates the fun of science. In this panel, we will have dramatic readings of scholarly research articles that are new to the people reading them. The audience will then get to ask these 'experts' about the papers they have presented. Hilarity, and then thinking, will ensue.
schedule.title: Dramatic Readings of Improbable Research

schedule.desc: Do you tire of all those aliens invading from our neighbour, Mars? Be they big headed and shouting 'Ack, Ack!', be-tentacled blobs with a dislike of the viruses or sibilant reptiles with the ability to survive freezing, they are always coming here and trying to take over. Come along and help us fight back through the medium of simple engineering, basic crafts, and chocolate.
schedule.title: Mars Attacks

schedule.desc: A welcoming space for nonbinary individuals to come together, share experiences, and celebrate representation and diversity in media, literature, and society.
schedule.title: Nonbinary fans meetup

schedule.desc: Pseudoscience – ideas or practices presented as based on scientific principles that in fact are not – is rampant in the modern world. For example, around 20% of UK adults believe that a person’s star sign influences their personality. Why is this the case? Can we tell the difference between science and pseudoscience? And is science fiction helping or hindering our ability to make this distinction?
schedule.title: The Enduring Appeal of Pseudoscience

schedule.desc: Let's explore the intriguing intersection of sociological science fiction and the political landscape in Poland during the transformative years of 1980-1990, delving into the works of Polish authors within the genre. The discussion will aim to examine how speculative narratives served as a unique lens through which societal changes, political tensions, and ideological shifts were both explored and influenced.
schedule.title: Polish Sociological Science Fiction in the Years 1980-1990

schedule.desc: Fanfic has deep roots in speculative fiction, long preceding Kirk/Spock or AO3 winning a Hugo; and so do retellings and reworkings of myth and fairytale. But what is the line between the two? Is there one? Our panellists will discuss where the line between a reimagining of a story and a fanfic of it lies, and how to distinguish the two – if there is such a distinction!
schedule.title: Fanfic or Re-Imagining?

schedule.desc: As the undeniable effects of climate change become more and more a part of our daily lives, so too are they becoming more present in our speculative fiction. Join SFF authors for a discussion on the various approaches to imagining and navigating future worlds with hotter temperatures, water scarcity, rising sea levels, crop failures, and the movement of climate refugees. How do you balance research and narrative, science and opinion, horror and hope?
schedule.title: The Spectrum of Climate Fiction

schedule.desc: Booktube! Bookstagram! Booktok! The Blogosphere! There are plenty of corners of the internet dedicated to celebrating the books we love, and each medium comes with its own strengths and challenges for a reviewer who wants to have their opinion heard. Let our panel of multifaceted reviewers take you on a tour of reviewing in all its online forms.
schedule.title: Tubes and Grams, Blogs and Toks: Reviewing Across the Internet

schedule.desc: A meetup for fans of the Mary Robinette Kowal's Lady Astronaut series to discuss the novels, characters, themes, and share their enthusiasm for the captivating world created by the author.
schedule.title: Lady Astronaut fans meetup

schedule.desc: The Future Worlds Prize is a writing prize for unpublished writers of colour in fantasy and sci-fi; its most recent winner was Ese Eheriene for her short story "The Suit Sellers of Kowloon". Our panel of former winners is joined by Ben Aaronovitch, one of the prize sponsors, to discuss the impact of the prize.
schedule.title: Space for New Voices - Future Worlds Prize Winners

schedule.desc:
Stereotypes and myths abound around sex work, from the "hookers with a heart of gold" to universally trafficked underage addicts. Fiction, including genre fiction, has often fallen back on those stereotypes but has also been willing to subvert them, treating sex workers as the real, diverse people they are. Our panel considers the ways SFF writers have used sex work in their fiction, what that says about speculative fiction, and the best portrayals of sex work they recommend in SFF.

Part of our Glasgow After Dark series. 18+ only.
schedule.title: The Future of the Oldest Profession: Portrayals of Sex Work in SFF
Grimdark with a Smile.

schedule.desc: Are you enthralled by the latest drama from Westeros in House of the Dragon or do you want to reminisce over the good old days of Game of Thrones? What are your favourite fan theories about the books, and what are your hopes for the future? Join other fans of ASOIAF for discussion and speculation.
schedule.title: Fans of A Song of Ice and Fire Meetup

schedule.desc: How do the rules of genre become adapted into the literal rules of play? This panel discusses the enduring impact of speculative fiction on videogames, boardgames, and TTRPGs. We will look at which genres adapt well into gaming and why, as well as systems and cool mechanics which offer a unique approach to different subgenres.
schedule.title: Genre in Gaming

schedule.desc: Join DM Tanya DePass with players Samantha Béart, Jeremy Cobb, Liv Kennedy and Russell Smith as they are led on a merry goosechase through hell. Will they save themselves or will the rather large, grumpy bird prevail? Join us and find out for some epic level shenaniganry.
schedule.title: Live TTRPG: An Infernal Goosechase from Glasgow to Avernus

schedule.desc:
This evening we bring the live performance by a full Symphony Orchestra!

Following the success of similar concerts at the Worldcons in London in 2014 and Dublin in 2019, the programme for the evening will include musical works inspired by science fiction and fantasy, with a particular focus on games and the music of Scotland.

Come along and experience the intensity of the music as it should be performed - live!
schedule.title: Worldcon Philharmonic Orchestra

schedule.desc:
Science fiction and fantasy have long been seen as the literature of ideas and boundary-pushing. In an age when we are seeing increasing legal challenges to both new and classic fiction that pushes social norms, especially around race and queerness, what is the role of SFF in challenging that? Can SFF continue to push boundaries set by the law, and if so, how?

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Book Bans and Moral Fascism (Online)

schedule.desc: In a world of VR, AR and MR, what does the future of video games look like in 2024? This panel will discuss future trends in video gaming, looking at technological advancements, the gaming industry, careers in gaming and the ever-developing role of AI in design, play and process.
schedule.title: The Future of Video Gaming

schedule.desc: What kinds of worlds can be built and stories be told when magic has rules that can be inferred from strict experimentation vs. when magic is a matter of beauty and taste? Is there overlap? The principles of perspective in representational art derive from mathematics, the principles of colour theory derive from optics, and the principles of colour creation derive from chemistry. Yet in our world there is often a hard divide between what is considered art and science. What could the division between art and science, or challenges to that division, mean for fictional magical systems?
schedule.title: Magic as Art vs Magic as Science

schedule.desc:
We'll be sharing songs and music until late. Come join our Filk Circle! We'll be starting with sharing classic filks from around the world.

Additional space for smaller circles is available in Jura and Barra.
schedule.title: Open Filk - Friday Classics

schedule.desc: If an alien picked you up in their tractor beam tonight, how would you react? Would you go peacefully, would you fight, would you eat their food? The panel goes into the nitty-gritty of what would happen if humans were actually abducted.
schedule.title: How Humans Would Really Behave if They were Abducted by Aliens

schedule.desc: Take Me to Your Reader is a podcast dedicated to science fiction movies adapted from books and short stories.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Take Me To Your Reader

schedule.desc:
James Tiptree Jr:  CIA official, international traveller, environmentalist, 'ineluctably masculine' writer of science fiction... …And, in 1976, ‘outed’ as Alice B Sheldon, a 61-year-old woman from Virginia. An award-winning SF-writer, born from a jar of English Marmalade; what happens when your secret’s out, but it’s only the signature that’s changed?

Contains reference to suicide and abortion. Suitable for 14+.

“Tiptree… is a fascinating biography… eloquently written, raising questions about gender, fulfilment, subterfuge and love.” Fringereview

"Engaging, affective and intimate" **** Broadway Baby

"Nuanced portrayal of a conflicted and complex woman" Best Actress Nominee – Buxton Fringe 2024 www.jennyrowe.co.uk/headpictures-productions.html
schedule.title: Tiptree: No One Else’s Damn Secret But My Own

schedule.desc:
Originating in fanfiction before making its way into more mainstream SFF, the premise of the Omegaverse is that a dominance hierarchy exists in humans that divides them into dominant Alphas, neutral Betas and submissive Omegas. There is also a focus on queer narratives. What are the key tropes of the genre? Why is it so popular?
 
Part of our Glasgow After Dark series. 18+ only.
schedule.title: Alpha/Beta/Omega: The Knotty Issue of the Omegaverse

schedule.desc: In the 20th century, it was possible to live on a writer’s income. Today, as the midlist disappears, most writers depend on a day job or a partner's income to make ends meet. How has this economic reality shaped the experience of navigating the industry? Does it close doors to writers from less advantaged backgrounds? What might it mean for the future of the industry?
schedule.title: Can Writing Pay the Bills in the Twenty-First Century?

schedule.desc: An event where fan fiction enthusiasts where they can share their works aloud in a supportive and creative atmosphere, fostering a community of storytelling enthusiasts.
schedule.title: Fan Fic Open Mic Night

schedule.desc: We all know that everything was invented by Scots, and that means Glasgow has more than its fair share of things that look like steampunk fantasies but which actually existed. Hear about tunnels and gasless dirigibles and some really bizarre ferries. Oh, and a monorail. Of course.
schedule.title: Steamin' Agin - Glasgow's Real Steampunk Revisited

schedule.desc: Whether you reside in Africa or are part of the diaspora, come along and meet other Worldcon members of African descent. All self-identified fans of African descent are invited to attend this meetup to mix, mingle, and get to know each other (we ask members who are not people of colour and of African descent to respect this space by not attending).
schedule.title: People of African Ancestry Meetup

schedule.desc:
Bring your bodies and hit the dance floor as DJ (and Hugo nominee!) John Scalzi spins absolutely all the biggest dance tunes from every era of pop music.

From the Bee Gees to Depeche Mode to Beyoncé and Chappell Roan, you'll dance til you drop... and then you'll dance some more!
schedule.title: The Dance Party at the End of the Universe

schedule.desc:
Death is the ultimate destination. Or is it? Characters in some books seem to pass into and out of death as if it had a revolving door, and in others they are killed off with the casualness of throwing out the recycling. Our panel discusses what emotional impact death has in fiction, and their favourite examples of it used well... or subverted completely, as well as reader reactions to character deaths, from outrage to literal disbelief.

Note that this is a virtual panel. We are also running a separate in person version.
schedule.title: Death, Where's Thy Sting? (Online Version)

schedule.desc:
Whether constitutional, absolute or symbolic, monarchical systems continue to fascinate readers and writers of fantasy fiction. Whether cruel tyrants or royals in exile, benevolent queens or warmongering empresses, it seems that more fantasies have monarchies than don’t. Our panellists will discuss the lure of royalty, some of their favourite examples of fantasy monarchs, good or bad, and why monarchy has had such a powerful hold on fantasy fiction.

Note that this is a virtual panel. We are also running a separate in person version.
schedule.title: "I Would Not Be a Queen for All the World": The Lure of Monarchy (Online)
Stroll with the Stars - Saturday, The Kelvingrove Park

schedule.desc: Topology is a branch of mathematics concerning shape. With it we can describe the properties of an object that stay the same if it is stretched, shrunk, or bent. Surprisingly, ideas from topology can be used to study the "shape" of data. This talk will introduce key ideas of topological data analysis and present its applications, from the structures of city streets to the coverage of key resources and the webs of drugged up spiders.
schedule.title: Topological Data Analysis

schedule.desc:
1. Through a Future Darkly: How Science Fiction Futures Colour the Way We View the Present - Jo Anderton
2. Han Born in 1986 - Taeyeon Song
3. The Sounds of Futures Past: Speculative Sound Design - Drake Andersen
schedule.title: Futures in Creative Practice

schedule.desc: Space technologies continue to be integrated seamlessly into our lives - global telecommunications, Earth imaging and satellite navigation services. This talk will explore a range of emerging technologies which could enable new space services including swarms of 'smart dust' devices to monitor the space environment, in-orbit fabrication of large space structures, ultra-lightweight orbiting reflectors to illuminate terrestrial solar power farms at night, and near Earth asteroids as a resource to reduce the scale of future space ventures.
schedule.title: Micro-to-Macro: Space Technologies at Extremes of Length-scale

schedule.desc: Delve into a ‘ginspirational’ look at how gin is produced in Scotland in 2024. Craig from Pixel Spirits Distillery & Spirit School in the West Highlands of Scotland will be taking you through the process of how his craft distillery produces award winning gin and the botanicals used in making the official Glasgow 2024 Worldcon Gin.
schedule.title: Gin Making in the Highlands: Creating the Glasgow 2024 Gin

schedule.desc:
The Glasgow School of Art has produced significant research into this event, including the production of a meticulously researched photo-real, 3D model of over 100 buildings and structures that comprised the Exhibition, three video interviews, recollections of visitors, use by schoolchildren, and immersive experiences in game engines and VR. We will showcase this research and, crucially, demonstrate the need to reassess narratives of the Exhibition from a post-colonial perspective. Whilst earlier research focused on architectural achievements, we are now using mixed-methodologies, including narrative co-design, to highlight the (previously-erased) voices of marginalised peoples and investigate polyvocal narratives about Glasgow's heritage.

Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.
schedule.title: Decolonising Narratives of the British Empire Exhibition of 1938

schedule.desc: This panel delves into how African mythology, folklore, and traditions shape fantastical worlds, creating narratives that challenge and expand the genre's boundaries. Join our authors as they explore the incorporation of African languages, spiritual beliefs, and historical elements into fantasy, highlighting both authenticity and creative reimagining. We will discuss representation, cultural appreciation, the growing impact of African-inspired fantasy on a global scale, and the magic and majesty of African heritage in fantasy storytelling.
schedule.title: African Cultural Influences in Fantasy

schedule.desc: The costumes for alien characters have evolved significantly over the last six decades. From the pointy-eared Vulcans of The Original Series Star Trek to the fabric-faced Cybermen from 1966 Doctor Who, this panel will discuss an overview of alien costume development over the last 60 years of television and how the changes impact the stories told.
schedule.title: Costuming Aliens Over Time

schedule.desc: We invite all individuals who identify themselves as asexual to this meetup (the asexual spectrum, abbreviated as acespec, refers to sexual orientations that are asexual or are closely related to asexuality).
schedule.title: Ace Spectrum Meetup

schedule.desc: Analog games have experienced a renaissance in recent years. But how far have they come? Join us for a look at the evolution of analog games, their mechanics and themes, and popularity.
schedule.title: Tabletop Games: Then and Now

schedule.desc: Many countries are currently facing a serious shortage of people trained in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). The panel discusses the reasons why this is so. There is plenty of anecdotal evidence of astronauts, scientists and engineers being influenced to take up their careers by reading and watching science fiction. Can our genre be used to help address the STEM crisis?
schedule.title: Science Fiction as a Tool to Increase STEM Uptake?

schedule.desc:
Main Business Meeting. Substantive debate on motions to amend the WSFS Constitution including the rules pertaining to the Hugo Awards and Worldcon
Site Selection.

There will be a 45-minute lunch break each day from 12:15 to 13:00. A pre-ordered, pre-packaged lunch for £10 will be available from The Village Hotel. Orders may be placed between 9:15 to 10:15 each day and then picked up during the lunch break.
10-minute ergo/bio breaks will be planned at 11:00 and 14:00. The exact time of the break will be dependent on where we are in the business, but breaks should occur within 10 minutes of the planned time.
schedule.title: WSFS Business Meeting - Saturday

schedule.desc: Whether it's as part of the story or to support their writing process, shared with their fans or kept strictly private, many writers create concept art for their own work. Our panellists share how and why their art complements their writing.
schedule.title: Writers Who Illuminate

schedule.desc: The works of Arthur C. Clarke, Robert Heinlein, Isaac Asimov and others have shaped the genre we love to read today. But some of stories from science fiction's past have aged badly and do not entirely resonate with today's readers. Our panellists will explore how readers could and should approach stories that might now be considered problematic.
schedule.title: Of Its Time: Reading Classic SFF

schedule.desc: Since Sputnik we have launched thousands of rockets and satellites into orbit. Some have re-entered our atmosphere at the end of their life, burning up in the process, but many were abandoned circling the Earth. Some collide to create more debris, or becoming hazards to other space traffic, with potentially disastrous consequences for the future of space exploration. This talk from a scientist with the UK Space Agency's Sustainability Team discusses space junk and what we are doing about it
schedule.title: Sustainable Space Exploration

schedule.desc: Latin lies at the roots of many modern European languages. Despite no longer being spoken, it still finds its way extensively into fantasy and science fiction for catergorising spells, aliens, and everything in between. Learn some of the basics of this dead language with Hugo finallist Emily Tesh in this session for ages 8-13.
schedule.title: Beginner's Latin

schedule.desc: Astronauts, cosmonauts, taikonauts... whichever space programme they flew with, we wanted to honour those brave beings who led the way into space and those who gave their lives in the attempt. Help us gather them together by searching them out in obvious and well-hidden locations around the convention spaces in the Crowne Plaza hotel. There's a prize for whomsoever finds the most! Pick up your entry form from the Info Desk from 10:00 on Saturday morning. Good luck and happy hunting!
schedule.title: Lost Espaciers Scavenger Hunt

schedule.desc: In recent years, fictional witchcraft has seen a large resurgence, both in online communities and in contemporary horror. How does this interact with the rise of real practitioners? Who are some of the great new witches of speculative fiction? What is it about the idea of witchcraft that appeals in these times of uncertainty, as queer/trans rights are being rolled back and abortion access denied?
schedule.title: The Return of the Witch to A Hostile World

schedule.desc: With so many comics available, what should you try next? Our panel of comic book experts will interview audience volunteers and recommend what else they might enjoy.
schedule.title: Comic Book Sommelier

schedule.desc: It used to be that if you wanted to resurrect a character, you had to turn back time. Now, you just bring over a doppelganger from the nearest parallel universe. Is this innovative or lazy? Why is this happening all of a sudden? What does it mean for narrative conventions when all bets are off?
schedule.title: Is the Multiverse the New Time Travel?

schedule.desc: A craft-focused meetup for LGBTQIA+ individuals and allies to come together, share skills, create art, and build community in a welcoming and inclusive environment.
schedule.title: LGBTQIA+ Crafternoon meetup

schedule.desc:
In 1507 alchemist John Damian flew from the ramparts of Stirling Castle to demonstrate the efficacy of flight to King James IV. He plummeted to earth and broke his thigh bone. We might not know of this momentous failure were it not for the seething envy of poet William Dunbar. When an enemy's ignominious defeat is not sufficient humiliation, the truly vengeful turns to poetry. Dunbar glories in Giovanni Damiano's failure to launch, but recording his crash landing is not sufficient to exorcise the revulsion he feels at the alchemist's unnatural magic--nor is it sufficient to dispel his apparent favour with the king, who remains fascinated with the modern science of alchemy. Unlike John Leslie's more measured account in A Historie of Scotland, Dunbar portrays Damian's flight as not only a failure, but as the logical end of a swindler and possibly even a murderer--and one of the 'sonis of Sathanis seid'. Dunbar sees the birds who attack him as 'Sanct Martynis fowle' representing nature as an aspect of the divine. The poet, claiming also to be divinely inspired, must take their part against the 'deviant con artist.'


Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.
schedule.title: Scotland’s First Flight: 1507

schedule.desc:
Being built on an old dock, much of Glasgow's real steampunk exists within easy walking distance of the SEC. Join Feòrag on a stroll to look at what remains. Meet at the east entrance to the SEC.
This item has limited spaces, please sign up at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: The Real Steampunk around the SEC: A Guided Walk

schedule.desc: Join our panel of authors and entomophiles as they discuss the appeal of the insect world and their favourite examples of bugs in science fiction. From insect specters and wasp artists in Nnedi Okorafor's Akata Witch and the highly advanced spider civilization of Adrian Tchaikovsky's Children of Time to the swarms of invading insects in Steph Swainston's The Year of Our War and the hive-minded insectoids of Justina Robson's Natural History, creepy crawlies have long held a fascination for writers of speculative fiction.
schedule.title: The Many Legs of SF: Creepy Crawlies in Space

schedule.desc: Young adulthood is a time of discovery, of new experiences, and of important first times—especially when it comes to gender and sexuality. Our panel looks at how YA books can reflect and represent a young person's exploration of their identity both accurately and respectfully. What unique ways of doing so are provided by fantasy and science fiction worlds and tropes?
schedule.title: Gender and Sexuality in YA Fiction

schedule.desc: Jack Kirby once famously said "Comics will break your heart." But comics and a shared love of comics can play many positive roles in people's lives, as therapy, as community, and as a means of creative exploration. Join us as our panellists share the love they've found in loving comics.
schedule.title: Comics Can Save Your Life

schedule.desc:
From great monuments commemorating rich merchants and powerful statesmen in the Necropolis in Glasgow and Greyfriars in Edinburgh, to humble memorials celebrating the lives of ordinary folk elsewhere, a story can be read from Scotland's greatest heritage asset ̶ her three thousand graveyards. schedule.desc:
France's dominance in western social dance continued into the early nineteenth century with the advent of the quadrille, a multi-part dance in square formation that is ancestral to both Irish set dancing and American square dancing of the present day. Two treatises published in Edinburgh and one Scottish manuscript provide the earliest and most detailed English-language information on the basic techniques, range of variations, and later evolution of the steps of the French quadrille. Alexander Strathy's Elements of the Art of Dancing (Edinburgh, 1822) and the anonymous Scottish manuscript Contre Danses à Paris (1818) are well-known to dance historians for their detailed descriptions of early quadrille style. More obscure is Madame Suinglé's Petits Secrets in Dancing (Edinburgh, 1848), which documents the transition in movement style from the elaborate ballet-like technique of the early nineteenth century to the gliding walk of dancers of later in the century. This paper will provide a non-technical review of the contents of these three works and explore their particular connections with France as well as their significance to the modern study of social dance evolution.

Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.
schedule.title: The Dance from France: the importance of Scottish sources in the study of early nineteenth century French quadrille technique

schedule.desc:
Robert Ferguson's treatment of Scotland's colonial policies drove him to a Jacobite defence of the governments and rights of Native Americans. Ferguson was a Scottish Minister and Radical Whig who converted to Jacobitism. He joined the ranks of Whiggish Jacobites calling for a Stuart restoration along classically liberal, Lockean lines. In 1699 he published A Just and Modest Vindication of the Scots Design, for the Having Established a Colony at Darien. This book seeks to substantiate the Scottish colonial title to Darien by sketching a theological framework of native rights. Ferguson applied his principles of contract theory, limited government, natural property rights, etc. to Amerindians. He even advocated rebellion against colonial powers. Sir William Keith, governor of Pennsylvania, and a former Jacobite utilized the Vindication as he crafted his 1730 Cherokee Treaty which influenced the 1732 Carolina-Creek treaty and the Yamacraw/Creek treaties of James Oglethorpe, another Jacobite, from 1733 to 1743. Ferguson's Whiggish Jacobite principles informed a Jacobite approach to Native American relations for over a decade. This paper argues that the existence of this Jacobite defence of indigenous rights offers an alternative trajectory of British Empire in the Americas under a Stuart restoration. There is also an alligator involved.

Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.
schedule.title: Jacobites, Amerindians, Liberals, and an Alligator

The image of the "herring lassie" is an enduring one in Scottish identity. Old photographs and paintings of fishwives and fish gutters, grinning in front of rows of barrels or looking forlornly out to sea, remain popular with tourists who visit the Scottish coast. But who were these women who worked hard gutting herring for the largest fishing industry in Europe? From the mid-19th to mid-20th centuries, thousands of women followed the herring shoals around Britain, Ireland and beyond to gut freshly landed fish and pack them into barrels. They faced harsh working conditions with a resilient spirit.

In this talk, Meg Hyland will use the words of the women's work songs to illuminate lives full of hard work, blood, fish guts, tears and, above all, laughter. The women sang while working, at dances hosted in their small wooden huts, and while striking for higher wages. They sang in Scottish Gaelic, English and Scots, learning from each other and sharing music across ethnic and national lines. Listen to archival recordings and learn how herring gutters used music to keep their spirits up in one of the toughest jobs for women in all of Scotland's history.

Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.

However, there were suffragist societies and suffragette activism across the length and breadth of Scotland. Some of these built on previous campaigning such as the fight against chattel slavery and the temperance movement. Protests & Suffragettes, a creative project led by a team of artists, activists, and local historians has spent nearly 10 years working to recover and re-voice the histories of women activists in Scotland.
During 2020/21, we conducted archival research and worked with academics and librarians to recover the history of the suffrage movement in Scotland and the women involved in it. From this we created a trump card game and an accompanying education pack, which we gifted to 100 schools across every region of Scotland. I will cover some of the key women, stories and events that we found. As Adele Patrick of Glasgow Women’s Library once inspiringly asked... "How many Scottish suffragettes can you name?"

schedule.desc:
The pursuit of accusations of witchcraft made against six women and one man in the village of Corstorphine near Edinburgh in 1649 can usefully open up the history of witch hunting in Scotland between 1563 and 1736. Among the thousands of victims, these seven cases may be small in number - five people died, and two others were released after a spell of imprisonment - but the vividly detailed records in the local church minute book tell a story typical of innumerable others. Accused and accusers were ordinary inhabitants, engaged in a confrontational procedure that casts great light on both everyday life in early modern Scotland and the beliefs that prompted conflict and the loss of several thousand lives. Though typical, this microhistory is a challenge to some of the stereotypes that still tend to dominate histories of witch hunting in this period.

Presented as part of the History of Scotland track.
schedule.title: A Case of Witch Hunting in Scotland: Corstorphoine 1649

schedule.desc:
Take a break from the SEC to see the gorgeous Glasgow University campus, and then join us for an afternoon of lightning talks showcasing the full range of research on fantasy being conducted at the University of Glasgow from around fifteen different researchers affiliated with the Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic.
The talks will be split into two sessions (14:00 - 15:15 and 15:45-17:00) with time for questions and for meeting Centre members in breaks between and after the talks.
schedule.title: Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic Research Showcase (Session 2)

schedule.desc: Join our plethora of poets for an hour of spectacular speculative poetry.
schedule.title: Speculative Poetry Jam

schedule.desc: The dictionary describes hopepunk as a subgenre of speculative fiction and art that shows optimism, gentleness, kindness, and collaboration to be effective weapons in the fight to create a better future. But does it have its roots in dystopian or utopian fiction?
schedule.title: Hopepunk: Dystopia or Utopia?

schedule.desc: Three Black Halflings is a podcast by Jasper William Cartwright, Olivia Kennedy (but everybody calls her Liv), and Jeremy Cobb: three nerdy friends with strong opinions and even stronger Charisma scores. Join them in their quest to explore diversity in the incredible worlds of D&D and pop culture while doling out DM tips, thought-provoking conversations, a band of guests and good times!
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Three Black Halflings

schedule.desc: Did you know that you've probably already got everything you need to extract DNA in your own kitchen? Get hands-on with St Andrews University Biologist V. Anne Smith who will guide you through extracting DNA from fruit using standard household items. You can even take some DNA home! Recommended age 7+. Adults of under-11s must stay for this workshop.
schedule.title: Extracting DNA with Household Supplies

schedule.desc: Let's delve into the contrasts, let's delve into culture and explore how we cultivate SFF within our own communities. Meet some of the local fandoms and discuss how are we involved in nurturing SFF in their own unique contexts.
schedule.title: Exploring SFF Fandom Across the Globe

schedule.desc: Who are the best animal companions in science fiction and fantasy books, and what makes them so? The Doctor’s K9 is an insufferable know it all; Nanny Ogg’s Greebo is a smelly vicious claw-ball but he’s a softy really; Geralt from Rivia's Roach, seems to be an interchabgeable horse; Data’s Spot is there to remind us that not all people are humans; Nibbler from Futureama. All these are superb pets. But why? What do we want to take into the future or fantasy with us, and what (or who) would be a terrible idea?
schedule.title: You Never Walk Alone: The Best Animal Companions in SFF

schedule.desc:
"Plenty old, not much new., something borrowed. nothing blue"

Mike Whitaker runs through a collection of his and other people's filk and filk-adjacent songs with help from an as yet unknown cast of extras.
schedule.title: Filk Concert: Mike Whitaker

schedule.desc: Our panellists discuss the legacy of Apollo, dive into the current Artemis missions, and consider future goals. How much of a setback is the decision to postpone the Artemis III lunar landing until late 2026? When might we expect to establish a permanent lunar colony? Could the moon be the source of the first profitable extra-terrestrial commodities?
schedule.title: Back to the Moon

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s Glasgow 2024 feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organisers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we may otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Saturday

schedule.desc: Osamu Tezuka is considered to be the Father of anime. So.... where are all the Mothers? From Yoshiko Nishitani to Rumiko Takahashi to CLAMP, women have been paving the way in anime and manga for decades. In this panel we will discuss those trailblazers and many, many more.
schedule.title: Not Just Osamu Tezuka: the Women Who Shaped Anime and Manga

schedule.desc: What are the best practices for writing historical fantasy?  Are there differences between 'historically inspired' and 'historical'? When can sticking too close to 'history' undermine you, and when does anacrhonism wreck your world? And is ther attraction the joy of detail and worldbuilding, or something else? Tips, where to start, and what to avoid.
schedule.title: Writing Historical Fantasy

schedule.desc: Come celebrate new and upcoming releases from NewCon Press! Featured is Ken MacLeod with his first short story collection for 18 years, A Jura for Julia, and its illustrator Fangorn. We will also be celebrating Ian Watson and his first novel in two decades, New Adventures of a Chinese Time Machine; G.W. Dexter's new Birdwatching at the End of the World, a debut genre novel from a critically acclaimed author with three mainstream novels; and Cherith Baldry's collection of new and previously published Arthurian stories chronicling the life of Sir Kay titled The Last Knight of Camelot.
schedule.title: NewCon Press Book Launch

schedule.desc:
In this interactive workshop, we share tips and techniques for reading your writing to an audience. You can then practice your reading performance and microphone work with us.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Reading Aloud for Writers

schedule.desc:
1. Dictionary Corner/Words of the Future - Catherine Sangster
2. The Future of Therolinguistics: Listening to Animals in the Anthropocene - Theodora Goss
3. Ursula K. Le Guin and the Red Book of Cannon Beach - Michael Everson
schedule.title: Linguistic Futures

schedule.desc: Light has mechanical properties including energy and momentum and through these can heat, push, pull and even twist matter. This talk will present and discuss some of the paradoxes and other subtleties that arise in studying such processes. These include whether a radiating atom feels a friction force (in apparent conflict with relativity) and does the momentum of light increase or decrease when it enters a piece of glass (it seems to do both!). Finally, can light sort chiral molecules that differ from each other only by reflection?
schedule.title: Optical Forces: Some Fundamentals and Some Surprises

schedule.desc: Glasgow Worldcons are not without their traditions: each of the previous ones have had a show written and performed by Reductio Ad Absurdum. In 1995 it was their loving demolition of Dune (or The Sand Of Music); in 2005 it was Lucas Back In Anger, their smash-and-grab on all things Star Wars, which was nominated for a Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation (Short Form) despite enraging Star Wars fans by reducing the second trilogy to a 12 minute ABBA karaoke with cardboard costumes. In 2024 their offering is a unique take on the Oscar-winning sensation, Everything, Everywhere, All At Once that becomes Nothing, Nowhere, Never Again. Reductio is basically Ian Sorensen and Phil Raines plus whoever else they can blackmail into performing. This year they have suckered Geoff Ryman, Emjay Ameringen and Julia Daly into joining them in the madness. It promises to be an amazing, hilarious romp through the alternate universes, time travel and the joys of growing old disgracefully. The multiverse will never be quite the same again!
schedule.title: Nothing, Nowhere, Never Again

schedule.desc: Gleaming spaceships crossing a black expanse are not the only future in science fiction: from Lavie Tidhar to Aliya Whiteley, authors are imagining the future, and it looks... weird. The panel will discuss the strange futures of the present; their literary heritage, their real inspirations, and why they're appearing so much now.
schedule.title: Weirding the Future

schedule.desc: Join us to celebrate the final countdown to Gollancz’s 100th anniversary with some of our most beloved veteran bestsellers and most exciting trail-blazing debuts.
schedule.title: Gollancz Turns 100!

schedule.desc: The latest developments on the impact of Generative AI and Large Language Models in the book industry is discussed in every field of the creative industries. What are the effects of it on writing?
schedule.title: Generative AI and Large Language Models in the Book Industry (Online)

schedule.desc: What makes the melted clocks of surrealism attract fantastists and the imagined worlds of fantasy attract surrealists? Our panel will discuss the crossover between the artistic movement and literary genre and their favourite examples of surreal fantasy. From China Miéville's Last Days of New Paris to Helen Oyeyemi's Parasol Against The Axe, surrealism is having a moment in fantasy, but the links between the two also go back decades.
schedule.title: Surrealism in Fantasy

schedule.desc: Past fan fund delegates discuss how their fandom trip enhanced and perhaps even permanently altered the way they interact with the worldwide fandom community.
schedule.title: How Fan Fund Trips Shaped the Lives of Past Delegates

schedule.desc: Kieron Gillen runs a live game of DIE RPG with a panel of special guests! Comic fans and RPG fans will enjoy this explosion of nerdy fun. Audience participation encouraged.
schedule.title: DIE RPG

schedule.desc: The panel discusses current efforts to detect life beyond Earth and considers what it might look like. Will it be carbon-based? Will it have DNA? Will it resemble Earth's extremophiles? Or will it be so exotic that we may not even recognise it? What can we expect to find, where will we find it, and how will the nature of the host planet and star have influenced the way life has developed there?
schedule.title: It's Life, Jim, but Not as We Know It

schedule.desc:
Learn to do ropes, 4-strand "round" braids, classic (3-strand) French and Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand) braids, as well as a crown braid (technically a horizontal modified (3-strand) French braid) and other advanced ideas like 5 and 7-strand fingering techniques. you can also learn shapes like hearts, spirals and a pull-up-weave. All will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the audience. BYO-brush, or use one provided.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.

Note that the Crafting Workshops area is at the back of Hall 4 by the food trucks.
schedule.title: Renaissance & Fancy Hair Braids Workshop

schedule.desc: Whether you call them bande dessinées, historietas, manga, manhua or comics, stories told with sequential art have a long history and a global appeal. Regional traditions can influence each other through publishing styles and ideas, and in this panel we'll take a tour through the shared history and culture of comics.
schedule.title: A World Tour Through Comics

schedule.desc: Help build a cardboard city, pristine and beautiful... Let's hope for the sake of the inhabitants that there's no Godzilla Stomp scheduled later in the day to destroy it all. Open to all ages.
schedule.title: Pre-apocalypse Town Building

schedule.desc: Writing about trauma can sometimes be necessary to tell a particular story in both fiction and non-fiction. What choices can writers make when dealing with these difficult topics, and why do they make them? What does and doesn't work? The conversation will also look at works that have dealt with trauma with various degrees of success and their impact.
schedule.title: Incorporating Trauma into Your Fiction Writing (Online)

schedule.desc: The world is full of folktales, but only a few are well known, thanks to Disney films and popular retellings. But what about those that haven't been adapted? A group of storytellers and folklorists will share their favourite lesser known folktales and myths from around the world, from origin myths to apocalypses.
schedule.title: Tales Not Told by Disney

schedule.desc: A meetup for all those who write in languages other than English.  Meet writers from different backgrounds and share experiences around the struggle to publish, reach audiences, and succeed in a primarily English-centric field.
schedule.title: Beyond English: Meetup for Writers of Other Languages

schedule.desc: Are you part of the Taos Toolbox cohort, or would you like to know more about workshops like Clarion, etc? Then this is the meetup for you!
schedule.title: Taos and Other Workshops Meetup

schedule.desc: Space is a great void, and spaceships are tiny points of light within that. From Adam Obeyanji's Braking Day, Rivers Solomons' An Unkindness of Ghosts, and Ken MacLeod’s Learning the World, generation ships are civilisations packed into these enclosed spaces, but we also see much smaller crews, such as Becky Chambers' Wayfarers, travelling through the void. What kinds of stories do these escape-less vessels lend themselves to? What narrative possibilities are opened up by the closing of physical possibilities? And which books use these constraints best?
schedule.title: Locked in Space

schedule.desc:
People experiencing homelessness regularly appear in genre fiction. All too often those portrayals fall back on tired and sometimes dangerous stereotypes which don't acknowledge the individual as a fully rounded person with hopes, aspirations, likes and dislikes. At a time when more and more people are homeless, and we have a wider definition of what homelessness is, it is important we consider how we write stories to enable them to see themselves in our fiction, rather than just appearing as corpses and victims to move the narrative along. The panel, some of whom have themselves been homeless, will discuss these portrayals, the fiction that gets it right, and how we can write complex and nuanced stories of homelessness without falling back on stereotype, cliche and misunderstandings.
Note that the terminology around this emotive topic is constantly evolving. During the discussion the participants will be talking about their own lived experiences and will use the language they feel most comfortable and familiar with.
Note that the terminology around this emotive topic is constantly evolving. During the discussion the participants will be talking about their own lived experiences and will use the language they feel most comfortable and familiar with.
schedule.title: Homelessness in Genre Fiction

schedule.desc: If the future is indigenous, what forms might it take? How do indigenous writers draw from their diverse traditions, languages, myths, music, and art to challenge colonial storytelling? What concerns are shared across indigenous futurisms, and how do they diverge? This panel brings different imaginations of indigenous futures into conversation, emphasizing diversity while opening the possibility for building bridges between communities.
schedule.title: Indigenous Futurisms in Conversation

schedule.desc: Dragons are a pillar of fantasy fiction, but within dragon lore and literature, there is an infinite variety of draconic personality and motivation. From the non-speaking but intelligent power symbols of Game of Thrones to the egotistical aloofness of Robin Hobb's creations, this panel will explore the ways in which dragons have been utilised in fantastical storytelling.
schedule.title: The Purpose of Dragons

schedule.desc: "Before the Dawn" started as a single song. Gradually it evolved into a vast shared world with many of the early British filk community contributing their own characters and stories. An abridged version was presented at Loncon. In this panel, some of the original songwriters will talk about the song cycle and about the early days of filk music in the UK.
schedule.title: Before the Dawn: A History of Early British Filk Music
Just Add Monsters: Horror-fying Your Genre

schedule.desc: We all know that children are our future and that giving them a good education is essential. This panel looks at how technology is being applied in education, both in and out of school, and discusses future developments in a world of growing technological possibilities.
