schedule.title: An Apple for the Robot? The Future of Educational Technology

schedule.desc: Ancient Egypt with Aliens! It's been 30 years since the Stargate movie launched a franchise on to the world. Our panellists discuss the influence of the film and the franchise and how it may have impacted the wider SFF landscape.
schedule.title: 30th Anniversary of Stargate

schedule.desc: CAMP is like art, we know it when we see it, and Science Fiction and Fantasy are filled with moments of utter camp, both accidental and purposeful. This panel will examine definitions of CAMP, why it appeals, and discuss favourite camp moments and characters (Ming the Merciless, Skeletor, Profion, etc.) as well as ways CAMP can be applied by writers/creators in their own works.
schedule.title: Carry On Outta Space! The Over the Top and Beyond the Stars galaxy of CAMP in Science Fiction and Fantasy

schedule.desc: With the huge rise of fantasy fiction focused on romance in recent years, why are we not seeing an equivalent rise in romance-focused science fiction? Are fantasy and romance just more compatible as genres? Do SF and fantasy readers have different levels of interest in romance? Is it just that SF romance doesn't have a catchy portmanteau term that makes marketing easy? Or are we just overlooking the work of Ann Leckie, Lois McMaster Bujold, Catherine Asaro and many others, all of whom have written Romance in Space! This panel will discuss the relationship between SF and romance past, present, and future, including recommendations of existing work that may have been overlooked, and brainstorming of that portmanteau (sci-mance? rom-ience? we'll keep working on it...)
schedule.title: Why Only Romantasy?

schedule.desc:
In shows such as Ghost River Theatre's Tomorrow's Child to the West End's Back to The Future and War of The Worlds, solid audio design is essential to a memorable theatrical production. This workshop / talk looks at the ins and outs of integrating sound design into your own writing.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Sound Design for Your Own Writing

schedule.desc: What is it about the combination of spies and the just-about-fantastical that keeps us coming back? From the psychedelic trip that is The Prisoner to the laser battles of Moonraker to the denial of physics in the Fast and Furious films, what is it that appeals about the splicing of spies and the near-impossible? Who are our favourite players in the farther-fetched Great Game?
schedule.title: Your Mission, Should You Choose to Accept It - Spy-Fi

schedule.desc:
Join us for an exceptional evening to celebrate the Winners of the Nommo Awards 2024 for the Best in African Speculative Fiction presented by some of the most exciting African writers; Tendai Huchu, Wole Talabi, Oghenechovwe Donald Ekpeki, Nnedi Okorafor and sponsor of our awards Tom Ilube.  The awards recognise the best in speculative fiction by Africans in four categories: The Ilube Award for Best Speculative Fiction Novel, and the Nommo Awards for Novella, Short Story and Graphic Novel.
 
The Nommo Awards now in its 7th edition are literary awards organised by The African Speculative Fiction Society (ASFS), a membership organization of African writers, editors, comic and graphic artists, and filmmakers in the in the fields of speculative fiction such as  science fiction, fantasy, stories of magic and traditional belief, alternative histories, horror, philosophical fiction and strange stuff that might not fit in anywhere else. Taking its name from Dogon cosmology, the Nommos are creatures who take a variety of forms, including appearing on land as fish, walking on their tails. This year’s finalists celebrate writers from Nigeria, South Africa, Ghana, Senegal, Tanzania, and Sierra Leone.
 
Thank you to Dublin 2019 - An Irish Worldcon, Glasgow 2024, A Worldcon for Our Futures, and the British Science Fiction Association (BSFA) for their financial support.
schedule.title: Nommo Awards

schedule.desc:
1. Resurrected Love: The Future of Death and Digitisation of Affect from Neuromancer (1984) to The Wandering Earth II (2023) - Yidan Hu
2. Digital Necromancy: Ethical Implications of Virtual Life After Death - Ava Kelly
schedule.title: Digital Afterlives

schedule.desc: From gestation pods to magical contraceptives, speculative fiction has a wide range of responses to human reproduction, some more informed than others. Our panel will discuss the ways in which speculative fiction imagines alternative ideas of reproduction and responds to real reproductive challenges, as well as offering examples of their favourite and most innovative speculative reproductive technologies.
schedule.title: Clones and Birthing Pods: Reproduction in SFF

schedule.desc: We invite our fan funds delegates to a friendly competition to test the extent of their knowledge about science fiction and fantasy, as well as their general knowledge about fandom and Worldcons.
schedule.title: Jeopardy! with TAFF and GUFF Delegates

schedule.desc: Join Mad Elf for an active, fun game featuring space facts, science fiction trivia, and collaboration. Guide your space probe (i.e. a blindfolded team-mate) to the appropriate celestial body (i.e. a balloon) using only vigorous audio-band transmissions (i.e. shouting)!
schedule.title: Finding Uranus

schedule.desc: In a society that is becoming ever more urban and reliant on technology, the sinister and increasingly alien nature of folk horror's rural setting and ancient traditions could explain the resurgence in its popularity in recent times. Often dealing with themes of isolation, folklore, paganism and the dark aspects of nature, folk horror provides rich soil to grow a sense of fear and foreboding. The panel will discuss what makes a novel folk horror and some of their favourite elements and examples of the genre.
schedule.title: It Takes a Village: Rural Superstition and Sacrifice in Folk Horror

schedule.desc: Whether you're an aspiring podcaster wanting to meet a new co-host, or you have three hundred episodes under your belt already, come along to our meetup session to chat to your fellow podcasters, exchange tech tips, and discuss your favourite feeds.
schedule.title: Podcast Meetup

schedule.desc:
Fandom is a family, and speculative fiction is full of found families, from quest groups to spaceship crews. We will talk about the attraction of found families, the pitfalls of writing them, and the best examples of found families in fiction... as well as those we'd love to be adopted into.

Note that this is a virtual panel. We are also running a separate in person version.
schedule.title: Blood is Thicker than Water: Found Family in SFF (Online Version)

schedule.desc: John McDaid is a singer-songwriter who explores big ideas and sf tropes with three chords and a sense of wonder. The New York Times called him "a mischievous guitarist and vocalist with a gift for the inimitable phrase," and Cory Doctorow praised his "superb, funny, weird and unexpected poetry."
schedule.title: Online Filk concert - John McDaid

schedule.desc: In this panel we will explore key topics and trends in contemporary Polish SFF. We will also make the case for stories and authors that deserve more recognition outside Poland.
schedule.title: Contemporary Trends in Polish Science Fiction and Fantasy

schedule.desc: A child-friendly filk circle - all welcome to come and listen or join in!
schedule.title: Filk for Kids

schedule.desc: Before the late 1940s, science fiction and fantasy books and magazines had been released by general purpose publishers. But after the end of the Second World War, a new breed of publisher emerged, dedicated to the production of genre literature and founded by people who were themselves fans. Some of what they brought out was new work, some of it collections of material that had previously appeared in magazines, but either way they played an important role in making SFF available, often in beautifully packaged editions.
schedule.title: The Post-War Birth of Specialty SFF Publishers

schedule.desc: Beautiful books, timeless storytelling. Join Flame Tree for a gathering of our wonderful authors, including launches by Allen Stroud, Francesco Verso, with book signings by Shona Kinsella, Anna Smith Spark, Marie O'Regan, Paul Kane, Rachel Fikes and more. See our WorldCon24 Special Print Edition Newsletter (New Mythologies in Space) and learn about our approach to myth and fiction through many different series.
schedule.title: Book Launch: Flame Tree Press

schedule.desc: Live Action Roleplaying (LARPing) can seem a little daunting from the outside! Do you want to get involved in LARP communities but are unsure where to start? This panel is an introduction to the LARP scene, with tips on what to expect, how to get involved, and how to find the games and player communities for you!
schedule.title: Introduction to LARP

schedule.desc: A meetup for the Doctor Who fans at Worldcon.
schedule.title: Doctor Who Fans Meetup

schedule.desc: Recent super hero movies have seriously underperformed at the box office. Is this a sign of superhero fatigue, or is it just that the films are not good? The panellists talk about the evolution of the superhero film from early Christopher Reeve's Superman through to 2024's box office dud Madame Web.
schedule.title: Are We Really Tired of Superhero Movies?

people.name: The History of the Twentieth Century

schedule.desc: It's 40 years since failed academics Venkman, Stantz and Spengler coopted Winston Zeddmore into a chaotic adventure with ghosts. This panel discusses how the Ghostbusters franchise has influenced pop culture - from theme songs to cartoon spinoffs to the modern films. Following on from these recent films, how is the franchise evolving in the 21st century?
schedule.title: 40th Anniversary of Ghostbusters

schedule.desc: Too often games involve the normalising of colonial mindsets through the exploration of "unknown lands" and conquest of Indigenous peoples. This panel will discuss ways games can make us rethink representations of race and colonialism as well as examining what decolonising mechanisms look like.
schedule.title: Decolonising Games
The Immersive Possibilities of Horror Audio

schedule.desc: Connect with fellow enthusiasts to celebrate the beloved works of an esteemed fantasy author Robin Hobb, diving into intricate worlds and unforgettable characters crafted with unparalleled skill and depth.
schedule.title: Fans of Robin Hobb Meetup

schedule.desc: Brain-machine interface (BMI) technology promises to help cure debilitating illnesses, allow magnification of human abilities, and perhaps even create the semblance of telepathy.  Sponsored by, and featuring experts from, the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE), this panel will discuss what is possible today and consider how future developments in BMI technology could transform the ways we live and work.
schedule.title: Your Future Thoughts May (Not) Be Your Own

schedule.desc: The Retro Hugo Awards, a tradition where Worldcons retrospectively awarded prizes for years prior to the establishment of the Hugo Awards, have had both avid supporters and vocal critics. The last two Worldcons eligible to grant Retro Hugos opted not to do so, and Glasgow is following suit. Does this signify the demise of the Retro Hugos? And if so, is this necessarily detrimental?
schedule.title: The Conclusion of the Retro Hugo Era

schedule.desc: Self-publishing has been on the rise for a while. When done properly it's a steady (or wild!) source of income. Careers have been made through this method, shifting perspectives on what is the 'right' way to get your stories in front of readers. Our panel discuss their experiences.
schedule.title: How the Rise of Self-publishing Is Changing the SFF Landscape

schedule.desc: Steven Universe is a show for kids which ultimately deals with some pretty adult themes. The panel discusses how such things as grief, queerness, unrequited love and PTSD are framed through and for kids. What does the show have to say about these feelings, why do kids need to know about them, and how can we (even as adults) learn from it?
schedule.title: What’s The Use of Feeling Blue? Grief, Queer Trauma and Growing Up in Steven Universe

schedule.desc:
BG3 is hailed as a narrative masterpiece, especially around the characters and relationships. Let's take a focused look at how relationships can play out, the agency of the Origin characters (and our Tav's!) as well as how the game deals with polyamory, past traumas and how that affects the way you interact with your party. Note: this panel will cover sexual traumas, abuse as presented by the game and in character backstories.

Please note there will be Challenge 25 checks on your ID in accordance with Scottish law because this is an 18+ panel.
schedule.title: Love, Sex, Agency & Intimacy in Baldur's Gate 3

schedule.desc: The Scottish Falsetto Sock Puppet Theatre have been performing comedy shows at the Edinburgh Fringe, and at comedy clubs, theatres, nationally and internationally since 2007. They have also appeared at the British Eastercon. Their dozen (to date) best selling and award winning shows include Shakespeare, Superheroes, last year's Eurovision Sock Contest, and their latest, Post Office Scandal The Musical. This is a show you do not want to miss!
schedule.title: Scottish Falsetto Sock Puppet Theatre

schedule.desc:
The Glasgow 2024 Masquerade is where we will celebrate costumes inspired by science fiction and fantasy. Costuming has been a feature of Worldcon since the very first in 1939, where Morojo (Myrtle R Douglas) and Forrest J Ackerman wore "futuristicostumes", designed and made by Morojo and inspired by the film Things to Come.

The Masquerade MC will be long time master costumer Kevin Roche.

Half-time entertainment will be provided by Sassafrass singing group, performing original a cappella folk music, mostly with fantasy, mythology and science fiction themes!

Whatever your level of experience in creating a costume, this is your opportunity to share your imagination and creative skills with an appreciative audience. All Worldcon members are welcome to participate, either by producing and entering costumes of your own or in groups, or by joining the audience to watch the show.

Whether you want to participate, or offer suggestions or ideas, get in touch via Masquerade@glasgow2024.org For full details of the rules and how to register, see the website here. The Masquerade desk will be open in Hall 4 on Thursday and Friday 10am-6pm, and Saturday 10am-12 noon. Masquerade participants must check in at the desk as soon as possible to receive information packets and release forms and to submit documentation and audio recordings, etc. New registrations will be accepted on-site until 12:00 noon on Saturday.
schedule.title: Glasgow 2024 Masquerade

schedule.desc: As the RPG and tabletop gaming hobby grows, we need to know how to create a warm, inviting, and safe space for new (and experienced) players. Come learn some best practices on creating a positive gaming environment for all.
schedule.title: How to Make Your Table More Inclusive

schedule.desc: In life and in literature, we want to protect children and adolescents from pain as long as possible, but we know it's just a question of time as, whether we like it or not, loneliness, grief, longing, and other difficult emotions are a part of life. This panel aims to examine how children's and YA literature handles such complicated topics and how favourite works can soothe, console, and inspire hope in readers of all ages.
schedule.title: Loneliness and Grief in Children’s and YA Fiction

schedule.desc: A meetup dedicated to fans of Terry Pratchett's Discworld series, where enthusiasts gather to discuss beloved characters, humorous plots, and the profound themes woven throughout Pratchett's iconic fantasy world.
schedule.title: Terry Pratchett's Discworld Fans meetup

schedule.desc:
Sex isn't only for humans. Whether it is hook-ups with a hamadryad or a relationship with a reptilian, monsters have long had a sexual charge for some people, as expressed in romance fiction, art, and more. Our panel will discuss the attraction of the inhuman, the logistics of monstrous hook-ups, and their favourite examples of doing the monster smash on the page.
 
Part of our Glasgow After Dark series. 18+ only.
Please note there will be Challenge 25 checks on your ID in accordance with Scottish law because this is an 18+ panel.
schedule.title: We Did the Monster Smash

schedule.desc: Your chance to bid for some of the beautiful, bizarre, rare and/or remarkable items created and donated to support the fan funds (see catalogue for advance details). The funds exist to bring fans together and strengthen connections across SF fandom worldwide, and the fundraising aims to be fannish, fantastic, and fun.
schedule.title: Fan Funds Auction

schedule.desc:
Few places are as magical as a library. From the mysterious underground library in Erin Morgenstern's The Starless Sea to the shadowy machinations of The Invisible Library created by Genevieve Cogman, libraries are far more than shelves of books and their fierce guardians. Why are readers and writers endlessly drawn to these repositories of the written word? And what does the library of the future look like?  
 
Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: All They're Stacked Up to Be: Libraries in SFF (Online)

schedule.desc: Chemistry perhaps has a lower profile in SFF than biology and physics, but the science and its history is a rich source of material for writers. Some stories using chemistry are noteworthy for their scientific accuracy. Others (featuring mysterious materials or unusual chemical reactions) require considerable suspension of belief. This presentation will explore the credible and outlandish ways in which SF writers have used chemistry.
schedule.title: Chemistry in SF: Cavorite, Coaxium and Other Fictions

schedule.desc:
In this non-AI generative class, Tara Campbell will explore three ways of unlocking new stories: gleaning horror from unfinished business, crafting narratives from common expressions, and using deliberate paradoxes to create new ways of looking at the world.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: A Little Strange Can Go a Long Way: Generating New Stories

schedule.desc: There has been a surge in self-published e-books written (largely) by ChatGPT whilst some magazine editors report being swamped by AI-generated stories. For now, these are easily identifiable and generally of poor quality. However, will a time come when AI-generated fiction is indistinguishable from human-generated stories and of a standard people might actually want to read? Should we accept that this is inevitable or resist the rise of AI fiction? And how do we resist?
schedule.title: AI and Creative Writing - Do Androids Dream of Winning a Hugo?

schedule.desc: We are always trying to depict the alien, but how far do you have to go to be truly out of this world? When you can't draw from a model, how do you create a believable fantasy creature or technological object? Are there software tools that can help? What artistic techniques help convince the viewer you were there? What in the natural order can you change? Are there rules you should never break?
schedule.title: Designing Things That Don't Exist

schedule.desc: Science fiction is at its imaginative best when it takes a big idea and extrapolates the heck out of it. Independence for Scotland has been at core of political debate for 20 years. It's a big idea about the future of a country. How does modern Scottish SF handle the politics of the constitution? Which writers and which stories explore the themes, and where does it take them? Should Scottish SF lead the march to a bright future or warn us about the darkness ahead? Let's find out.
schedule.title: The Politics of Modern Scottish SF

schedule.desc:
We’ll be sharing songs and music until late. Come join our Filk Circle!

Additional space for smaller circles is available in Jura and Barra.
schedule.title: Open Filk - Saturday

schedule.desc: What do we love about fanfic? The ships! Alternate realities! Adult topics! Fix-it fic! X-reader! More adventures! Why does an original procedural have gay pirates as a main trope? And why did action-adventure sci-fi spawn the coffee shop AU? Do we just always want something else? Or ever more of a very good thing? Join this panel as we get our squee on.
schedule.title: Everything We Love (a Little or a Lot) About Fanfiction

schedule.desc:
DJ Scapegoat (Steve Fletcher) will be your DJ this evening, and the theme will be 'Wild Wasteland' with a post-apocalyptic aesthetic!

Steve says: I tend to play pretty open format; I can cover anything from 60s to today, and will spin whatever the crowd on the night vibes to...  Anything from swing to Kpop, metal to dance! I always try to incorporate requests into my sets, so I'll start with some chilled stuff then start upping the energy as folk start wanting to dance!
schedule.title: DJ Scapegoat's Wild Wasteland

schedule.desc: Join your fellow convention members, and perhaps some big names, for a stroll (2 miles/3.2km) along the Clyde to and from Tall Ship Glenlee, which is moored downstream from the SEC, led by Farah Mendlesohn and Mike Scott. The route is wheelchair-accessible, and we will adjust our pace to match the abilities of the slowest walkers. We advise against joining this walk if you are on the programme at 10:00, because we might not be back in time for you to make your way to the Green Room. Note that you won’t be able to board the ship or enter the visitor centre until they open to the public at 11:00. Sign up at the Registration Desk by 18:00 the previous day, and meet at 09:00 outside the Crowne Plaza hotel’s main entrance.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars - Sunday, The Tall Ship

schedule.desc: How far can we push the human body with bioengineering approaches such as cyberpunk implants, 3D printed prosthetics and nanotechnology? Can we use technology as a tool to overcome biological limits and design humans to work better in specific environments? At what point do such modifications question the definition of a human being? The panel discusses the fact, fiction, and ethics of future anatomy.
schedule.title: I Sing the Body Robotic – The Anatomy of Future Bodies

schedule.desc: Gather with fellow fans to delve into the captivating world of Martha Wells' Murderbot Diaries, discussing its beloved characters, thrilling plots, and thought-provoking themes in this engaging meetup.
schedule.title: Murderbot Diaries meetup

schedule.desc:
Join award-winning and internationally bestselling author Kate Forsyth for her most popular workshop 'Plotting & Planning', in which she shares her best tips on learning how to plot a novel.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Creative Writing Workshop from Kate Forsyth

schedule.desc: Book marketing in the current digital landscape has been a game changer for many creatives. Our panellists explore how shifting technology and social media have become a minefield and a gold mine for novelists promoting their work.
schedule.title: Book Marketing in the Digital Age

schedule.desc: Young Adult fantasy and science fiction literature has matured since it started gaining popularity. New works deal with much more complex issues than ever before. Yet one trope, or cliché, seems to endure, despite its common use, especially in YA: the "chosen one." Can today's readers still sympathize with chosen heroes and heroines? Has the time not come to choose something else?
schedule.title: The Chosen Everyone
From Antarctica to Space

schedule.desc: How do you make sure your podcast audio is clean, professional, and appealing to the ears of your listeners? Join us for a deep dive into the audio recording and editing process, showcasing strategies for gracefully integrating music or sound effects into your podcast, integrating multiple audio files into a balanced and unified whole, improving the quality of sub-standard audio, and output formats appropriate to your unique circumstances.
schedule.title: Podcast Production: Audio Recording and Editing

schedule.desc: No one can deny the impact that the Harry Potter series had on children's literature and reading. But it's nearly two decades since the last installment of the series was released, so why are we still using it as a benchmark? Our panel discusses the biggest hits since then along with how they have influenced children's books, and take a look at what might come next.
schedule.title: Beyond the Boy Wizard: What Children's Literature Did Next

schedule.desc: First published in the US in 1924, We by Russian writer Yevgeny Zamyatin is a seminal work of science fiction. It wasn't until 1988 that it was published in Russia - clearly this was a book that the people in power in the Soviet Union wanted erased. Yet it ushered in a new genre - the future dystopia - and in doing so, gave birth to the many dystopian novels and films which have found their way into our popular culture, from directly inspiring George Orwell's 1984 to influencing novels such as Ursula K. Le Guin's The Dispossessed and Kurt Vonnegut's Player Piano.
schedule.title: The Birth of Dystopia: 100 Years of We

schedule.desc: What are the elements of a good cover for a science fiction, fantasy or horror book? Our panel examines the expectations and conventions, the ways these have changed, and the ways in which images can sell or misplace a book.
schedule.title: Book Cover Design for Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror

schedule.desc: In the 1930s and 1940s the Futurians were active in New York, a radical Marxist-influenced group of fans who wanted science fiction to fight fascism and work for the betterment of society. The Futurians included many who would go onto become major authors in their own right. How did they relate to the wider science fiction community? And how did the Futurians navigate the changed political climate of the early Cold War?
schedule.title: The Anti-Fascist Science Fiction Fan Movement of the 1930s and 1940s

schedule.desc: How do you define your creative self, and how do you feel about how the rest of the world defines you and what you do? Every term for a person who creates has some assumptions and historical/cultural baggage attached. Do you feel that you had to "earn" the term you use to define what you do or push back against gatekeeping? Are you a "real" artist? And yes, Imposter Syndrome will be part of this discussion, too.
schedule.title: Artist, Craftsperson, Maker, Crafter – What’s in a Name?

schedule.desc:
Site Selection Business Meeting (Second Main Meeting). At this session, the primary item of business is receiving a report on the outcome of Site Selection for the 2026 Worldcon. After that report, substantive debate will continue on items not resolved in previous sessions.

There will be a 45-minute lunch break each day from 12:15 to 13:00. A pre-ordered, pre-packaged lunch for £10 will be available from The Village Hotel. Orders may be placed between 9:15 to 10:15 each day and then picked up during the lunch break.
10-minute ergo/bio breaks will be planned at 11:00 and 14:00. The exact time of the break will be dependent on where we are in the business, but breaks should occur within 10 minutes of the planned time.
schedule.title: WSFS Business Meeting - Sunday

schedule.desc: From Ben Aaronovitch's magical London to T. L. Huchu's near-future Edinburgh, the settings of urban fantasy novels are often a key element of the story and maybe even the central character. Come along as our panellists share their favourite urban fantasy settings and discuss how to write about a familiar place but not as you know it!
schedule.title: Urban Fantasy Settings

schedule.desc: According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation, by 2050 Earth will be home to over 9 billion people, and we will have to produce around 60% more food than at present to sustain them. However, land degradation is a global concern and agriculture a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. The panel discusses ways in which we might sustainably feed future populations - ideally without resorting to Soylent Green!
schedule.title: Sustainability 3: Feeding the Future

schedule.desc: An opportunity to meet trans SFF authors from different parts of the world.
schedule.title: LGBTQIA+: Trans SFF Author Meetup

schedule.desc: The queer-coded villain has a long and illustrious history, from pre-code horror Cat People to Disney’s drag-queen-inspired Ursula. Who are the greatest icons of queer villainy? What kind of portrayals of queerness have we seen over the years? And how are queer authors today subverting these tropes to create complex new characters?
schedule.title: A History of Queer Villainy

schedule.desc: Narrative audio, whether it is radio plays, podcasts, or audiobooks, makes up a huge part of modern genre fiction. What makes a great audio narrative, and what works are pushing the boundaries of audio fiction? How do you write with your listeners in mind, whether it is a full scripted drama or a book that will be performed?
schedule.title: The Best of Narrative Audio

schedule.desc: Lyndsey Luther stars in this one-person interactive show. Watch her hero set out on their journey, and direct them along the way as she acts out your ideas! Recommended for ages 5-11.
schedule.title: The Hero's Journey

schedule.desc: A presentation of the history of Swedish fandom from the 1950s until today, illustrated by the music the fans made. Includes original recordings.
schedule.title: A Musical History of Swedish Fandom

schedule.desc: Within the science fiction (SF) landscape of China, women have played vital roles from the genre's earliest days. Yet, recognition as a distinct and influential group has only begun to surface in recent years. The discourse around Chinese female SF often reflects the broader Chinese-Anglophone dialogue where Chinese (female) SF is scrutinized as the newcomer against the backdrop of established norms with an expectation to exhibit certain "Chineseness" or "femininity." This roundtable seeks to unravel these complexities without resorting to essentialist views.
schedule.title: Unpacking Chinese Female SF

schedule.desc: In the 80s, truly interactive theatre was the stuff of fiction. Now it seems that the future is here. Are experiences such as The Locksmith's Dream, Crash of The Elysium, Bridge Command and Star Wars Galaxy's Edge modern theatre or something else? What does the future hold? Where is the line between escape rooms, LARP, theatre, and art? Our panel will investigate.
schedule.title: Beyond Dream Park: Interactive Science Fiction and Theatre

schedule.desc: Kieron Gillen presents a cut-down version of his Comics Masterclass.
schedule.title: Comics Masterclass Mastercut

schedule.desc: Alasdair Gray was one of Scotland's greatest speculative writers. His novel Poor Things (recently adapted for the cinema) is often described as a postmodern revision of Frankenstein while his masterpiece Lanark offers a dystopian reimagination of his home city Glasgow. Come along to find out more about how his creative genius continues to inspire new generations of writers.
schedule.title: Alasdair Gray: Writer. Artist. Visionary.

schedule.desc: Alien visits to Earth, whether as invading forces arriving on green streaks from Mars or snapping up singers for intergalactic song contests, have long been a staple of science fiction. Our panel will discuss their favourite extraterrestrial visitors, what brings aliens to Earth, and how writers use these ideas as commentaries on the world.
schedule.title: First Contacts and Third Encounters

schedule.desc: Make and decorate a balloon rocket, then race it along a string. Recommended for ages 4-11. Adults must remain for this workshop.
schedule.title: Balloon Rockets

schedule.desc: Since Great A'tuin first swam into the cosmos in 1983, the Discworld has dominated the fantasy genre. Terry Pratchett has legions of fans and has converted readers to fantasy with satirisations of the genre's excesses, as well as Shakespeare, economics, the very idea of story, and much more. Our group of Discworld fans will talk all things flat, including adaptations, Roundworld meet-ups, and the ongoing influences of Pratchett's titanic literary achievement.
schedule.title: The Legacy of the Discworld

schedule.desc: Or else, you might say - parenting done right. We've invited some of the unconventional parents who will share with you the parenting methods they used to raise a proper geek and, hopefully, future fandom members as well. Some stories may be funny, others quite unexpected!
schedule.title: Look! I Have Raised a Geek!

schedule.desc:
Science fiction and fantasy written by Scots go way back in time, and today many Scottish writers are writing exciting new works to add to the collection. This presentation will look at Scottish SF writers from the past: some you'll know, others who will surprise you, and we'll explore contemporary Scottish SF. Maybe we'll identify some of the themes and ideas that are being taken up by current and future Scottish SF writers.

The presentation will include videos of story readings and live readings (selected from attendees of Glasgow 2024). Participation from the audience will be encouraged to feed in ideas to help us develop SF Caledonia as a showcase for Scottish SF.
schedule.title: SF Caledonia: A Stroll Through Scottish Science Fiction, Past, Present and Future

schedule.desc: Have you ever wondered what goes into writing a filk song? Where do people get their inspiration for the themes and topics, and how do they transform their ideas into finished songs to share with the fannish community? Our filkers share some of their trade secrets.
schedule.title: So You Want to Write a Filk Song

schedule.desc: Do you have or need great science fiction and fantasy related patterns for sewing, knitting, and other crafts? If you have, then come share, and if you need some, then come find out what our panellists have to offer.
schedule.title: SFF Patterns for Crafts

schedule.desc:
1. Eco-futures and Sustainable Fandom: Changing the Narrative in SF/F Fandom - Nicolle Lamerichs
2. Climate Catastrophe in Perpetual Utopia: Exploring Children's Comics and Games, and Actualizing Climate Change in Aquicorn Cove - Grace A. T. Worm
schedule.title: Ecological Futures
Table Talk: Patrick Nielsen Hayden and Teresa Nielsen Hayden

schedule.desc: A panel of writers will share how they incorporate fashion into their written work. What are the techniques used to seamlessly include fashion in SFF writing?
schedule.title: How to Write Fashion into SFF

schedule.desc: For many, science fiction and fantasy is the ultimate act of escapism: the avoidance of reality by imagining exciting but impossible activities. From orcs opening coffee shops to daring space adventurers, this panel discusses what makes the best escapist stories.
schedule.title: Reality Bites: Escapism in SFF

schedule.desc: If you've ever wondered how SF fans come to be very serious Worldcon guests of honour, Claire Brialey and Mark Plummer are still wondering, too. But they invite you to spend an hour reflecting on how they got here from finding fandom in the mid-1980s and whose fault it is really. (Disclaimer: it will not all be very serious.)
schedule.title: SF Fandom: Its Part in Our Downfall

schedule.desc: Panellists discuss the past, present and future of Arabian fiction and how it has influenced fiction globally. We will consider the history of Arabian Fiction, the causes behind its demise, and the rise and future of Arabian Fiction.
schedule.title: 1001 Years Later: Where is Arabian Fiction?

schedule.desc: For conrunners, delivering a high-quality convention is a serious endeavor and involves very hard work. Getting proper rest and resuming regular life afterward is not an easy task. Additionally, all attendees, from regular members to staff and con committee, experience post-con blues that we have to handle before arriving at the next year's edition. Let's discuss our experiences and how we cope with all these challenges.
schedule.title: Con Aftercare, Recovery and Dealing with Aftercon Blues

schedule.desc: Faith and the divine have played a huge role in fantasy, from Terry Pratchett's Small Gods to N. K. Jemisin's Inheritance Trilogy and Silvia Moreno-Garcia's Gods of Jade and Shadow. This panel will discuss the presentations and representations of the divine in fantasy, the ways writers put faith on the page, and the role of gods in story.
schedule.title: Gods and Faith in Fantasy
Diversity in Tabletop RPGs

schedule.desc:
Join conservation scientist and award-winning author Lorraine Wilson in this workshop exploring climate fiction as an act of resistance and empowerment, and developing tools for crafting speculative narratives that speak against the status quo.
Please be mindful when signing up for this workshop. This is a Scottish BPOC Writers' Network event for Black and PoC based in Scotland (or who, pre-COVID, would have normally been resident in Scotland), the UK and Ireland.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Embracing Nature: Liberation Through Climate Fiction

schedule.desc: Economics is the "dismal science", but economic speculative fiction is far from dismal; writers have experimented with all kinds of economic models from social credit to gift exchange, in worlds fantastical or space bound. And that's without thinking about the impact of magic on currency values or space travel on the flow of trade. Our panellists will share their favourite examples of economic systems in SFF, which ideas they think the genre should be doing more with, and even what economics can learn from speculative fiction!
schedule.title: All the World's Books Depend on the Beancounter: Economics in SFF

schedule.desc:
This is not just any map. It will help you identify your strengths and also some of the stereotypes and cultural assumptions you bring with you into the world you build. As a Medieval historian, Gillian Polack will use a Medieval-style world for this workshop, but the skills you learn will apply far more widely. 

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Mapping How to Build a World (Fiction and Gaming)

schedule.desc: It would be wrong to think of post-war science fiction as a boys club with a "No Girls Allowed" sign on the door. Women were active as writers, editors, fans, and artists, key players in the scene even if outnumbered by their male counterparts. Look back with us on the contribution of these often fascinating characters of late 1940s science fiction.
schedule.title: Women of Post-war Science Fiction: Writers, Editors, Fans, Artists.

schedule.desc: Whether constitutional, absolute or symbolic, monarchical systems continue to fascinate readers and writers of fantasy fiction. Whether cruel tyrants or royals in exile, benevolent queens or warmongering empresses, it seems that more fantasies have monarchies than don’t. Our panellists will discuss the lure of royalty, some of their favourite examples of fantasy monarchs, good or bad, and why monarchy has had such a powerful hold on fantasy fiction.
schedule.title: "I Would Not Be a Queen for All the World": The Lure of Monarchy

schedule.desc: We're launching a new award at Glasgow Worldcon in honour of the late great Brian Aldiss's centenary year - 2025. On this panel we discuss Brian's part in the science fiction and fantasy worlds and talk more about the how's and why's of starting the new award and exactly what genres and classes it covers.
schedule.title: The Aldiss Award for World-Building in SF and Fantasy

schedule.desc:
Lucy Locket lost her pocket, Kitty Fisher found it. Have you ever wondered how that could happen? In the eighteenth century, a woman's pocket was essentially a bag tied at her waist. In this workshop, you will hand sew a pocket inspired by the eighteenth century artefact, resulting in an object that is both appealing and useful.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.

​​​​​​​Note that the Crafting Workshops area is at the back of Hall 4 by the food trucks.
schedule.title: Hand Sew an Eighteenth Century Pocket

schedule.desc:
Join Guest of Honour Chris Baker to learn more about his personal artwork, including oil painting, sculpture and printmaking.
Part of a series of presentations by Chris Baker about his artwork.
schedule.title: Chris Baker (Fangorn) Presents His Life as an Artist

schedule.desc: As more and more books are optioned for TV or film, our panellists discuss how best to bring the spirit of the book to the screen. Should you stick closely to what's written or adapt the stories more loosely?
schedule.title: Adapting Books for TV and Film

schedule.desc: How do writers from different backgrounds approach writing fiction in English? What kind of advantages and disadvantages does writing in a second language have, especially in genre fiction?
schedule.title: Worldbuilding in a Language Not Your Own

schedule.desc: Description: Celebrate our newest Fantasy titles, with a drink, readings, Q&A, signing: Lucifer & Son by David Craig, Sooty Feathers book 3 – The living and undead alike continue to fall like autumn leaves as the supernatural war in Glasgow escalates. The Harlequin: The Draper’s Reel by J.A. Mortimore and Penelope Hill – a master trickster foolishly agreed to steal a reel from the drapers’ god. The heist of a lifetime. But his own god is paying far too much attention. Plus Lacuna by Erin Hosfield – You can abandon your past... but your secrets won’t abandon you.
schedule.title: Elsewhen Press Fantasy Book Launch

schedule.desc:
Join Glasgow 2024's own Tiara Queen to make your very own tiara!

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops. Please note that there will be a charge of £15 for the materials for this workshop, payable to the workshop leader.
schedule.title: Make Your Own Tiara with Sara Felix

schedule.desc: Japanese Role Playing Games have developed relatively independently to their western counterpart, evolving their own unique tropes, mechanics, and worldbuilding staples. In this panel we will discuss what makes a JRPG, trace its history, and shed light on some hidden gems of the genre - it's not all just Final Fantasy!
schedule.title: Let's Kill and Dethrone God: the History of JRPGs

schedule.desc: It is inevitable that the world will face another pandemic. But what will it be? Another coronavirus? Zika? Some form of haemorrhagic fever? A new type of influenza? Or so called "Disease X" (the World Health Organisation's term for a currently unknown pathogen or pathogen variant with potential to cause a pandemic)? And where will it come from - nature, a laboratory, or perhaps even from space?
schedule.title: From Whence Cometh the Next Pandemic?

schedule.desc: From short to long, serious to snarky, glowing to excoriating, good written reviews can be as much an art form as the works they are about, and there’s a lot of different ways to go about writing one. Join our panel as they talk about the ingredients that go into a well-written review and the different roles that reviews play in the bookish community.
schedule.title: What are Reviews For? Balancing Critique, Recommendation, Promotion and the Art of Criticism in the written review

schedule.desc:
1. The Queer Art of Failure in Gaming Cultures - Gabriel Elvery and Francis Gene-Rowe
2. Dystopic Queer Futures in Seth Dickinson's Masquerade Series - Rebecca Gault
3. The Waters of Fantasy Canon and Their Futures - Sam Tegtmeyer
schedule.title: Queering Futures

schedule.desc: The history, people and landscape of Scotland have had a considerable influence on science fiction (Gemmell, Martin, MacLeod) and fantasy and folklore (as in the work of our GoH Terri Windling). Some writers who use Scotland know it intimately. Others appear to be locked into the fantasy Scotland of Braveheart. Why is this, and what are the opportunities and pitfalls caused by this phenomena? Are some kinds of Scotland more palatable than others? What would our panel like to see?
schedule.title: Scot-ish: The Influence of Scotland on Fantasy Worldbuilding

schedule.desc: Writers love imagining the consequences of a single change in military fortune or the fate of an individual political figure. Exploring the influence of our greatest authors, artists and composers on history is no less compelling. What alternate realities are possible when we do not lose certain brilliant artists so young? How historically powerful could shifts in cultural tastes be?
schedule.title: The Arts and Alternate History

schedule.desc: Have fun learning and playing a range of group improvisation games enjoyed by budding actors worldwide. Bring your sharpest wits and most expressive face! Recommended for ages 6+.
schedule.title: Improv Theatre Games

schedule.desc: We often acknowledge mythology and folklore as the roots of fantasy fiction for adults, but how much do writers use the other stories we read and heard as children as source material and inspiration? After all, even the publishing industry recognises the value of children's fiction in determining what works for adults - we wouldn't have The Lord of the Rings without the success of The Hobbit. Our panel discusses how childhood favourites have influenced modern fantasy.
schedule.title: How Children's Literature Shaped Fantasy Fiction

schedule.desc: Come and hear Scotland's Black and PoC SFF authors and emerging writers read their work.
schedule.title: We Are Here! Scottish Black and PoC Writers Showcase

schedule.desc: Make light-up cards and more! Learn to craft with LEDs and copper tape. (This workshop is running twice to accomodate more participants.) Recommended for ages 6-15.
schedule.title: Paper Circuit Workshop 2

schedule.desc: In 2022, the Double Asteroid Redirection Test spacecraft deliberately crashed into a small asteroid, Dimorphos. The DART mission investigated a possible technique for moving asteroids, perhaps useful someday for "planetary defense" if a threatening object is ever discovered.  An Italian spacecraft, LICIACube, accompanied DART, snapping pictures of its final moments and the messy plume of its aftermath. This year Europe will send a followup mission to Dimorphos to examine the damage.
schedule.title: NASA's DART: The Spacecraft That Moved an Asteroid

schedule.desc:
A pre-recorded Victorian adventure and superhero story. Mrs Hawking works as a covert agent for women victimized by Victorian society, with the indifferent support of her protégé Mary Stone and nephew Nathaniel. But when two mysterious ladies come to them with a nigh impossible mission, Mrs. Hawking and her assistants must come together as a true team in order to see that justice is done.
Content warning: themes of sexual assault.
schedule.title: Mrs. Hawking: Vivat Regina

schedule.desc: After the masquerade is over, entrants are invited to talk about their costumes, explaining their ideas and techniques. If possible, please bring your costumes and accessories. Signing up is encouraged. Non-masquerade participants are also warmly welcomed.
schedule.title: Post-Masquerade Show and Tell

schedule.desc: In western SF, "robot laws" are about controlling robots while in Japanese SF, "robot laws" are about robot civil rights. Let's consider the central but different places robots have had in both traditions, from Bester, Heinlein and Tezuka through Gundam, Lee and Thompson to Prasad, Cargill, MacLeod, Wells and Concrete Revolution.
schedule.title: Robots in Western and Non-Western SF Traditions

schedule.desc: From H.G. Wells' The Time Machine to This is How You Lose The Time War by Amal-El Mohtar and Max Gladstone, A.G. Riddle's Lost in Time to Audrey Niffenegger's The Time Traveller's Wife, readers and writers are eternally fascinated by the concept of traveling in time. Join our panel as they discuss what makes a successful time travel story and how - or if - the genre keeps inventing itself.
schedule.title: Near, Far, Whenever You Are

schedule.desc:
The Irish Video Game Orchestra (IVGO) is a group of passionate musicians at the forefront of the video game music scene. Established in 2015, the IVGO brings the intricate and powerful scores of video game landscapes to audiences across Ireland and the UK. They performed at the 2019 Worldcon in Dublin and Eurocon in Belfast. They are excited to come to Glasgow.

The IVGO write: Join us at Worldcon as we take you on an immersive journey through beloved video game realms, bringing to life the iconic scores that resonate with many generations of gaming enthusiasts. From the sweeping melodies of The Elder Scrolls to the powerful dynamics of Baldur's Gate 3, the IVGO's performances bridge the gap between the worlds we have traversed on screen and reality.
schedule.title: Irish Video Game Orchestra

schedule.desc:
A combination of cataclysmic events results in the extinction of the human race, leaving behind an AI being programmed to recreate humanity when the time is right, with the complete works of Shakespeare as a guide to the human spirit. Humanity must thrive... but at what cost?

This original sci-fi storytelling show was inspired by Mary Shelley's ‘Frankenstein’, and will leave you wondering who the real monster is.

Originally created in collaboration with the London Science Museum, Quintessence is written and performed by award-winning actor Emily Carding.
schedule.title: Quintessence
Table Talk: Francesca T Barbini - Luna Press Publishing

people.name: Francesca T Barbini - Luna Press Publishing

schedule.desc: Written against the backdrop of the Vietnam War, Ursula K. Le Guin’s 1974 novel The Dispossessed explores the idea of an anarchist utopia and critically interrogates the very concept of utopias. The book went on to win the Hugo, Locus and Nebula Award for Best Novel. Our panellists will delve deeper into the ideas and themes in Le Guin's novel and debate its continued relevance and place in the canon of SF utopias.
schedule.title: An Ambiguous Utopia: 50 Years of Ursula K. Le Guin's The Dispossessed

schedule.desc: When you hear the sound of hooves, it might just be a unicorn, heraldic symbol of Scotland. From its appearances in legends across the world and the tall tales of travellers, as well as in recent fiction, readers and writers are endlessly fascinated by the horse-like beast with its spiralling horn. We will explore the unicorn's history as a symbol of purity, a focus of magical powers, and a metaphor for the destruction of the Earth's wild places.
schedule.title: Unicorns in History, Myth and Fiction

schedule.desc: From the gore of The Walking Dead and the folk horror of Scarenthood to the psychological terrors of The Nice House on the Lake, horror in comics and graphic novels comes in many forms. When the reader controls the pace of the narrative, how do writers and artists balance the seen and the unseen to induce the same thrills and chills as horror films?
schedule.title: Fear Factor: Horror in Comics and Graphic Novels

schedule.desc: Gods and monsters, swords and sorcery, legends and folktales: there's no limit to what can be depicted in comics and graphic novels like Monstress or Saga. What makes this medium particularly suited to igniting the imagination of writers, artists and readers alike?
schedule.title: Exploring the Fantastical through Comics and Graphic Novels

schedule.desc: Join the Bona Books team and a few of our authors in launching I Want That Twink OBLITERATED! An anthology of queer science fiction and fantasy in the pulp style.
schedule.title: Bona Books Launch I WANT THAT TWINK OBLITERATED

schedule.desc: If you're a fan of fountain pens and stationery, come meet your fellow enthusiasts!
schedule.title: Fountain Pen and Stationery Enthusiasts Meetup
Best Cats of SFF

schedule.desc: Magic objects are all well and good, but what happens when you have a sword with its own opinions about the uses to which it's being put? What happens when a key negotiates with a lock? Or your magical objects are magical only because they contain trapped spirits? Haunted houses are often given a certain personality, but can we push that? How can inanimate objects affect a story when they are granted agency?
schedule.title: It's Aliiiive! Sentient Inanimate Objects in Genre Fiction

schedule.desc:
Astronomers have found over 5,000 planets outside our solar system. Many of these “exoplanets” are completely unlike Earth—there are scorching-hot gas giants, planets covered entirely in lava or ocean, and more! Following a presentation on exoplanets from a University of St Andrews researcher, you will have the chance to design your own alien in this fun workshop. Come doodle and imagine and chat about science! This workshop is in conjunction with the Alien Worlds exhibit this summer at the Wardlaw Museum in St Andrews. For ages 8 years to adult. 

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Design Your Own Alien

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s Glasgow 2024 feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organisers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we may otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Sunday

schedule.desc: Fandom returned from the Second World War, with conventions re-emerging and zine production expanding. The fandom of the period was very different to that of our time, but the post-war fans laid down templates that persist to this day. What were the key trends in late 1940s fandom? How interntational was fandom? And how diverse?
schedule.title: Fandom of the Late 1940s

schedule.desc: It's been 31 years! MYST debuted in 1993 and led to a series of games, books, soundtracks, and more! This panel will discuss the history of our favorite puzzle game and look at new developments in the works.
schedule.title: 30 Years of MYST

schedule.desc: Printed progress reports, souvenir books, pocket programs, conbooks, fanzines, and books are common items in the fandom and at fandom conventions. Even though all of them exist in their digital PDF versions (or sometimes in-app versions as well), we still have a deep sentiment for paper itself. Why is this so? What makes us stick with old ways when the future has already arrived?
schedule.title: Why Do We Still Love Paper and Tangible Things?

schedule.desc: Join us as we explore the rich history of fanfic cultures as they developed from zines to online platforms like AO3 and beyond.
schedule.title: The History and Development of Fanfic Cultures

schedule.desc: What do you do when you meet a ghost? Ghosts appear in YA and middle-grade fiction in many ways, often carrying messages or needing help with their unfinished business. Are ghosts still strictly for scary stories, or are their appearances less frightful these days? And what new skills does the modern protagonist have to tackle supernatural phenoma?
schedule.title: Things That Go Bump in the Night

schedule.desc: Gaelic is one of Scotland's oldest languages. But being an old language doesn't mean you can't have new words! Come along to have fun exploring how to bring sci-fi and fantasy words into minority languages, using Gaelic as an example. Recommended for ages 10-15.
schedule.title: How do you say TARDIS in Gaelic?

schedule.desc: Build your own space satellite while giving a new life to some of our convention junk! Or maybe make some aliens to visit it? Or a Nessie of your own? The only limit is the strenght of our glue! Recommended for ages 4-12.
schedule.title: Junk Satellites

schedule.desc: Forget exams. Here villainous teachers, treacherous classmates and other evils stand in the way of graduation. In recent years, there has been a resurgence of Dark Academia books, from R.F. Kuang's award-winning Babel to Olivie Blakes' The Atlas Six series. Why are readers and writers fascinated with this (perceived) dark side of education? And how much do these book reflect and challenge the institutions we all love, and love to hate.
schedule.title: Dark Academia: The Lure of Evil Institutions

schedule.desc: A miscellany of songs old and new, inspired by books, TV, Movies etc, covering a wide range of themes, including Space, SF, Fantasy, History, Alternate History, Murder Mysteries, not to mention life, the universe and everything, plus quirks that catch Valerie’s fancy. All of the above is subject to change, but there might even be a singalong or two……
schedule.title: Filk Concert: Valerie Housden

schedule.desc:
1. Bring Your Shovels: Hauntology in Hungarian New Weird Short Fictions - Andras Fodor
2. The Apocalyptic Poetics of Godzilla Minus One - Takayuki Tatsumi
schedule.title: Monstrous Futures

schedule.desc: 3D printers have become much more capable and affordable. This panel will review the current types of printers, discuss the benefits and trade-offs of each type, and look at the current trends in how 3D printers are likely to continue to advance.
schedule.title: 3D Printing: What's Available, Getting Started, and Current Trends

schedule.desc: A meetup for fans of Iain M. Banks' works to discuss his novels, characters, themes, and share their admiration for his unique contributions to science fiction literature.
schedule.title: Iain M. Banks Fan meetup

schedule.desc: Our panellists discuss the history of science from ancient times to the present day. What were some of the greatest scientific advances? How did they change the way that we think and live? What were some of the greatest scientific misconceptions, and how did those errors challenge science to evolve into the discipline we know today?
schedule.title: Is Science "A History of Corrected Mistakes"?

schedule.desc: Manga and anime have been imported and marketed in different countries in a variety of ways, from the '70s to today. Our panel share fun stories of how they first encountered Japanese animation and comics in their countries.
schedule.title: Manga and Anime from the '70s to Today

schedule.desc: Parasocial relationships (one-way relationships in which fans feel like they "know" a media personality) have always existed. However, with content creation - and especially live streaming - those relationships take on somewhat new twists that many streamers don't expect. This panel of content creators will discuss the unusual, one-and-a-half-sided parasocial relationships that can exist between you and your community, how it can affect you, as well as how our panellists have successfully navigated things.
schedule.title: Parasocial Relationships and You

schedule.desc:
1. Sacred Visions: Apocalyptic Imaginaries and Socio-Political Critique in Netflix's Sacred Games - Sheenjini Ghosh
2. Disorienting Dream as a Way of Knowing: The Exagoge & Beyond - Elizabeth Stell
3. Writing the Future, Rethinking the Past, Changing the Present: Octavia E. Butler's Parable duology and the Book of Revelation - Luise Roessel
schedule.title: Religious Futures

schedule.desc: TJ and Mitchell Burnside-Clapp have been writing and singing filksongs since before they even met, in fact, since before either of them knew what filk was. Between the two of them they have accumulated over 80 years of performance experience, more than a dozen convention GoH spots, five Pegasus Awards for Excellence in Filking, three somewhat musically inclined children, and some amount of what might be called "fame" in unexpected circles. TJ and Mitchell perform songs about space, technology, science fiction, and humor from their own imaginations as well as from their many creative friends, including songs by TJ's filk singing group Technical Difficulties (which features Linda Melnick, Sheila Willis, and Jean Stevenson in its various incarnations). They are delighted to share their eclectic musical stylings with the 2024 Glasgow Worldcon.
schedule.title: Filk Concert: TJ and Mitchell Burnside Clapp

schedule.desc:
Miles Cameron is a renowned historical re-enactor and author, writing SFF under Miles Cameron, and historical fiction as Christian Cameron. He also has a long-running web series, Writing Fighting, where he demonstrates techniques from historical combat to help make it easier to write accurate, exciting fight scenes.

This is an opportunity to experience a live Writing Fighting workshop, to get a feel for how a battle might play out and bring that into your writing. Drawing on a range of cultures and historical masters, as well as different combat situations and weapons, Miles demonstrates the physical realities and pacing of combat techniques to show how to effectively write fights and avoid common pitfalls.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Writing Fighting - Sword Techniques Workshop

schedule.desc: Fairy tales, legends and myths may well be the oldest narrative form, having their roots in the oral traditions of pre-literate human societies more than 100,000 years old. These ancient stories have been retold, reimagined, and subverted by writers for centuries, from Shakespeare to Disney to Anne Sexton. The 21st century has seen the popularity of such retellings explode, along with a new academic interest in its many manifestations. Why? This panel of fairytale experts seeks to answer this question, and many more about the history, meaning and purpose of wonder tales from around the world.
schedule.title: Shapeshifting Stories: Respinning Fairy Tales & Myths

schedule.desc: Join us as we share opportunities for costuming outside of SFF conventions. From the Jane Austen Festival in Bath to the Fringe Festival, and Versailles to the Piazza San Marco, where can you wear your greatest outfits? We will also discuss potential barriers to wearing costumes, looking at topics like safety, cultural appropriation, and what you shouldn't do because it would be in poor taste.
schedule.title: Costume Opportunities and Barriers

schedule.desc: The shorter the fiction, the harder it can get. How do you create compelling worlds in so few words? What are the best practices and approaches?
schedule.title: Flash Fiction: The Art of Storytelling in Under 1,000 Words

schedule.desc: The Bad Girls of SFF used to be Femme Fatales, out to seduce the hero (or sometimes the villain) with their feminine wiles. Bad Girls now raise demons, conquer planets and plot and plan to bring down the world. Whether they're fighting with their words, their wits, or their weapons, these women keep us on our toes and turning the page
schedule.title: Bad Girls of SFF: Villainous Female Characters

schedule.desc: Become a part of the cosmos as a planet, moon or comet! Get to know the bodies in our solar system and recreate it to scale before dancing their motions all together. Recommended for ages 5-13.
schedule.title: The Solar System Ballet

schedule.desc:
In this hands-on tasting experience you'll learn all about the history and crafting of gin. You'll taste a variety of different gins that reflect this history and the ways that gin has been made and appreciated through time. Of course this will include our signature Glasgow 2024 Gin, crafted and distilled in collaboration with Pixel Spirits Distillery & Spirit School. Space is limited and advance sign up is requested, although drop-ins are welcome if space is available.
Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
Please note there will be Challenge 25 checks on your ID in accordance with Scottish law.
schedule.title: Gin Tasting Session #3

schedule.desc: Join us for a space odyssey, from the fantastical to the real! Ken Gordon, the ESA Space Solutions Ambassador for Scotland, will pitch a wild ESA-funded project, then put it under the microscope with analogue astronaut Josh Gribben. Drawing on their simulated moonbase experience, Josh and Ken will explore the hilarious gap between sci-fi dreams and lunar reality. Get ready for laughter, learning, and separating space odyssey from lunar lunacy!
schedule.title: Cosmic Odyssey – Thinking Beyond Earth

people.name: One Small Step for Mankind, one giant leap for business!

schedule.desc: Deb Geisler was an extraordinary conrunner, a science fiction fan, and a well loved friend and mentor to many in our community. She was chair of Noreascon 4, the 2004 World Science Fiction Convention, and volunteered her time, experience, and snark to many other conventions. Please join us for a celebration of the life of Deb's life and contributions to fandom.
schedule.title: Deb Geisler Memorial

schedule.desc: Disabled creators, professionals, and players are invited to hang out and meet others who may share similar experiences. How can we encourage greater attention to issues of representation and the accessibility of play across all levels of the gaming industry?
schedule.title: Disabled Creators in the Gaming Industry Meetup

schedule.desc: What were the tech breakthroughs and inventions that forever changed our fandom? How did the introduction of typewriters and conventional photography allow us to progress with our hobby? How did the introduction of cheap commercial flights enable fans to meet each other? How did the introduction of mobile phones change the game for us, along with the emergence of the Internet? Are VR fandom meets a thing? And what other amazing advancements will enhance our collective fandom experience?
schedule.title: Technology in the Service of Fandom

schedule.desc: The art of the silent movie; the economy of a two minute scene conveying 10  years; a captionless graphic novel page... there are many ways of telling…without telling. This panel discusses the subtle, the silent, the economical and the ingenius within weaving a tale without weighty dialogue.
schedule.title: Storytelling without Words

schedule.desc: Genre cookbooks exist for properties as diverse as Street Fighter and Middle Earth. Some are licenced, some fan productions, and some allude to their properties without ever making such clear references as to be sued. But do they make edible food? Do they add to the world they're spun out of? Our panel discusses the best flavoured recipes, and the best flavour texts, on this table of the genre buffet.
schedule.title: Cooking the Books

schedule.desc: Navigating the publishing world can be challenging and demanding with pressures and expectations from publishers and readers. So how can you cope when health is not always on your side?
schedule.title: Sustaining Relationships in Publishing as a Disabled Author

schedule.desc: Is the wilderness a myth? Indigenous groups say the land weeps without people, people who care for it properly, that is. Yet the myth of the land without people, open for settlement, is a powerful one in Western science fiction. How do writers of the fantastic use wilderness settings? Is the wild a friend or foe? Are wild places their own characters or only mirrors to human strengths and weaknesses? Which writers have challenged ideas of the Empty Space open to physical and cultureal conquest.
schedule.title: The Myth of the Wilderness

schedule.desc:
Come along as Special Guest T.L. Huchu chats about his publishing journey, writing genre and bringing together his Zimbabwean background with his chosen home Scotland. 

Previously published in the adult market (as Tendai Huchu), T.L. Huchu took the urban fantasy scene by storm in 2021 with the publication of "The Library of the Dead",  the first book in the Edinburgh Nights series set in an alternate Edinburgh.

His previous books (The Hairdresser of Harare and The Maestro, The Magistrate and the Mathematician) have been translated into multiple languages and his short fiction has won awards.

Tendai grew up in Zimbabwe but has lived in Edinburgh for most of his adult life.
schedule.title: Special Guest Interview: Tendai Huchu

schedule.desc: Meet the Broads of Broad Universe! The authors of Broad Universe will drop you into their fictional universes with short readings from multiple authors and works. Within the session you will hear a variety of writers in a variety of speculative fiction subgenres, like a variety box of chocolate! Broad Universe is an international organization dedicated to promoting women and traditionally marginalized genders in Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Horror.
schedule.title: Broad Universe Rapid Fire Reading

schedule.desc: Science fiction has often been a mirror of the times in which it is written, and with the current climate situation, it can be hard to avoid to falling into a pit of despair when writing. But the rise of solarpunk, hopepunk and more has given us a different angle to consider. What is the state of the Cli-Fi scene, and what's to come?
schedule.title: Climate Fiction: Despair or Hope? (Online)

schedule.desc: Crafting, making, and cosplay all take equipment and materials. The panel will discuss different approaches to making space in your home for making, from boxes under the bed to dedicated makerspaces in garages and basements. Also, we'll discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using community makerspaces as an alternative.
schedule.title: Making Space for Making

schedule.desc: The announcement of the first direct detection of gravitational waves in 2015 was the result of many decades of experimental effort, stemming from the predictions of Einstein and others almost a century before. People often ask what are gravitational waves, how did we detect them, where is the field going, and why should we care anyway? This talk will try to answer these questions in an accessible manner.
schedule.title: Gravitational Waves – What, How, Where, Why?

schedule.desc: How have dragons changed in their on-screen existence? With the advent of new technology, more "realistic" dragons are possible. What are the panellists favourite dragons? Is it the early Disney Maleficent Dragon or Taro from the 7th Voyage of Sinbad, Haku from Spirited Away or the dragons in Game of Thrones? All dragons are up for discussion and perhaps an epic battle to determine the finest beast!
schedule.title: Here Be Dragons!!

schedule.desc:
There are a lot of costs associated with publishing and self-publishing. Even though a writer might be making money selling books, it can still be hard to break even, let alone to make a profit. In this workshop we will look at how to assess the costs of writing and to take them into account.

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Workshop: I’m Selling Books, but Am I Making Money?

schedule.desc: Occasionally, things don't go as planned. Some might argue they frequently veer off course. Some mishaps are deemed as type two fun while others fall into the category of type three fun (meaning "no fun at all"). We'll consider experiences at conventions run by our panellists, and welcome input from the audience about their own chaotic moments.
schedule.title: S#it, Here We Go...

schedule.desc: Death is the ultimate destination. Or is it? Characters in some books seem to pass into and out of death as if it had a revolving door, and in others they are killed off with the casualness of throwing out the recycling. Our panel discusses what emotional impact death has in fiction, and their favourite examples of it used well... or subverted completely, as well as reader reactions to character deaths, from outrage to literal disbelief.
schedule.title: Death, Where's Thy Sting?

schedule.desc: The divided self reaches back to R. L. Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde and James Hogg's Confessions of a Justified Sinner and forward to Star Trek's Tom Riker and Marvel's Hulk via the work of psychiatrist R. D. Laing. Modern authors to explore it include Christopher Priest,  Lois McMaster Bujold and Matt Ruff who posit it as a trauma response while David Levithan and Lauren McLaughlin used it to explore identity issues. So what makes this trope so attractive? Why do we keep coming back to it, and where are we seeing it done well?
schedule.title: Evil Twins and the Divided Self

schedule.desc: Our panellists will explore how rapidly expanding scientific knowledge has affected science fiction. With technology that could only be dreamt of a few decades ago now routinely available, is there still ample scope for the imagination? Or is truth now stranger than fiction?
schedule.title: Has Science Ruined Science Fiction?

schedule.desc: Participants must work together in teams to save the space leopard and her eggs from being devoured by predators. This will involve shooting the predators with Nerf guns and solving puzzles to win points and save the species.
schedule.title: Save the Space Leopards!

schedule.desc: A meetup for fans of LGBTQIA+ and queer-themed content in various fandoms to come together, discuss their favorite characters, ships, and storylines, and celebrate diverse representation in media and pop culture.
schedule.title: LGBTQIA+ and Queer Fandoms meetup

schedule.desc:
1. Reproductive Futures in Louisa Hall's Reproduction (2023) - Anna McFarlane
2. Repression of and Pressure to Reproduce in Young Adult Science Fiction - Jani Ylönen
schedule.title: Reproductive Futures

schedule.desc:
Released in 1984, Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind is one of Hayao Miyazaki's earliest movies, pre-dating even the Ghibli studio. In this panel we will discuss the reception and censorship of the movie in the West, its various inspirations, and what it has to say about environmentalism, war, and the duties we have to each other and to our planet.
​​​
schedule.title: 40th Anniversary of Nausicaa

schedule.desc: The eye is one of the most complex parts of the body--and one of the most commonly misrepresented in fiction. What is the anatomy of the eye (human or animal), and how does this correspond to vision? How were vision impairments treated historically? What is the emerging technology for vision correction? Dive into the windows of the soul to learn about the very small organ to which there is more than meets the...eye.
schedule.title: The Eye – Vision for the Future

schedule.desc:
Another Castle is the geekiest (mostly) women’s choir in Helsinki, Finland, who draw their inspiration from fantasy, sci-fi, video games, anime, films, etc.

They performed at the 2017 Helsinki and 2019 Dublin Worldcons to great acclaim, and Glasgow 2024 is honoured to host them.
schedule.title: Another Castle

schedule.desc: Have you ever been to a bookshop or library and had a book recommended to you that has changed your life? Been introduced to your new favourite author by a passing suggestion from a librarian or bookseller? Do you want to learn more about the arcane processes behind recommending books you might not even have read? Join us for a discussion of the thought that goes into recommendations on the shop floor and in the library, and some live audience-based recommendations from our expert panel!
schedule.title: Booksellers and Librarians Recommend...

schedule.desc: Selkies make frequent appearances in filk while Nessie has also been known to come up and listen. Scottish myths, legends and folktales are rich fodder for filkers across the world, but what's been overdone, and who or what has yet to star in their own filk song?
schedule.title: Scottish Myths and Legends in Filk

schedule.desc: Post-apocalypse Earth is a staple of science fiction, and the current climate crisis suggests we're rapidly heading in that direction. But is this inevitable? The panel compares climate doomism (the idea that we’re already past the point of being able to do anything about global warming and will probably become extinct) versus a more hopeful, solarpunk-style view of a sustainable post climate apocalypse future.
schedule.title: Sustainability 4: It’s Only the End of the World Again!

people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

schedule.desc: Do you know your MMOs from your NPCs? Do you prefer to Min/Max or Min/Min? Do you love Loot Drops and Level Ups? If you love gaming and want to buff your TBR, then look no further! LitRPGs and Progression Fantasies take the character levelling conventions and language from computer games like World of Warcraft and translate them into fiction. Our panellists will explore the tropes and traits of this SFF subgenre and share some of their favourite examples.
schedule.title: AFK: LitRPG and Progression Fantasy fiction

schedule.desc: The operational lifetime of the International Space Station (ISS) will come to an end in 2030 then, in 2031, it will be deorbited and allowed to crash into a remote part of the South Pacific. The panel discusses what has been achieved by the ISS and what will replace it, comparing the actual experience of sustaining a habitable environment in LEO with depictions in science fiction
schedule.title: Low Earth Orbit Space Stations – What Does the Future Hold?

schedule.desc:
Monsters have been used historically as metaphors to keep women in line. Don't go into the forest; don't stray from the path. They have often also been used to represent and demonise women. Are we seeing a change in monster narratives? Are books today starting to explore how the monstrous might be used to empower women instead?

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Don't Go Into the Forest: Monsters and Feminism (Online)

schedule.desc: Poland has a rich history of awards created to honour its best writers. Some were brought to life by the industry itself while others were created by Polish writers and fans. Some of the awards are still with us while others were discontinued. What were the most important awards of the past? Which of the awards that still exist are the most important for fans and the most likely to boost sales? And what do writers think about the awards?
schedule.title: A History of Polish Literary Awards

schedule.desc: Should we regulate advances in AI development to limit the chance of self-awareness emerging? If we do create self-aware AIs, should we give them free will and teach them the difference between right and wrong (if so, according to whose morality)? Alternatively, if we deny them free will, are we creating a slave race? Free-willed partners or obedient servants - the panel discusses which we should choose and why.
schedule.title: AI and Ethics - Do Androids Dream of Having Free Will?

schedule.desc: Short fiction is great for many reasons: it could be someone's first step into writing or a way to hone writing skills, to be nominated for awards, and even to make money. In this panel, you will hear from authors who know the short stories market and who will share their experiences, tips and how-tos.
schedule.title: How to Write Short Stories That Sell (Online)
