schedule.desc: Consumer technology companies have thrived by making their products simple and intuitive to use, hiding away the complexity of the technology. Meanwhile science fiction portrays scientists and engineers as their 1960s equivalents, not the hyper-specialised team workers of today. Taking as an example the latest version of the Raspberry Pi, the Pi 5, this presentation will delve deep inside the silicon to bring the unbelievable hidden to light.
schedule.title: The Hidden Complexity of Technology: Inside Raspberry Pi 5

schedule.desc:
There once was a girl from Arrakis...

Join our panel of poets as they improvise SFF themed limericks using suggestions from the audience.
schedule.title: SFF Limericks In Real Time

schedule.desc: The third of the Initiative for Interstellar Studies programme items on worldships in fact and fiction features a speculative discussion of daily life onboard the worldship. This will include topics such as governance, education, ethics, morals, religious beliefs, and wealth/resource management, with particular emphasis on the transmission of information and purpose.
schedule.title: Worldships 3: Generational Relations and Socio-Economic Structures

schedule.desc: This roundtable panel examines how science fiction works illuminate transgender experiences of temporality. For gender variant people who experience time as non-linear - as cyclical or twisted, static or stretched - science fiction presents a treasure trove of language and images with which to approach our present moment. The genre’s explorations of time travel, parallel worlds, and apocalyptic scenarios offer invaluable tools for thinking about - and hopefully beyond - the current crises that trans communities face.
schedule.title: Time Loops and Parallel Worlds: Transgender Temporalities

schedule.desc: Creating inclusive conversations that discuss which future we want has never been more important, and science fiction has an important role to play in this. Through short stories, whose world-building has been iterated with scientists, everyone can take a step back and consider plausible scenarios. Using real examples of projects with academia, government and think-tanks, this talk will give an overview of what applied science fiction is and why it has value to SF writers, scientists and society.
schedule.title: Applied Science Fiction: the Who, What, Why and How

schedule.desc: The panel discusses prospects for exploring and eventually settling other bodies in the solar system. How long before we take our first footsteps on Mars? When will we begin mining the asteroids? And how will we adapt as a species to living in so many contrasting environments?
schedule.title: Settling the Solar System: Building a Space Society

schedule.desc: Is Doctor Who actually Scottish? Thus far there have been four Scottish Doctors, from Sylvester McCoy to Ncuti Gatwa, current occupant of the TARDIS. Several Doctor Who stories have been set in Scotland while there are rumours that the TARDIS itself can be seen in central Glasgow. How has the Scottishness of the Doctors influenced the show? And how has the country been reflected in the programme?
schedule.title: Doctor Who and Scotland

schedule.desc: A light-hearted discussion on tech that sometimes performs so poorly it's hard to see the point of it, e.g. the autocorrect function in word processing software that adds spilling errors to all your documents when you're not licking. The panel propose some examples. Bring your own favourites.
schedule.title: Pointless Technology

schedule.desc: A mild-mannered structural engineer by day, Gary stalks the stages and filk rooms of Northeast conventions, singing of space flight, lunar colonies and hyperspace hotels. Come listen and sing along virtually to a few of his instantly-hummable songs.
schedule.title: Online Filk Concert: Gary Ehrlich

schedule.desc: Join Jon Davies of science outreach company ThinkScience for a fun science demonstration lecture, featuring vividly re-enacted personal NDEs (nearly disastrous experiences) and some spectacular clues, all of which relate to various popular and obscure sci-fi movies and stories. Will you guess them all? Includes one thousand nails, a giant hot air balloon and some buckets of water...!
schedule.title: Very Tall Tales from a SF Fan – Science Demonstration Lecture

schedule.desc: Join C.L. McCartney and Trip Galey for this presentation on The Very Queer History of SFF. They'll discuss how hard it is to define what is and is not queer, how its even harder to excavate the potential queer roots of...anything, and then give it a try anyway. Expect queer myth and history from around the world, prominent queer and possibly queer figures in the modern rise of science fiction and fantasy, and a rapid fire blitz through people, works, and genre movements you can explore further yourself! Plus campery.
schedule.title: The Very Queer History of SFF

schedule.desc:
Does the speculative nature of SFF romance and erotica lead to a more fluid imagining of gender and romantic partnerships?

Part of our Glasgow After Dark series. 18+ only.
Please note there will be Challenge 25 checks on your ID in accordance with Scottish law because this is an 18+ panel.
schedule.title: The Possibilities of Gender in SFF Romance and Erotica

Please join your Chair Professor Esther MacCallum-Stewart and several of our Guests of Honour and Special Guests for the most prestigious awards in science fiction and fantasy.

Watch the Hugo Awards ceremony on the big screen in the Lomond Auditorium.

Doors open from 19:30.
schedule.title: 2024 Hugo Awards Ceremony - Overflow Viewing!

schedule.desc: For millennia, humans have played games of one form or another, either on their own or with others, and for a range of purposes. This talk will look at the mathematical analysis and surprisingly rich structure of a variety of games, such as peg solitaire, noughts and crosses, Nim, Go, Sprouts, and others.
schedule.title: The Mathematics of Games

schedule.desc:
We’ll be sharing songs and music until late. Come join our Filk Circle!

Additional space for smaller circles is available in Jura and Barra.
schedule.title: Open Filk - Sunday

schedule.desc:
Just add murder! From crime-solving wizards to undead detectives, the joy of the fantasy, science-fiction and horror genre is its versatility and how well it plays with others, especially crime. Come along as this panel discusses their favourite genre mashups and the ingredients to a criminally good SFFH story.

Note that this is an online panel. We are also running a separate in-person version.
schedule.title: Fantasy Noir and Other SFFH Mashups (Online)

schedule.desc: Isekai (Japanese portal fantasy) has been exploding in popularity with no signs of slowing down, but what makes it so popular? What themes resonate with fans across age ranges and demographics? And most importantly, why does no one in an isekai ever want to go back home?
schedule.title: Help, I Got Reincarnated Into a Worldcon Panel!

schedule.desc:
Whether or not you’ve got the blues after the Hugo results, come enjoy listening and dancing to some late-night blues! 

Blues music and dance are part of African-American culture, evolving from African rhythms and movement styles.  Some quick instruction will be offered to get you started, but creativity and self-expression, solo or with a partner, are encouraged!
schedule.title: Post-Hugo Blues Dance

schedule.desc: Writers often find inspiration outside the familiar, but access to other cultures by those from cultures of power brings with it issues of privilege, exploitation, and challenges from subaltern authors. This panel will discuss appropriation, how it works, and how to avoid it.
schedule.title: Appropriation Versus Inspiration

schedule.desc: Join your fellow convention members, and perhaps some big names, for a gentle stroll (1.3 miles/2km) around Festival Park, across the river from the SEC, led by Farah Mendlesohn and Mike Scott. The route is wheelchair-accessible, and we will adjust our pace to match the abilities of the slowest walkers. Sign up at the Registration Desk by 18:00 the previous day, and meet at 09:00 outside the Crowne Plaza hotel’s main entrance.
schedule.title: Stroll with the Stars - Monday, Festival Park

schedule.desc: Your cat might be a fluffy adorable ball of loveliness, but they are also trying to kill you, from their razor-sharp claws to their tiny teeth and the contents of their bowels. Come along, and find out more!
schedule.title: How Your Cat Is Trying to Kill You

schedule.desc:
We're constantly hearing about the climate emergency, but how many of us fully understand the issues behind it? Climate Fresk (from the French fresque, meaning fresco) is a card game based on scientific evidence published by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. Working in groups, you will explore the causes and consequences of climate change in a fun, interactive way and be empowered to take high-impact climate action. Our workshop will be led by trained Fresk Facilitators from the University of Strathclyde.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: Climate Fresk

schedule.desc: From Mary Shelley's Frankenstein to Martha Wells' Murderbot Diaries, speculative fiction has long been used as a medium to explore philosphical concepts such as free will, the nature of persons and transhumanism. Join this panel as they discuss speculative fiction as a legitimate and versatile avenue for 'doing' philosophy.
schedule.title: Do Philosophers Dream of Electric Sheep?

schedule.desc: The very premise of alternate history is based on an assumption that our own history is the product of random happenstance rather than destiny. Consequently, this subgenre seems particularly well suited to challenge assumptions about colonialism, and existing societal power imbalances. This panel will discuss progressive examples of alternate history, as well as looking at why alternate history sometimes does not reach its potential to be an intersectional and diverse subgenre. The Sidewise Awards For Alternate History will be presented at this panel.
schedule.title: A People's Alternate History

schedule.desc: A space elevator is a free-standing tower that can be used to lift payloads into geosynchronous orbit. The concept has been around for more than 100 years, with one of the best-known SF examples in Clarke's The Fountains of Paradise. A related concept is the skyhook - an orbiting station with a long tether dangling towards the atmosphere to which objects can be attached. The panel discusses these technologies and speculates on when they might become a reality for Earth, the Moon, or Mars.
schedule.title: Going Up - Space Elevators as Highways to the Stars

schedule.desc: Bespoke Shoemaker SunnyJim Morgan takes you on a tour of what's on your feet. Ever wondered what makes an Oxford different from a Derby? How high heels are made? Are elves involved? We'll cover that, as well as some of the history of shoes and shoemaking, the parts of a shoe, some of the different methods of construction, materials used, and a few of the places you can learn more.
schedule.title: Anatomy of a Shoe

schedule.desc:
Discuss a range of fantastic texts with tutors and doctoral students affiliated with the University of Glasgow’s unique MLitt in Fantasy Literature.  The Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic will offer a series of 75-minute small-group seminars, including discussions of early fantastical narratives, canonical authors such as J.R.R. Tolkien and Ursula K. Le Guin, contemporary Fantasy fictions, and fantasies in diverse forms.
The there will be four parallel sessions in this block. Each of the taster slots can accommodate up to 30 people.
You may find the sing up link for this item at the bottom of this page: https://glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/glasgow-university/
schedule.title: Fantasy Master’s Taster Sessions (Session 1)

schedule.desc: When everyone is starting a podcast, how do we make our fandom inclusive? What extra barriers exist for minority podcasters to start, thrive, and grow their podcasts? How do you find a diverse audience and ensure they have a great listening experience, and how do you keep your fandom a welcoming place to be?
schedule.title: Inclusive Podcasting

schedule.desc: A meetup for artists and illustrators seeking a community. The British Fantasy Society is very keen to connect with more artists who may be interested in submitting work.
schedule.title: British Fantasy Society Meetup for Artists and Illustrators Interested in Submitting Work

schedule.desc: Join us for an engaging discussion panel on sustainability and sff fandom, where we'll delve into eco-friendly initiatives within the community and their intersection with themes from speculative fiction. Let's explore how our love for science fiction and fantasy can inspire real-world sustainability efforts together!
schedule.title: Sustainability and SFF Fandom

schedule.desc: Main Business Meeting—Overflow. Any items of business that have not been resolved by the end of Sunday's session will be debated during this overflow session.
schedule.title: WSFS Business Meeting - Monday

schedule.desc: With SFF being one of the biggest markets for TTRPGs and boardgames, what new tabletop games are out there that will appeal to fans of all types? Do any games build on existing franchises and universes in exciting new ways or create entirely new worlds you want more people to get lost in? Let's talk about boardgames, their mechanics and worldbuilding, and take the chance to yell about great new releases and old favourites!
schedule.title: Boardgaming for SFF Fans

schedule.desc: Immerse yourself in the captivating world of steampunk alongside fellow enthusiasts, sharing inspirations, creations, and a deep appreciation for the genre's unique blend of Victorian aesthetics and futuristic innovation. Join us for engaging discussions and a celebration of all things steampunk!
schedule.title: Fans of Steampunk Meetup

schedule.desc: If AI is really going to bring about the end of humankind, how will this happen? Is it going to be a dramatic Skynet/Matrix/War Games kind of thing, a gentle slide into ennui and obsolescence, or will the Internet of Things simply make life unbearable through incessant delivery of the wrong online groceries? Would a sapient AI notice, let alone care, that we're here? The panel put forward potential scenarios and discuss which ones are most probable.
schedule.title: AI and the End Times - Do Androids Dream of Killing Us All?

people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

schedule.desc:
There can't be many people with internet access who haven't heard the name of Studio Ghibli. It's one of the most famous film studios on the planet, producing classics like Spirited Away, Howl's Moving Castle and Princess Mononoke. Both Princess Mononoke and the studio's perennial favourite My Neighbour Totoro have been transformed into stage shows. Concerts of their magical film scores draw huge crowds. But there's a lot more to Studio Ghibli than just movies. Its art is driven by inspiration from Japanese and Western art, by energies from the streets of Japan and by the mystical qualities of its traditions and its wild places.

Helen McCarthy, who wrote the first books in English on anime and on Ghibli's co- founding director Hayao Miyazaki, will take you on a journey through the studio's history and inspiration, with time and space to appreciate selected artworks and a list of sources - books, websites and places to visit - if you want to explore further.
schedule.title: The Art History of Studio Ghibli

schedule.desc: What do you do if you've been a constant costumer, and you find yourself downsizing? Moving? Changing sizes or shape? Come ask costumers your burning questions about how to deal with the inevitable accumulation of costumes. Those who have made the hard choices about what to say goodbye to will share how they did it and how you can avoid your beautiful creations ending up in the landfill.
schedule.title: And Then What? How to Downsize Your Costume Closet

schedule.desc: A presentation by Dr. Penny Hill on behalf of the Embroiderers' Guild. The oldest surviving English embroideries include items from the early 10th century, although the art had been well established long before then. This presentation examines how embroidery in Britain developed from stitching with simple wool and linen threads through to the contemporary use of man-made fibres, chemical dyes, and mixed media techniques.
schedule.title: Distaff to Digital: 1000 Years of Decorative Stitching

schedule.desc: Scotland boasts a rich history of conventions with many being organized in Glasgow. What were the cornerstones of fandom meetings and cons in the past century? Who ran them, and how did they evolve into modern-day fandom events?
schedule.title: A History of Scottish Conventions in Glasgow

schedule.desc: The ocean is full of creatures stranger than science fiction! Learn more about them in this interactive talk, as well as how they can inspire creativity and respect for our planet. Recommended for ages 8-15.
schedule.title: Ocean Oddities

schedule.desc: 2024 sees the 75th anniversary of the publication of 1984 and its entry into the public domain. 'Orwellian' has become an adjective, and ideas from the book have become part of popular culture, from newspeak to Room 101. Our panel talks about the book itself and the myths and misunderstandings that have grown up around it, as well as its legacy and imprint on subsequent dystopian fiction and imagery.
schedule.title: 75th Anniversary of 1984

schedule.desc: A podcast about science fiction and SF fandom from John Coxon, Alison Scott, and Liz Batty.
schedule.title: Live Podcast: Octothorpe

schedule.desc: Curious to know what floor of the convention we're on, or what the consensus is on our favourite shade of blue? Come and join us for our Queue Data Analysis Extravaganza, where we will draw out these and other scientific insights from our queue polls. We will also feature short presentations on similarly serious and important scientific topics from guest speakers.
schedule.title: The Queue Data Analysis Extravaganza

schedule.desc: Hopepunk is a reaction to decades of dystopian, nihilistic fiction, explores how goodness and optimism can be acts of rebellion. We welcome all indviduals who enjoy hopepunk to this meetup.
schedule.title: Fans of Hopepunk meetup

schedule.desc: Let's put our tadpoles together, and discuss the latest installment in the franchise. What parts of D&D did it get right? What could've been done better? And who is the hottest pansexual in Faerûn?
schedule.title: Baldur's Gate 3

schedule.desc: Ensemble casts have become a standard feature of YA fiction, often with each member of the cast having their own point of view chapters. What is the secret to creating a successful ensemble? Are there roles that always need to be filled: the leader, the intellect, the comic relief? Do you still need a single protagonist, or can you let the readers cheer for their favourites?
schedule.title: Assemble Your Squad: Ensembles in YA
String Theory Made Easy

schedule.desc: Fantasy can forge an intimate connection with a sense of place or a wild displacement. Authors such Alan Garner, Jeannette Ng, Alasdair Gray, Nnedi Okorafor, and many others write work that is deeply embedded in the landscape. What does being tied to the land mean for a piece of fiction, and what does consciously undoing that tie allow? Who is embedded in place powerfully, and for whom is it lightly worn... or not there at all?
schedule.title: Finding Story in the Landscape

schedule.desc:
1. Alien Landscape, Alien Gender: Futurist, Hopepunk Genders in Space - Lilith Acadia
2. Bodies in Flux: Transhuman Queerness in Ari North's Always Human - Anna Oleszczuk
3. Touch Utopia. Science Fictional Practices of Somatic Communication - Aramo Olaya
schedule.title: Bodily Futures

schedule.desc: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory is building two large radio telescopes in South Africa and Australia. This talk will allow you to find out about what's involved in doing this, particularly looking at the software and computing needed to deal with the huge amount of data involved. You'll also find out what it's like to work on such a huge international project and maybe find a few references to science fiction in there as well!
schedule.title: SKAO: Building the World's Largest Radio Telescope

schedule.desc: Many everyday items now contain microprocessors - we use our smartphones to tell our smart TVs to screen a particular show whilst our smart meters tally up the electricity used. Could we live without this tech, and what would be the consequences? Might we be forced to return to a less-technologically reliant society if AI becomes problematic?
schedule.title: Can We Turn the Machines Off?

people.name: Steve Willis   Fairhaven - A Novel of Climate Optimism

schedule.desc: “Strong female character” has too often been a euphemism for a sword-wielding amazon battling those who wronged her. Fun and glorious though those women are, this panel will talk about the women who lead through intelligence, charisma, patience, or other skills.
schedule.title: Strong Female Leads Who Don't Kick Ass
Surviving the Zombie Apocalypse

schedule.desc: Sword lesbians are a recognised and popular trope in fantasy and science fiction. How do we think about heroic positions and expansive gender expression in sff? How do queer people position ourselves in relationship to traditional masculinity and its phallus/sword continuum? Do we reclaim roles like knight/cavalier/Jedi, or do we find different ways for women/femmes to fight? Are sword lesbians also an expression of athleticism, when athleticism is often coded as masculine despite not really being tied to the masc/femme axis at all?
schedule.title: Sword Lesbians. Discuss.

schedule.desc:
Discuss a range of fantastic texts with tutors and doctoral students affiliated with the University of Glasgow’s unique MLitt in Fantasy Literature.  The Centre for Fantasy and the Fantastic will offer a series of 75-minute small-group seminars, including discussions of early fantastical narratives, canonical authors such as J.R.R. Tolkien and Ursula K. Le Guin, contemporary Fantasy fictions, and fantasies in diverse forms.

schedule.title: Fantasy Master’s Taster Sessions (Session 2)

schedule.desc: Costumers and cosplayers often struggle with taking their creations on the road. Our panellists will discuss tips and tricks used both for local and international travel, as well as practical concerns for wearing complicated costumes.
schedule.title: Travelling with and Wearing Complicated Costumes

schedule.desc: Can real magic and real science ever be reconciled? This talk will show how combining our most successful scientific theories to model the universe can help explain some of the most mysterious abilities of the human mind, including, perhaps, something of the nature of consciousness itself. A whirlwind tour of relativity, quantum physics, entropy and chaos theory. And some real magic.
schedule.title: Magic Is the Engineering of Coincidence

schedule.desc: With the availability of genetic technology increasing and costs decreasing, might we soon be in a position to edit our own genes? If we could, should it be allowed only for medical benefit (for example to eliminate susceptibility to a hereditary disease), or should we be able to change our appearance and characteristics at will, as depicted in science fiction?
schedule.title: Garage-Level Gene Manipulation

schedule.desc: A meetup for all lovers of board games who wish to share their experiences with modern and traditional board games, whether as players or game designers.
schedule.title: Board Game Enthusiasts Meetup

schedule.desc: Streamline the plot of your mystery by centering it on the perfect crime. Learn the ins-and-outs of method, motive and opportunity, how to create an iconic cast of suspects, and how to leave a trail of compelling clues to keep your readers guessing all the way to the surprising-yet-inevitable conclusion.
schedule.title: Mystery Writing: Plotting the Perfect Crime

schedule.desc: From zero-gravity CSI to intergalatic police detectives, join our panel as they discuss their favourite space-set mysteries. Just remember, in space, no one can hear you scream.
schedule.title: There's Been a Murder - Whodunits in Space

schedule.desc: What's the future for public transport and for those who work in public transport? How can and should it adapt to the need to reduce emissions? What changes will we see in working and living patterns, and what will the effects be? What technical advances will we see both in small and large-scale transport? How do the politics of public transport vary in different countries and between different areas, for example urban and rural communities?
schedule.title: E-bike Schemes or Superloops? The Future of Public Transportation

schedule.desc: From holding a Session Zero to adding an X Card at the table, there's a wide variety of safety tools out there. Come learn about how including safety tools in your TTRPG can be an easy and inclusive way to make everyone comfortable before, during, and after play.
schedule.title: Safety Tools for Tabletop Roleplaying Games

schedule.desc: The Scottish space sector is a hidden gem - not many people know that we build more satellites here than anywhere in the world outside of Silicon Valley. For the past twenty years we have been driving the technology that is catalysing the commercialisation of space. But how did that happen? This talk will give you a brief history of how Scotland found itself as a leader in New Space and describe the technology used and the types of data that can be generated from fleets of shoebox-sized satellites.
schedule.title: The Awesome Scottish Space Sector

schedule.desc: Organizational meeting of the WSFS Mark Protection Committee for its 2024/2025 year. Election of MPC Officers and any other business. This meeting is open to Glasgow Worldcon attendees, but only MPC members have the right to vote and introduce or debate business.
schedule.title: Mark Protection Committee Meeting 2023/2024

schedule.desc: Many recordings of early conventions and tapes are now in danger of being lost. Recently there have been a number of efforts to recover these treasures before they are no longer playable. In this panel we will discuss some of the issues that have come up
schedule.title: Rescuing Lost Music

schedule.desc: Join eight authors as they launch their new books! In this special group launch, you'll get to hear from each author as they introduce their new title before you'll have the opportunity to meet and chat with them, get books signed, etc. It'll be a geat way to discover new novels, novellas, and short fiction by a variety of science fiction, fantasy, and horror authors! Featuring Clara Ward (Be the Sea; SF), Rob Hayes (Demon: Archive of the God Eater, book 1 of the God Eater Saga; Fantasy), Sandra Bond (Three Men in Orbit; Edwardian Steampunk), Pippa Goldschmidt (short story collection Schrödinger’s Wife (and Other Possibilities); SF), Rosalie M. Lin (Daughter of Calamity; alternate 1930s Shanghai Fantasy ), Yaroslav Barsukov (Sleeping Worlds Have No Memory; SF & Fantasy), Debbie Iancu-Haddad (Tar and Bone, an Achten Tan prequel; Fantasy); and Ryann Fletcher (Exiled Advocate; Urban Fantasy).
schedule.title: Group Book Launch - Monday

schedule.desc: 2023 marked the 20th anniversary of the first volume of the Death Note manga - one of the most influential series of the 2000s. Since 2003, Death Note has spawned a critically acclaimed anime, light novel, video games, and multiple live action adaptations (the 2017 Netflix one starring Willem Dafoe!). Join us as we reminiscence about 20 years of death gods, fatal mind games, and potato chips.
schedule.title: If I'm Not Kira and You're Not Kira, Who is Writing in the Death Note?

schedule.desc:
Learn to crochet a two-dimensional dragon at this practical workshop. Your dragon can be used to embellish clothing or a costume, or it can be an art piece in its own right. This workshop is suitable for adults and teens. It is helpful if you have crocheted before, but if the dragon defeats you, you could always crochet a cat, which is easier.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
​​​​​​​
Note that the Crafting Workshops area is at the back of Hall 4 by the food trucks.
schedule.title: That Would Look Good with a Dragon

schedule.desc: From Jules Verne's Nautilus to R. J. Barker's bone ships, the sentient starships of Iain M. Bank's Culture to Ken MacLeod’s junkyard Space Submarines and Becky Chambers' Exodus fleet, science fiction and fantasy literature is full of great ways to get from A to B and maybe also C. Join our panellists as they share their favourite modes of genre transport.
schedule.title: All Aboard: Fantastical Voyages Through Space and Time

schedule.desc:
Join Phoebe Wagner in her workshop on how to write solarpunk. We will discuss definitions, existing literature, and focus on brainstorming different solarpunk stories before sharing the results.

​​​​​​​Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.
schedule.title: How to Write Solarpunk

schedule.desc: The Edinburgh Fringe is happening right now, as well as a series of other festivals. It can be rather daunting. The panel discuss their hard won experiences of the Edinburgh Fringe and share some top tips for you to get the best out of it.
schedule.title: Edinburgh Fringe Survival Guide

schedule.desc: Writers often are drawn to imagining a far future, usually in space, often of humankind rather than a specific place or people. This panel explores Scotland as a specific setting for stories and how tthe nation's ambitions and characteristics are played out in a far, and not so far, future.
schedule.title: Writing Future Scotland

schedule.desc:
1. "Lesbians at the End of the World" in Naomi Alderman's The Future and Gabrielle Korn's Yours for the Taking - Lois Wilson-McFarland
2. "It probably would have meant peace forever": Sexual Politics in a Post-Apocalyptic World - Grace Borland Sinclair
3. 'Writing Back' to Heteropatriarchal Power in Nicola Griffith's Spear - Helen Young
schedule.title: Futures of Sexuality

schedule.desc: Join us for today’s Glasgow 2024 feedback session. This is the best way to connect with the convention organisers and ask any questions you have about the con. Your participation will help us to address current issues and capture new opportunities that we may otherwise miss. Your feedback matters and will be heard by future Worldcon organizers as well!
schedule.title: Feedback Session - Monday

schedule.desc: Many classic fantasy works for children and YA end with the protagonists finding their way home, or at least back to reality, after their adventures in another world. But in others, they get to stay in their new lives, sometimes even joined by their original family, or else they take part of their adventures back home. We explore whether home really is best and what going home really means.
schedule.title: Home Sweet Home?

schedule.desc: It has been said that once you’ve solved all the other problems with generation starships, dealing with the economic problems involved would be trivial. Is that right, or would the economic problems be important as well? In this talk we will explore what the economics of a generation starship might look like in practice, in comparison with how this is handled in science fiction.
schedule.title: Economics of Generation Starships

schedule.desc: Come together with fellow enthusiasts of the Space Kingdom of Dundee to celebrate its rich lore, unique characters, and thrilling adventures. Join us for engaging discussions, share fan theories, and revel in the imaginative world-building of this beloved universe created by band Gloryhammer!
schedule.title: Subjects of the Space Kingdom of Dundee meetup

schedule.desc: A meetup for Southeast Asian authors to connect, share insights, and discuss their craft, exploring the rich cultural tapestry and storytelling traditions of the region through their own works.
schedule.title: Southeast Asian Authors meetup

schedule.desc: Textiles are an integral part of human (and non-human!) spaces - from nomadic tent villages to the Colosseum, and from chair upholstery to ship sails. Our panellists discuss how textiles weave their way into human spaces and how breakthroughs in textiles and materials can impact the very spaces we live and work in. They'll also discuss the agricultural, mechanical and industrial processes behind these fabrics and how they shape the settlements, societies and worlds - both real and imagined - which we inhabit.
schedule.title: The Impact of Textiles on the Built Environment

schedule.desc: Science fiction (and other genres) are increasingly recognising the importance of translators with translated work awards, but too often the translator still receives litte credit. This year we have Hugo nominees that are presented in two languages . This panel looks at the incredible skill it takes to be a good translator, the challenges of different genres (poetry, fiction, comics, picture books, non fiction), and what the 'art and craft' means to each of the panellists.
schedule.title: The Art and Craft of Literary Translation

schedule.desc: Writing a play is only part of the process. How do you make sure that your text, your actors, and your vision align?
schedule.title: Directing Actors Who Are Performing Your Writing

schedule.desc: Another game show from the Dutch reality television hit factory, The Traitors is now an internationally renowned evolution from the highly popular Werewolf card game with shows in multiple countries. We discuss what is so gripping about the show, why we keep coming back, the excellent and contrasting presenters and standout moments in the various series.
schedule.title: The Traitors - Reality Television for Gamers

schedule.desc: Peace reigns over the beautiful Cardboard City. But wait! What's this? A horde of raveging monsters come to destroy it? What are the odds??? Recommended for ages 0-15.
schedule.title: Godzilla Stomp

schedule.desc: A light-hearted balloon-style debate in which master debaters try to convince the audience which extinct, fictional or mythical creature should be brought (back) to life - assuming a suitable sample of DNA were available from which to create it - and why their choice is better than anyone else's. Come along, and vote to keep your favourite from being eliminated.
schedule.title: Jurassic Park: Extinction Rebellion

schedule.desc: Imagine if you could build your own museum and share access to it, even make revenue from it, using our most precious cultural artefacts from across the globe. The University of Glasgow, along with partners Edify, Historic Environment Scotland and National Museums Scotland, are bringing together XR technology - Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality - and museum collections to allow just that. In this talk Principal Investigator Neil McDonnell will introduce the Museums in the Metaverse project and how it addresses the great economic potential for XR technology in the Cultural Heritage sector.
schedule.title: Museums in the Metaverse

schedule.desc: From K9 to Hedwig,  Pikachu to Purza, or from Spot to Sunny, which fictional pets have the affection of this panel and why? Here, we speak of alternative adventurers, sidekicks and faithful friends who have become a memorable part of the story.
schedule.title: Who's a Pretty Boy? Pets in SFF

schedule.desc: From Jasper Fforde's Thursday Next to Diana Wynne Jones' Tough Guide to Fantasyland, fantasy has a long tradition of satirising the (so-called) real world and its own genre. Together, we will send up and take apart fantasy's satirical strands and wonder why it is so good a tool for playing with reality and itself.
schedule.title: Satirical Fantasy

schedule.desc: Come join pianist and singer, Mary Crowell as she regales you with songs of Radium Girls, Devils, and Dice.
schedule.title: Filk Concert: Dr Mary Crowell

schedule.desc: A meetup and networking opportunity for writers of colour only.
schedule.title: Writers of Colour Meetup

schedule.desc: Was the resulting expansion of the Star Wars Universe only possible because of The Phantom Menace? This panel will discuss the first Star Wars film of the 90s and the knock-on effects it had on SFF culture in the 25 years since its release. From Jar Jar to Andor, our panellists cover it all!
schedule.title: 25th Anniversary of Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace

schedule.desc: From Tolkien's Quenya to the sign language used in L. R. Lam's Dragonfall, languages help showcase the cultures that use them. From assumptions in the words to the metaphors we use, this panel will discuss the ways that languages expand and deepen the worlds we read and the ways both real and constructed languages impact our reading.
schedule.title: Languages as World-Building

schedule.desc: A gathering for Star Trek enthusiasts to celebrate their love for the iconic science fiction franchise, discussing favorite episodes, characters, and sharing memorabilia. Live long and prosper!
schedule.title: Star Trek Fans Meetup

schedule.desc:
Learn to do ropes, 4-strand "round" braids, classic (3-strand) French and Dutch (or inverted-French or underhand) braids, as well as a crown braid (technically a horizontal modified (3-strand) French braid) and other advanced ideas like 5 and 7-strand fingering techniques. you can also learn shapes like hearts, spirals and a pull-up-weave. All will be tailored to the desires and abilities of the audience. BYO-brush, or use one provided.

Information about sign ups for this workshop will be available at glasgow2024.org/whats-on/programme/workshops.

Note that the Crafting Workshops area is at the back of Hall 4 by the food trucks.
schedule.title: Renaissance & Fancy Hair Braids Workshop #2

schedule.desc:
This is the British Sign Language 'room' for the Closing Ceremony. The signer will be on stage and on camera. 

All good things must come to an end and sadly Glasgow 2024 must finish, although Worldcon goes on. That ending will come on Monday afternoon at the Closing Ceremony hosted by Chair, Professor Esther MacCallum-Stewart, when we say goodbye to our Guests, say many thank-yous for all the contributions made, and share highlights of the convention and any final outcomes of votes held.

The official handing over to the committee of the 83rd World Science Fiction Convention will then take place, and there will be a presentation of what we can expect to see from Seattle, Washington in 2025.

We'll close out the convention in style with the help of The Jiggers Ceilidh band!

Come along and have fun, then enjoy the Dead Dog party which starts immediately afterwards.
schedule.title: Ceilidh with The Jiggers

schedule.desc: It's all over! Come and chill, swap anecdotes, and say your goodbyes!
schedule.title: Dead Dog Party
